(x^2 - y^2)^2 + 4x^2 y^2 = 256 + 900 = 1156, so x^2 + y^2 = 34 or x^2 + y^2

= -34.
For x^2 + y^2 = 34: x^2 = 25 and y^2 = 9, giving (5, 3) and (-5, -3) (xy =

15 > 0 forces equal signs).
For x^2 + y^2 = -34: x^2 = -9 and y^2 = -25, giving

(3i, -5i) and (-3i, 5i) (again xy = 15 forces the signs shown).
Solution set = {(5, 3),

(-5, -3), (3i, -5i), (-3i, 5i)}. 8.
From the first equation, y = (9 - x^2)/x (x != 0).

Substituting in the second: x^2 - (9 - x^2)^2/x^2 = 2, i.e. x^4 - 2x^2 - (81 -

18x^2 + x^4) = 0, i.e.
16x^2 = 81, so x = +- 9/4 and y = +- 7/4 (same sign as x).

Solution set = {(9/4, 7/4), (-9/4, -7/4)}. 9.
From the second equation, y = (2x^2 +

3)/x (x != 0).
Substituting in the first: ((2x^2 + 3)/x)^2 - 7 = 2(2x^2 + 3), i.e. 4x^2

+ 12 + 9/x^2 - 7 = 4x^2 + 6, i.e.
9/x^2 = 1, so x = +- 3.
Then y = 7 for x = 3 and

y = -7 for x = -3.
Solution set = {(3, 7), (-3, -7)}. 10.
(x + y)^2 = x^2 + y^2 + 2xy

= 9, so x + y = +- 3; (x - y)^2 = x^2 + y^2 - 2xy = 1, so x - y = +- 1. Combining:

(x, y) = (2, 1), (1, 2), (-2, -1) or (-1, -2).
Solution set = {(2, 1), (1, 2), (-2, -1), (-1,

-2)}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x^2 = 6 + 3y^2 and 3x^2 - 5y^2 = 7. What are the values of x and y?
options: x = +-sqrt(6), y = +-2 with linked signs only
mcqs.why: From the first equation x^2 = (6 + 3y^2)/2. Substituting: 3(6 + 3y^2)/2 - 5y^2 = 7 gives 18 + 9y^2 - 10y^2 = 14, so y^2 = 4 and y = +-2. Then 2x^2 = 6 + 3(4) = 18, so x^2 = 9 and x = +-3; only squares occur, so all four sign combinations work.

mcqs.q: Solve: 8x^2 = y^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 = 19. What is x^2?
For 8x^2 = y^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 = 19, what is the correct value of y? (The printed key has an error here.)
mcqs.why: y^2 = 8x^2 = 8(19/17) = 152/17, so y = +-sqrt(152/17) = +-2 sqrt(38/17). The printed key's 2 sqrt(38/7) is wrong: 152/7 would not satisfy x^2 + 2y^2 = 19, so the corrected denominator 17 is used.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x^2 - 8 = 5y^2 and x^2 - 13 = -2y^2. What is the solution set?
How does x^2 - 5xy + 6y^2 = 0 factorise in the system with x^2 + y^2 = 45?
mcqs.why: x^2 - 5xy + 6y^2 = (x - 2y)(x - 3y), since 2 + 3 = 5 and 2 x 3 = 6. So x = 2y or x = 3y, the two cases used with x^2 + y^2 = 45.

mcqs.q: In x^2 - 5xy + 6y^2 = 0 with x^2 + y^2 = 45, the case x = 2y gives which solutions?
In 12x^2 - 25xy + 12y^2 = 0 with 4x^2 + 7y^2 = 148, the case y = 4x/3 gives which solutions?
Solve: 12x^2 - 11xy + 2y^2 = 0 and 2x^2 + 7xy = 60. Which solutions come from the branch y = 4x? (The printed key omits this branch.)
mcqs.why: (3x - 2y)(4x - y) = 0 gives y = 3x/2 or y = 4x. For y = 4x: 2x^2 + 7x(4x) = 30x^2 = 60, so x^2 = 2, x = +-sqrt(2), y = +-4 sqrt(2). This branch satisfies both equations but the printed key lists only the other branch, so it is included here.

mcqs.q: Solve: x^2 - y^2 = 16 and xy = 15. What are the real solutions?
Solve: x^2 + y^2 = 5 and xy = 2. What is the solution set?

lessons.title: Exercise 4.10
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-5

1. The product of one less than a certain positive number and two less than three

times the number is 14. Find the number. 2. The sum of a positive number and its

square is 380. Find the number. 3. Divide 40 into two parts such that the sum of

their squares is greater than 2 times their product by 100. 4. The sum of a positive

number and its reciprocal is 26/5. Find the number. 5. A number exceeds its square

root by 56. Find the number.

1.
Let the number be x: (x - 1)(3x - 2) = 14, i.e.
3x^2 - 5x - 12 = (3x + 4)(x - 3) = 0.

Since x is positive, x = 3. 2.
Let the number be x: x + x^2 = 380, i.e. x^2 + x - 380

= (x + 20)(x - 19) = 0.
Since x is positive, x = 19. 3.
Let the parts be x and 40 - x:

x^2 + (40 - x)^2 = 2x(40 - x) + 100, i.e.
4x^2 - 160x + 1500 = 0, i.e. x^2 - 40x +

375 = (x - 15)(x - 25) = 0.
So the parts are 15 and 25. 4.
Let the number be x: x +

1/x = 26/5, i.e.
5x^2 - 26x + 5 = (5x - 1)(x - 5) = 0, so x = 5 or x = 1/5 (the two

values are reciprocals of each other; both satisfy the condition). 5. Let the number

be x: x - sqrt(x) = 56.
Put t = sqrt(x): t^2 - t - 56 = (t - 8)(t + 7) = 0. Since t >= 0, t

= 8 and x = 64.

Q6-10

6. Find two consecutive numbers, whose product is 132. (Hint: Suppose the

numbers are x and x + 1). 7. The difference between the cubes of two consecutive

even numbers is 296. Find them. (Hint: Let two consecutive even numbers be x and

x + 2). 8. A farmer bought some sheep for Rs. 9000. If he had paid Rs. 100 less for

each, he would have got 3 sheep more for the same money. How many sheep did

he buy, when the rate in each case is uniform? 9. A man sold his stock of eggs for

Rs. 240. If he had 2 dozen more, he would have got the same money by selling the

whole for Rs. 0.50 per dozen cheaper. How many dozen eggs did he sell? 10. A

cyclist travelled 48 km at a uniform speed. Had he travelled 2 km/hour slower, he

would have taken 2 hours more to perform the journey. How long did he take to

cover 48 km?

6. x(x + 1) = 132, i.e. x^2 + x - 132 = (x + 12)(x - 11) = 0.
Taking the positive

value, x = 11, so the numbers are 11 and 12. 7.
(x + 2)^3 - x^3 = 296, i.e. 6x^2 +

12x + 8 = 296, i.e. x^2 + 2x - 48 = (x + 8)(x - 6) = 0.
Taking the positive even

value, x = 6, so the numbers are 6 and 8. 8.
Let n be the number of sheep: the price

per sheep is 9000/n.
Then (n + 3)(9000/n - 100) = 9000, i.e.
27000/n - 100n - 300 =

0, i.e. n^2 + 3n - 270 = (n + 18)(n - 15) = 0.
So n = 15 sheep. 9. Let d be the

number of dozen eggs: the price per dozen is 240/d.
Then (d + 2)(240/d - 0.50) =

240, i.e.
480/d - 0.5d - 1 = 0, i.e. d^2 + 2d - 960 = (d + 32)(d - 30) = 0. So d = 30

dozen. 10.
Let the speed be v km/hour: the time taken is 48/v hours. Then 48/(v - 2)

= 48/v + 2, i.e.
24/(v - 2) - 24/v = 1, i.e.
48 = v(v - 2), i.e. v^2 - 2v - 48 = (v - 8)(v +

6) = 0.
Taking v = 8 km/hour, the time taken is 48/8 = 6 hours.

Q11-15

11. The area of a rectangular field is 297 square meters. Had it been 3 meters

longer and one meter shorter, the area would have been 3 square meters more.

Find its length and breadth. 12. The length of a rectangular piece of paper exceeds

its breadth by 5 cm. If a strip 0.5 cm wide be cut all around the piece of paper, the

area of the remaining part would be 500 square cms. Find its original dimensions.

13. A number consists of two digits whose product is 18. If the digits are

interchanged, the new number becomes 27 less than the original number. Find the

number. 14. A number consists of two digits whose product is 14. If the digits are

interchanged, the resulting number will exceed the original number by 45. Find the

number. 15. The area of a right triangle is 210 square meters. If its hypotenuse is 37

meters long, find the length of the base and the altitude.

11.
Let the length be l and the breadth be b: lb = 297 and (l + 3)(b - 1) = 300.

Expanding the second: lb - l + 3b - 3 = 300, i.e. -l + 3b = 6, so l = 3b - 6.

Substituting: (3b - 6)b = 297, i.e. b^2 - 2b - 99 = (b - 11)(b + 9) = 0. So b = 11 m

and l = 27 m. 12.
Let the breadth be b cm: the length is b + 5 cm. After cutting a

0.5 cm strip all around, the remaining piece is (b + 4) cm by (b - 1) cm, so (b + 4)(b

- 1) = 500, i.e. b^2 + 3b - 504 = (b + 24)(b - 21) = 0.
So the breadth is 21 cm and

the length is 26 cm. 13.
Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y: xy = 18 and

(10y + x) = (10x + y) - 27, i.e. x - y = 3.
So x = y + 3 and (y + 3)y = 18, i.e. y^2 +

3y - 18 = (y + 6)(y - 3) = 0.
So y = 3 and x = 6, giving the number 63. 14. Let the

tens digit be x and the units digit be y: xy = 14 and (10y + x) = (10x + y) + 45, i.e.

y - x = 5.
So y = x + 5 and x(x + 5) = 14, i.e. x^2 + 5x - 14 = (x + 7)(x - 2) = 0. So

x = 2 and y = 7, giving the number 27. 15.
Let the base be a and the altitude be b:

(1/2)ab = 210, so ab = 420; and a^2 + b^2 = 37^2 = 1369. Then (a + b)^2 =

1369 + 840 = 2209, so a + b = 47.
Hence a and b are the roots of t^2 - 47t + 420

= (t - 35)(t - 12) = 0, so the base is 35 m and the altitude is 12 m (or vice versa).

Q16-20

16. The area of a rectangle is 1680 square meters. If its diagonal is 58 meters long,

find the length and the breadth of the rectangle. 17. To do a piece of work, A takes

10 days more than B. Together they finish the work in 12 days. How long would B

take to finish it alone? (Hint: If some one takes x days to finish a work, the one day's

work will be 1/x). 18. To complete a job, A and B take 4 days working together. A

alone takes twice as long as B alone to finish the same job. How long would each

one alone take to do the job? 19. An open box is to be made from a square piece of

tin by cutting a piece 2 dm square from each corner and then folding the sides of

the remaining piece. If the capacity of the box is to be 128 c.dm, find the length of

the side of the piece. 20. A man invests Rs. 100,000 in two companies. His total

profit is Rs. 3080. If he receives Rs. 1980 from one company and at the rate 1%

more from the other, find the amount of each investment.

16.
Let the length be l and the breadth be b: lb = 1680 and l^2 + b^2 = 58^2 =

3364.
Then (l + b)^2 = 3364 + 3360 = 6724, so l + b = 82.
Hence l and b are the

roots of t^2 - 82t + 1680 = (t - 42)(t - 40) = 0, so the length is 42 m and the

breadth is 40 m. 17.
Let B take x days: A takes x + 10 days.
Together: 1/x + 1/(x +

10) = 1/12, i.e.
12(2x + 10) = x(x + 10), i.e. x^2 - 14x - 120 = (x - 20)(x + 6) = 0.

So B alone takes 20 days. 18.
Let B take x days: A takes 2x days. Together: 1/x +

1/(2x) = 1/4, i.e.
3/(2x) = 1/4, so x = 6.
Hence B alone takes 6 days and A alone

takes 12 days. 19.
Let the side of the square piece be s dm: after cutting 2 dm

squares from the corners and folding, the box is (s - 4) dm by (s - 4) dm by 2 dm, so

its capacity is 2(s - 4)^2 = 128, i.e.
(s - 4)^2 = 64, so s - 4 = 8 (taking the positive

value) and s = 12 dm. 20.
Let the two investments be Rs. x and Rs. (100000 - x), at

rates r% and (r + 1)% respectively, with profits Rs. 1980 and Rs. 3080: x r/100 =

1980 and (100000 - x)(r + 1)/100 = 3080.
From the first, r = 198000/x. Substituting:

(100000 - x)(198000 + x)/(100x) = 3080, i.e.
(100000 - x)(198000 + x) = 308000x,

i.e. x^2 + 406000x - 19800000000 = 0, i.e.
(x - 44000)(x + 450000) = 0. So x =

44000, and the investments are Rs.
44,000 (at 4.5%, giving profit Rs. 1980) and Rs.

56,000 (at 5.5%, giving profit Rs.
3080), as in the printed key.
FLAG: the question as

printed says 'total profit is Rs.
3080', but under that literal reading (profits 1980 and

1100) the investments would be about Rs. 70,974 and Rs.
29,026 (or about Rs.

56,297 and Rs.
43,703 if the 1980 profit is at the higher rate), not the key's Rs.

56,000 and Rs. 44,000.
The solution above follows the reading that reproduces the

printed key exactly: the two profits are Rs. 1980 and Rs. 3080.

mcqs.q: The product of one less than a positive number and two less than three times the number is 14. Find the number.
mcqs.why: (x - 1)(3x - 2) = 14 gives 3x^2 - 5x - 12 = (3x + 4)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 3 or x = -4/3. The number is positive, so x = 3.

mcqs.q: The sum of a positive number and its square is 380. Find the number.
mcqs.why: x + x^2 = 380 gives x^2 + x - 380 = (x + 20)(x - 19) = 0, so x = 19 or x = -20. The number is positive, so x = 19. Check: 19 + 361 = 380.

mcqs.q: Divide 40 into two parts such that the sum of their squares exceeds twice their product by 100. What are the parts?
The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is 26/5. Find the number(s).
mcqs.why: x + 1/x = 26/5 gives 5x^2 - 26x + 5 = (5x - 1)(x - 5) = 0, so x = 5 or x = 1/5. The two values are reciprocals of each other and both satisfy the condition.

mcqs.q: A number exceeds its square root by 56. Find the number.
mcqs.why: x - sqrt(x) = 56. Put t = sqrt(x): t^2 - t - 56 = (t - 8)(t + 7) = 0. Since t >= 0, t = 8, so x = t^2 = 64.

mcqs.q: Find two consecutive numbers whose product is 132.
mcqs.why: x(x + 1) = 132 gives x^2 + x - 132 = (x + 12)(x - 11) = 0. Taking the positive value x = 11, the numbers are 11 and 12. Check: 11 x 12 = 132.

mcqs.q: The difference between the cubes of two consecutive even numbers is 296. Find them.
mcqs.why: (x + 2)^3 - x^3 = 296 gives 6x^2 + 12x + 8 = 296, i.e. x^2 + 2x - 48 = (x + 8)(x - 6) = 0. Taking the positive even value x = 6, the numbers are 6 and 8.

mcqs.q: A farmer bought some sheep for Rs. 9000. If he had paid Rs. 100 less for each, he would have got 3 sheep more for the same money. How many sheep did he buy?
A man sold his stock of eggs for Rs. 240. If he had 2 dozen more, he would have got the same money by selling the whole for Rs. 0.50 per dozen cheaper. How many dozen eggs did he sell?
A cyclist travelled 48 km at a uniform speed. Had he travelled 2 km/hour slower, he would have taken 2 hours more. How long did he take to cover 48 km?

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Resolve 1/(x^2 - 1) into partial fractions

Step 1: x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1).
Write 1/((x - 1)(x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 1). Step

2: Identity: 1 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 1).
Step 3: Put x = 1: 1 = 2A, so A = 1/2. Put x = -1:

1 = -2B, so B = -1/2.
Answer: 1/(2(x - 1)) - 1/(2(x + 1)).
This agrees with the book's

Answers (p. 416).

Q2

2. Resolve (x^2 + 1)/((x + 1)(x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: The fraction is improper (numerator and denominator both degree 2).

Divide: (x^2 + 1)/(x^2 - 1) = 1 + 2/(x^2 - 1).
Step 2: Resolve 2/((x - 1)(x + 1)) =

A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 1): identity 2 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 1); x = 1 gives A = 1; x = -1 gives

B = -1.
Answer: 1 + 1/(x - 1) - 1/(x + 1).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p.

416).

Q3

3. Resolve (2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x + 3). Step

2: Identity: 2x + 1 = A(x + 2)(x + 3) + B(x - 1)(x + 3) + C(x - 1)(x + 2). Step 3: Put x

= 1: 3 = A(3)(4) = 12A, so A = 1/4.
Put x = -2: -3 = B(-3)(1) = -3B, so B = 1. Put x =

-3: -5 = C(-4)(-1) = 4C, so C = -5/4.
Answer: 1/(4(x - 1)) + 1/(x + 2) - 5/(4(x + 3)).

This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 416).

Q4

4. Resolve (3x^2 - 4x - 5)/((x - 2)(x^2 + 7x + 10)) into partial fractions

Step 1: x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x + 2)(x + 5), so the fraction is (3x^2 - 4x - 5)/((x - 2)(x +

2)(x + 5)) = A/(x - 2) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x + 5).
Step 2: Identity: 3x^2 - 4x - 5 = A(x +

2)(x + 5) + B(x - 2)(x + 5) + C(x - 2)(x + 2).
Step 3: Put x = 2: 12 - 8 - 5 = -1 =

A(4)(7) = 28A, so A = -1/28.
Put x = -2: 12 + 8 - 5 = 15 = B(-4)(3) = -12B, so B =

-5/4.
Put x = -5: 75 + 20 - 5 = 90 = C(-7)(-3) = 21C, so C = 30/7.
Answer: -1/(28(x -

2)) - 5/(4(x + 2)) + 30/(7(x + 5)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 416).

Q5

5. Resolve 1/((x - 1)(2x - 1)(3x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((x - 1)(2x - 1)(3x - 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(2x - 1) + C/(3x - 1). Step 2:

Identity: 1 = A(2x - 1)(3x - 1) + B(x - 1)(3x - 1) + C(x - 1)(2x - 1).
Step 3: Put x = 1:

1 = A(1)(2) = 2A, so A = 1/2.
Put x = 1/2: 1 = B(-1/2)(1/2) = -B/4, so B = -4. Put x =

1/3: 1 = C(-2/3)(-1/3) = 2C/9, so C = 9/2.
Answer: 1/(2(x - 1)) - 4/(2x - 1) + 9/(2(3x -

1)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 416).

Q6

6. Resolve x/((x - a)(x - b)(x - c)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write x/((x - a)(x - b)(x - c)) = A/(x - a) + B/(x - b) + C/(x - c). Step 2: Identity:

x = A(x - b)(x - c) + B(x - a)(x - c) + C(x - a)(x - b).
Step 3: Put x = a: a = A(a - b)(a -

c), so A = a/((a - b)(a - c)).
Put x = b: b = B(b - a)(b - c), so B = b/((b - a)(b - c)). Put

x = c: c = C(c - a)(c - b), so C = c/((c - a)(c - b)).
Answer: a/((a - b)(a - c)(x - a)) +

b/((b - a)(b - c)(x - b)) + c/((c - a)(c - b)(x - c)).
This agrees with the book's Answers

(p. 416).

Q7

7. Resolve (6x^3 + 5x^2 - 7)/(2x^2 - x - 1) into partial fractions

Step 1: The fraction is improper.
Divide: (3x + 4)(2x^2 - x - 1) = 6x^3 + 5x^2 - 7x -

4, so (6x^3 + 5x^2 - 7) = (3x + 4)(2x^2 - x - 1) + (7x - 3).
Step 2: Resolve (7x -

3)/((2x + 1)(x - 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(2x + 1): identity 7x - 3 = A(2x + 1) + B(x - 1); x

= 1 gives 4 = 3A, so A = 4/3; x = -1/2 gives -13/2 = B(-3/2), so B = 13/3. Step 3:

Answer: 3x + 4 + 4/(3(x - 1)) + 13/(3(2x + 1)).
This agrees with the book's Answers

(p. 416).

Q8

8. Resolve (2x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3)/(2x^3 + x^2 - 3x) into partial fractions

Step 1: The denominator factors as x(2x + 3)(x - 1).
The numerator minus the

denominator is -2x + 3, so the fraction equals 1 + (-2x + 3)/(x(2x + 3)(x - 1)). Step

2: Resolve (-2x + 3)/(x(2x + 3)(x - 1)) = A/x + B/(2x + 3) + C/(x - 1): identity -2x + 3

= A(2x + 3)(x - 1) + Bx(x - 1) + Cx(2x + 3).
Put x = 0: 3 = A(3)(-1) = -3A, so A = -1.

Put x = 1: 1 = C(1)(5) = 5C, so C = 1/5.
Put x = -3/2: 6 = B(-3/2)(-5/2) = 15B/4, so B

= 8/5.
Step 3: Answer: 1 - 1/x + 8/(5(2x + 3)) + 1/(5(x - 1)).
This agrees with the

book's Answers (p. 416).

Q9

9. Resolve (x - 1)(x - 3)(x - 5)/((x - 2)(x - 4)(x - 6)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Both numerator and denominator are monic cubics, so the fraction equals 1

plus a proper fraction.
Numerator minus denominator: (x^3 - 9x^2 + 23x - 15) -

(x^3 - 12x^2 + 44x - 48) = 3x^2 - 21x + 33 = 3(x^2 - 7x + 11). Step 2: Resolve

3(x^2 - 7x + 11)/((x - 2)(x - 4)(x - 6)) = A/(x - 2) + B/(x - 4) + C/(x - 6). Put x = 2:

3(4 - 14 + 11) = 3 = A(-2)(-4) = 8A, so A = 3/8.
Put x = 4: 3(16 - 28 + 11) = -3 =

B(2)(-2) = -4B, so B = 3/4.
Put x = 6: 3(36 - 42 + 11) = 15 = C(4)(2) = 8C, so C =

15/8.
Answer: 1 + 3/(8(x - 2)) + 3/(4(x - 4)) + 15/(8(x - 6)).
This agrees with the

book's Answers (p. 416).

Q10

10. Resolve 1/((1 - ax)(1 - bx)(1 - cx)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((1 - ax)(1 - bx)(1 - cx)) = A/(1 - ax) + B/(1 - bx) + C/(1 - cx). Step 2:

Identity: 1 = A(1 - bx)(1 - cx) + B(1 - ax)(1 - cx) + C(1 - ax)(1 - bx). Step 3: Put x =

1/a: 1 = A(1 - b/a)(1 - c/a) = A(a - b)(a - c)/a^2, so A = a^2/((a - b)(a - c)). Similarly

B = b^2/((b - a)(b - c)) and C = c^2/((c - a)(c - b)).
Answer: a^2/((a - b)(a - c)(1 -

ax)) + b^2/((b - a)(b - c)(1 - bx)) + c^2/((c - a)(c - b)(1 - cx)).
This agrees with the

book's Answers (p. 416).

Q11

11. Resolve (x^2 + a^2)/((x^2 + b^2)(x^2 + c^2)(x^2 + d^2)) into partial

fractions. [Hint: Put x^2 = y to make factors of the denominator linear]

Step 1: Put y = x^2.
Then the fraction is (y + a^2)/((y + b^2)(y + c^2)(y + d^2))

= A/(y + b^2) + B/(y + c^2) + C/(y + d^2).
Step 2: Identity: y + a^2 = A(y +

c^2)(y + d^2) + B(y + b^2)(y + d^2) + C(y + b^2)(y + c^2). Step 3: Put y =

-b^2: a^2 - b^2 = A(c^2 - b^2)(d^2 - b^2), so A = (a^2 - b^2)/((c^2 - b^2)(d^2 -

b^2)).
Similarly B = (a^2 - c^2)/((b^2 - c^2)(d^2 - c^2)) and C = (a^2 -

d^2)/((b^2 - d^2)(c^2 - d^2)).
Step 4: Replacing y by x^2 gives the answer: (a^2 -

b^2)/((c^2 - b^2)(d^2 - b^2)(x^2 + b^2)) + (a^2 - c^2)/((b^2 - c^2)(d^2 -

c^2)(x^2 + c^2)) + (a^2 - d^2)/((b^2 - d^2)(c^2 - d^2)(x^2 + d^2)). This agrees

with the book's Answers (p. 416) (the key writes each denominator with the factors

in the opposite order, which is the same value since two sign changes cancel).

mcqs.q: In resolving 1/(x^2 - 1) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 1), what is A?
In resolving 1/(x^2 - 1) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 1), what is B?
Resolve (x^2 + 1)/((x + 1)(x - 1)) into partial fractions.
mcqs.why: The fraction is improper: (x^2 + 1)/(x^2 - 1) = 1 + 2/(x^2 - 1). For 2/((x - 1)(x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 1): x = 1 gives A = 1 and x = -1 gives B = -1, so the answer is 1 + 1/(x - 1) - 1/(x + 1).

mcqs.q: In resolving (2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x + 3), what is A?
In resolving (2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x + 3), what is B?
In resolving (2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x + 3), what is C?
In resolving 1/((x - 1)(2x - 1)(3x - 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(2x - 1) + C/(3x - 1), what is B?
In resolving (6x^3 + 5x^2 - 7)/(2x^2 - x - 1), after dividing out the quotient 3x + 4, the remainder (7x - 3)/((2x + 1)(x - 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(2x + 1) has A equal to what?
mcqs.why: (3x + 4)(2x^2 - x - 1) = 6x^3 + 5x^2 - 7x - 4, so the remainder is 7x - 3. Identity: 7x - 3 = A(2x + 1) + B(x - 1). Put x = 1: 4 = 3A, so A = 4/3 (and B = 13/3).

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Resolve (2x^2 - 3x + 4)/(x - 1)^3 into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (2x^2 - 3x + 4)/(x - 1)^3 = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x - 1)^3. Step

2: Identity: 2x^2 - 3x + 4 = A(x - 1)^2 + B(x - 1) + C. Step 3: Put x = 1: 2 - 3 + 4 =

3 = C. Equating x^2 coefficients: A = 2.
Equating x coefficients: -2A + B = -3, so B

= 1.
Answer: 2/(x - 1) + 1/(x - 1)^2 + 3/(x - 1)^3.
This agrees with the book's

Answers (p. 416).

Q2

2. Resolve (5x^2 - 2x + 3)/(x + 2)^3 into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (5x^2 - 2x + 3)/(x + 2)^3 = A/(x + 2) + B/(x + 2)^2 + C/(x + 2)^3.

Step 2: Identity: 5x^2 - 2x + 3 = A(x + 2)^2 + B(x + 2) + C. Step 3: Put x = -2: 20

+ 4 + 3 = 27 = C. Equating x^2 coefficients: A = 5.
Equating x coefficients: 4A + B

= -2, so B = -22.
Answer: 5/(x + 2) - 22/(x + 2)^2 + 27/(x + 2)^3. This agrees with

the book's Answers (p. 416).

Q3

3. Resolve 4x/((x + 1)^2 (x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 4x/((x + 1)^2 (x - 1)) = A/(x + 1) + B/(x + 1)^2 + C/(x - 1). Step 2:

Identity: 4x = A(x + 1)(x - 1) + B(x - 1) + C(x + 1)^2.
Step 3: Put x = -1: -4 = B(-2),

so B = 2.
Put x = 1: 4 = C(4), so C = 1.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A =

-1.
Answer: -1/(x + 1) + 2/(x + 1)^2 + 1/(x - 1).
This agrees with the book's Answers

(p. 416).

Q4

4. Resolve 9/((x + 2)^2 (x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 9/((x + 2)^2 (x - 1)) = A/(x + 2) + B/(x + 2)^2 + C/(x - 1). Step 2:

Identity: 9 = A(x + 2)(x - 1) + B(x - 1) + C(x + 2)^2.
Step 3: Put x = -2: 9 = B(-3), so

B = -3.
Put x = 1: 9 = C(9), so C = 1.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A =

-1.
Answer: -1/(x + 2) - 3/(x + 2)^2 + 1/(x - 1).
This agrees with the book's Answers

(p. 416).

Q5

5. Resolve 1/((x - 3)^2 (x + 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((x - 3)^2 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 3) + B/(x - 3)^2 + C/(x + 1). Step 2:

Identity: 1 = A(x - 3)(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + C(x - 3)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 3: 1 = B(4), so

B = 1/4.
Put x = -1: 1 = C(16), so C = 1/16.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so

A = -1/16.
Answer: -1/(16(x - 3)) + 1/(4(x - 3)^2) + 1/(16(x + 1)). This agrees with

the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q6

6. Resolve x^2/((x - 2)(x - 1)^2) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write x^2/((x - 2)(x - 1)^2) = A/(x - 2) + B/(x - 1) + C/(x - 1)^2. Step 2:

Identity: x^2 = A(x - 1)^2 + B(x - 2)(x - 1) + C(x - 2).
Step 3: Put x = 2: 4 = A(1), so

A = 4.
Put x = 1: 1 = C(-1), so C = -1.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A + B, so B =

-3.
Answer: 4/(x - 2) - 3/(x - 1) - 1/(x - 1)^2.
This agrees with the book's Answers (p.

417).

Q7

7. Resolve 1/((x - 1)^2 (x + 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((x - 1)^2 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x + 1). Step 2:

Identity: 1 = A(x - 1)(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + C(x - 1)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 1: 1 = B(2), so

B = 1/2.
Put x = -1: 1 = C(4), so C = 1/4.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A

= -1/4.
Answer: -1/(4(x - 1)) + 1/(2(x - 1)^2) + 1/(4(x + 1)).
This agrees with the

book's Answers (p. 417).

Q8

8. Resolve x^2/((x - 1)^3 (x + 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write x^2/((x - 1)^3 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x - 1)^3 + D/(x +

1).
Step 2: Identity: x^2 = A(x - 1)^2 (x + 1) + B(x - 1)(x + 1) + C(x + 1) + D(x -

1)^3.
Step 3: Put x = 1: 1 = C(2), so C = 1/2.
Put x = -1: 1 = D(-8), so D = -1/8.

Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A + D, so A = 1/8.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A

+ B - 3D?
Expanding fully: A(x^3 - x^2 - x + 1) + B(x^2 - 1) + C(x + 1) + D(x^3 -

3x^2 + 3x - 1); the x^2 coefficient is -A + B - 3D = -1/8 + B + 3/8 = B + 1/4 = 1, so

B = 3/4.
Answer: 1/(8(x - 1)) + 3/(4(x - 1)^2) + 1/(2(x - 1)^3) - 1/(8(x + 1)). FLAG:

the printed key gives the last term as -1/(2(x - 1)^3); the cover-up value is x^2/(x +

1) at x = 1, which is +1/2, and recombining the key's form differs from the fraction

by -1/(x - 1)^3, so the key's sign is a misprint and the correct term is +1/(2(x -

1)^3).

Q9

9. Resolve (x - 1)/((x - 2)(x + 1)^3) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (x - 1)/((x - 2)(x + 1)^3) = A/(x - 2) + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 1)^2 + D/(x

+ 1)^3.
Step 2: Identity: x - 1 = A(x + 1)^3 + B(x - 2)(x + 1)^2 + C(x - 2)(x + 1) +

D(x - 2).
Step 3: Put x = 2: 1 = A(27), so A = 1/27.
Put x = -1: -2 = D(-3), so D = 2/3.

Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A + B, so B = -1/27.
Expanding: A(x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x

+ 1) + B(x^3 - 3x - 2) + C(x^2 - x - 2) + D(x - 2); the x^2 coefficient is 3A + C =

1/9 + C = 0, so C = -1/9.
Answer: 1/(27(x - 2)) - 1/(27(x + 1)) - 1/(9(x + 1)^2) +

2/(3(x + 1)^3).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q10

10. Resolve 4x^3/((x^2 - 1)(x + 1)^2) into partial fractions

Step 1: (x^2 - 1)(x + 1)^2 = (x - 1)(x + 1)^3.
Write 4x^3/((x - 1)(x + 1)^3) = A/(x -

1) + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 1)^2 + D/(x + 1)^3.
Step 2: Identity: 4x^3 = A(x + 1)^3 +

B(x - 1)(x + 1)^2 + C(x - 1)(x + 1) + D(x - 1).
Step 3: Put x = 1: 4 = A(8), so A =

1/2.
Put x = -1: -4 = D(-2), so D = 2.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 4 = A + B, so B =

7/2.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = 3A - B + C?
Expanding: A(x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1)

+ B(x^3 + x^2 - x - 1) + C(x^2 - 1) + D(x - 1); the x^2 coefficient is 3A + B + C =

3/2 + 7/2 + C = 5 + C = 0, so C = -5.
Answer: 1/(2(x - 1)) + 7/(2(x + 1)) - 5/(x +

1)^2 + 2/(x + 1)^3.
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q11

11. Resolve (2x + 1)/((x + 3)(x - 1)(x + 2)^2) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (2x + 1)/((x + 3)(x - 1)(x + 2)^2) = A/(x + 3) + B/(x - 1) + C/(x + 2) +

D/(x + 2)^2.
Step 2: Identity: 2x + 1 = A(x - 1)(x + 2)^2 + B(x + 3)(x + 2)^2 + C(x

+ 3)(x - 1)(x + 2) + D(x + 3)(x - 1).
Step 3: Put x = -3: -5 = A(-4)(1) = -4A, so A =

5/4.
Put x = 1: 3 = B(4)(9) = 36B, so B = 1/12.
Put x = -2: -3 = D(1)(-3) = -3D, so D

= 1.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A + B + C, so C = -5/4 - 1/12 = -4/3. Answer:

5/(4(x + 3)) + 1/(12(x - 1)) - 4/(3(x + 2)) + 1/(x + 2)^2.
This agrees with the book's

Answers (p. 417).

Q12

12. Resolve 2x^4/((x - 3)(x + 2)^2) into partial fractions

Step 1: (x - 3)(x + 2)^2 = x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 12.
Dividing: (2x - 2)(x^3 + x^2 - 8x -

12) = 2x^4 - 18x^2 - 8x + 24, so 2x^4 = (2x - 2)(x - 3)(x + 2)^2 + (18x^2 + 8x -

24).
Step 2: Resolve (18x^2 + 8x - 24)/((x - 3)(x + 2)^2) = A/(x - 3) + B/(x + 2) +

C/(x + 2)^2.
Put x = 3: 162 + 24 - 24 = 162 = A(25), so A = 162/25. Put x = -2: 72 -

16 - 24 = 32 = C(-5), so C = -32/5.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 18 = A + B, so B =

288/25.
Answer: 2x - 2 + 162/(25(x - 3)) + 288/(25(x + 2)) - 32/(5(x + 2)^2). This

agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

mcqs.q: In resolving (2x^2 - 3x + 4)/(x - 1)^3 = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x - 1)^3, what is C?
mcqs.why: 2x^2 - 3x + 4 = A(x - 1)^2 + B(x - 1) + C. Put x = 1: 2 - 3 + 4 = 3 = C, so C = 3 (equating x^2 coefficients gives A = 2 and then B = 1).

mcqs.q: In resolving (2x^2 - 3x + 4)/(x - 1)^3 = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x - 1)^3, what is B?
mcqs.why: 2x^2 - 3x + 4 = A(x - 1)^2 + B(x - 1) + C with A = 2 and C = 3. Equating x coefficients: -2A + B = -3, so B = -3 + 2A = -3 + 4 = 1.

mcqs.q: In resolving (5x^2 - 2x + 3)/(x + 2)^3 = A/(x + 2) + B/(x + 2)^2 + C/(x + 2)^3, what is B?
mcqs.why: 5x^2 - 2x + 3 = A(x + 2)^2 + B(x + 2) + C. Equating x^2 coefficients: A = 5. Equating x coefficients: 4A + B = -2, so B = -2 - 4(5) = -22 (and C = 27 from x = -2).

mcqs.q: In resolving 4x/((x + 1)^2 (x - 1)) = A/(x + 1) + B/(x + 1)^2 + C/(x - 1), what is B?
mcqs.why: 4x = A(x + 1)(x - 1) + B(x - 1) + C(x + 1)^2. Put x = -1: -4 = B(-2), so B = 2 (also x = 1 gives C = 1 and then A = -1).

mcqs.q: In resolving 9/((x + 2)^2 (x - 1)) = A/(x + 2) + B/(x + 2)^2 + C/(x - 1), what is B?
mcqs.why: 9 = A(x + 2)(x - 1) + B(x - 1) + C(x + 2)^2. Put x = -2: 9 = B(-3), so B = -3 (also x = 1 gives C = 1 and then A = -1).

mcqs.q: In resolving 1/((x - 3)^2 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 3) + B/(x - 3)^2 + C/(x + 1), what is C?
In resolving x^2/((x - 2)(x - 1)^2) = A/(x - 2) + B/(x - 1) + C/(x - 1)^2, what is A?
mcqs.why: x^2 = A(x - 1)^2 + B(x - 2)(x - 1) + C(x - 2). Put x = 2: 4 = A(1)^2, so A = 4 (also x = 1 gives C = -1 and then B = -3).

mcqs.q: In resolving 1/((x - 1)^2 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x + 1), what is B?
mcqs.why: 1 = A(x - 1)(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + C(x - 1)^2. Put x = 1: 1 = B(2), so B = 1/2 (also x = -1 gives C = 1/4 and then A = -1/4).

mcqs.q: In resolving x^2/((x - 1)^3 (x + 1)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + C/(x - 1)^3 + D/(x + 1), what is C? (The printed key has an error here.)
mcqs.why: x^2 = A(x - 1)^2(x + 1) + B(x - 1)(x + 1) + C(x + 1) + D(x - 1)^3. Put x = 1: 1 = C(2), so C = 1/2. The printed key's last-term form with -1/(2(x - 1)^3) is a misprint: the cover-up value x^2/(x + 1) at x = 1 is +1/2, and the key's form differs from the fraction by -1/(x - 1)^3, so the correct term is +1/(2(x - 1)^3).

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Resolve (9x - 7)/((x^2 + 1)(x + 3)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (9x - 7)/((x^2 + 1)(x + 3)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + C/(x + 3). Step 2:

Identity: 9x - 7 = (Ax + B)(x + 3) + C(x^2 + 1).
Step 3: Put x = -3: -34 = C(10), so C

= -17/5.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A = 17/5.
Equating constants: -7 =

3B + C, so 3B = -7 + 17/5 = -18/5, B = -6/5.
Answer: (17x - 6)/(5(x^2 + 1)) - 17/(5(x

+ 3)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q2

2. Resolve 1/((x^2 + 1)(x + 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((x^2 + 1)(x + 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + C/(x + 1). Step 2:

Identity: 1 = (Ax + B)(x + 1) + C(x^2 + 1).
Step 3: Put x = -1: 1 = C(2), so C = 1/2.

Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A = -1/2.
Equating constants: 1 = B + C, so

B = 1/2.
Answer: (1 - x)/(2(x^2 + 1)) + 1/(2(x + 1)).
This agrees with the book's

Answers (p. 417) (the key writes (1 - x)/(2(1 + x^2))).

Q3

3. Resolve (3x + 7)/((x^2 + 4)(x + 3)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (3x + 7)/((x^2 + 4)(x + 3)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 4) + C/(x + 3). Step 2:

Identity: 3x + 7 = (Ax + B)(x + 3) + C(x^2 + 4).
Step 3: Put x = -3: -2 = C(13), so C

= -2/13.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A = 2/13.
Equating constants: 7 =

3B + 4C = 3B - 8/13, so 3B = 99/13, B = 33/13.
Answer: (2x + 33)/(13(x^2 + 4)) -

2/(13(x + 3)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q4

4. Resolve (x^2 + 15)/((x^2 + 2x + 5)(x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (x^2 + 15)/((x^2 + 2x + 5)(x - 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 2x + 5) + C/(x -

1).
Step 2: Identity: x^2 + 15 = (Ax + B)(x - 1) + C(x^2 + 2x + 5). Step 3: Put x =

1: 16 = C(8), so C = 2.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A + C, so A = -1. Equating

constants: 15 = -B + 5C = -B + 10, so B = -5.
Answer: -(x + 5)/(x^2 + 2x + 5) +

2/(x - 1).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q5

5. Resolve x^2/((x^2 + 4)(x + 2)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write x^2/((x^2 + 4)(x + 2)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 4) + C/(x + 2). Step 2:

Identity: x^2 = (Ax + B)(x + 2) + C(x^2 + 4).
Step 3: Put x = -2: 4 = C(8), so C =

1/2.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A + C, so A = 1/2.
Equating constants: 0 = 2B +

4C = 2B + 2, so B = -1.
Answer: (x - 2)/(2(x^2 + 4)) + 1/(2(x + 2)). This agrees with

the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q6

6. Resolve (x^2 + 1)/(x^3 + 1) into partial fractions

Step 1: x^3 + 1 = (x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1).
Write (x^2 + 1)/((x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1)) = (Ax

+ B)/(x^2 - x + 1) + C/(x + 1).
Step 2: Identity: x^2 + 1 = (Ax + B)(x + 1) + C(x^2

- x + 1).
Step 3: Put x = -1: 2 = C(3), so C = 2/3.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A +

C, so A = 1/3.
Equating constants: 1 = B + C, so B = 1/3.
Answer: (x + 1)/(3(x^2 - x

+ 1)) + 2/(3(x + 1)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q7

7. Resolve (x^2 + 2x + 2)/((x^2 + 3)(x + 1)(x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: (x + 1)(x - 1) = x^2 - 1.
Write (x^2 + 2x + 2)/((x^2 + 3)(x^2 - 1)) = (Ax +

B)/(x^2 + 3) + C/(x + 1) + D/(x - 1).
Step 2: Identity: x^2 + 2x + 2 = (Ax + B)(x^2

- 1) + C(x^2 + 3)(x - 1) + D(x^2 + 3)(x + 1).
Step 3: Put x = -1: 1 = C(4)(-2) = -8C,

so C = -1/8.
Put x = 1: 5 = D(4)(2) = 8D, so D = 5/8.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 =

A + C + D = A + 1/2, so A = -1/2.
Equating constants: 2 = -B - 3C + 3D = -B + 3/8

+ 15/8 = -B + 9/4, so B = 1/4.
Answer: -(2x - 1)/(4(x^2 + 3)) - 1/(8(x + 1)) + 5/(8(x -

1)).
FLAG: the printed key's form for this question does not recombine to the printed

fraction (it differs by a non-zero rational function), so the key is misprinted here; the

answer above recombines exactly to the fraction in the question.

Q8

8. Resolve 1/((x - 1)^2 (x^2 + 2)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 1/((x - 1)^2 (x^2 + 2)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x - 1)^2 + (Cx + D)/(x^2 + 2).

Step 2: Identity: 1 = A(x - 1)(x^2 + 2) + B(x^2 + 2) + (Cx + D)(x - 1)^2. Step 3:

Put x = 1: 1 = B(3), so B = 1/3.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A + C. Equating x

coefficients: 0 = 2A + C - 2D. Equating constants: 1 = -2A + 2B + D = -2A + 2/3 +

D. Solving with C = -A: from the x coefficient, 2A - A - 2D = 0, so D = A/2; from the

constant, -2A + 2/3 + A/2 = 1, so -3A/2 = 1/3, A = -2/9, C = 2/9, D = -1/9. Answer:

-2/(9(x - 1)) + 1/(3(x - 1)^2) + (2x - 1)/(9(x^2 + 2)).
FLAG: the printed key's form

does not recombine to 1/((x - 1)^2 (x^2 + 2)) (it differs by x/(2(x - 1)^2 (x^2 +

2))), so the key is misprinted here; the answer above recombines exactly.

Q9

9. Resolve x^4/(1 - x^4) into partial fractions

Step 1: x^4/(1 - x^4) = -1 + 1/(1 - x^4), since x^4 = -(1 - x^4) + 1. Step 2: 1 - x^4

= (1 - x)(1 + x)(1 + x^2).
Write 1/((1 - x)(1 + x)(1 + x^2)) = A/(1 - x) + B/(1 + x) +

(Cx + D)/(1 + x^2).
Step 3: Identity: 1 = A(1 + x)(1 + x^2) + B(1 - x)(1 + x^2) +

(Cx + D)(1 - x^2).
Put x = 1: 1 = A(2)(2) = 4A, so A = 1/4.
Put x = -1: 1 = B(2)(2) =

4B, so B = 1/4.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A - B - C = -C, so C = 0. Equating

constants: 1 = A + B + D = 1/2 + D, so D = 1/2.
Answer: -1 + 1/(4(1 - x)) + 1/(4(1 +

x)) + 1/(2(1 + x^2)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q10

10. Resolve (x^2 - 2x + 3)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1) into partial fractions

Step 1: x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1).
Write (x^2 - 2x + 3)/((x^2 +

x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 - x + 1). Step 2:

Identity: x^2 - 2x + 3 = (Ax + B)(x^2 - x + 1) + (Cx + D)(x^2 + x + 1). Step 3:

Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so C = -A. Equating x coefficients: -2 = A - B +

C + D = -B + D, so D = B - 2.
Equating constants: 3 = B + D = 2B - 2, so B = 5/2, D

= 1/2.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = -A + B - C + D = -2A + 3, so A = 1, C = -1.

Answer: (2x + 5)/(2(x^2 + x + 1)) + (-2x + 1)/(2(x^2 - x + 1)). FLAG: the printed

key's form recombines to (x^2 - 2x)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1), i.e. the numerator without

the +3, so the key is misprinted here; the answer above recombines exactly to the

printed fraction.

mcqs.q: In resolving (9x - 7)/((x^2 + 1)(x + 3)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + C/(x + 3), what is C?
In resolving (9x - 7)/((x^2 + 1)(x + 3)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + C/(x + 3), what is A?
mcqs.why: 9x - 7 = (Ax + B)(x + 3) + C(x^2 + 1) with C = -17/5. Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = A + C, so A = -C = 17/5 (and B = -6/5 from the constants).

mcqs.q: In resolving 1/((x^2 + 1)(x + 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + C/(x + 1), what is C?
In resolving (3x + 7)/((x^2 + 4)(x + 3)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 4) + C/(x + 3), what is B?
mcqs.why: 3x + 7 = (Ax + B)(x + 3) + C(x^2 + 4) with C = -2/13 and A = 2/13. Equating constants: 7 = 3B + 4C = 3B - 8/13, so 3B = 99/13 and B = 33/13.

mcqs.q: In resolving (x^2 + 15)/((x^2 + 2x + 5)(x - 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 2x + 5) + C/(x - 1), what is C?
In resolving x^2/((x^2 + 4)(x + 2)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 4) + C/(x + 2), what is A?
mcqs.why: x^2 = (Ax + B)(x + 2) + C(x^2 + 4). Put x = -2: 4 = 8C, so C = 1/2. Equating x^2 coefficients: 1 = A + C, so A = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2 (and B = -1).

mcqs.q: In resolving (x^2 + 1)/(x^3 + 1) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 - x + 1) + C/(x + 1), what is C?
In resolving x^4/(1 - x^4) = -1 + A/(1 - x) + B/(1 + x) + (Cx + D)/(1 + x^2), what is D?
mcqs.why: x^4/(1 - x^4) = -1 + 1/(1 - x^4) and 1 = A(1 + x)(1 + x^2) + B(1 - x)(1 + x^2) + (Cx + D)(1 - x^2). Cover-up gives A = B = 1/4 and C = 0; equating constants: 1 = A + B + D = 1/2 + D, so D = 1/2.

mcqs.q: In resolving (x^2 - 2x + 3)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 - x + 1), what is B? (The printed key has an error here.)
mcqs.why: x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1). Equating constants: 3 = B + D; equating x coefficients: -2 = -B + D, so D = B - 2 and 3 = 2B - 2, giving B = 5/2 (with A = 1, C = -1, D = 1/2). The printed key's form recombines to the numerator without the +3, so it is misprinted; the value above recombines exactly.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Resolve (x^3 + 2x + 2)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (x^3 + 2x + 2)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx +

D)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2.
Step 2: Identity: x^3 + 2x + 2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + x + 1) + Cx +

D. Step 3: Equating x^3 coefficients: A = 1.
Equating x^2 coefficients: A + B = 0,

so B = -1.
Equating x coefficients: A + B + C = 2, so C = 2.
Equating constants: B +

D = 2, so D = 3.
Answer: (x - 1)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (2x + 3)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2. This

agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q2

2. Resolve x^2/((x^2 + 1)^2 (x - 1)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write x^2/((x^2 + 1)^2 (x - 1)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 +

1)^2 + E/(x - 1).
Step 2: Identity: x^2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 1)(x - 1) + (Cx + D)(x - 1)

+ E(x^2 + 1)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 1: 1 = E(4), so E = 1/4.
Equating x^4 coefficients:

0 = A + E, so A = -1/4.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = -A + B, so B = -1/4.

Expanding (Ax + B)(x^3 - x^2 + x - 1) + (Cx + D)(x - 1) + E(x^2 + 1)^2: the x^2

coefficient is A - B + C + 2E = C + 1/2 = 1, so C = 1/2; the x coefficient is -A + B - C

+ D = D - 1/2 = 0, so D = 1/2.
Answer: -(x + 1)/(4(x^2 + 1)) + (x + 1)/(2(x^2 +

1)^2) + 1/(4(x - 1)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q3

3. Resolve (2x - 5)/((x^2 + 2)^2 (x - 2)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write (2x - 5)/((x^2 + 2)^2 (x - 2)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 2) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 +

2)^2 + E/(x - 2).
Step 2: Identity: 2x - 5 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 2)(x - 2) + (Cx + D)(x - 2)

+ E(x^2 + 2)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 2: -1 = E(36), so E = -1/36. Equating x^4

coefficients: 0 = A + E, so A = 1/36.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = -2A + B, so B =

2/36 = 1/18.
Equating x^2 coefficients: 0 = 2A - 2B + C + 4E = 1/18 - 1/9 + C - 1/9

= C - 1/6, so C = 1/6.
Equating constants: -5 = -4B - 2D + 4E = -2/9 - 2D - 1/9 = -1/3

- 2D, so D = 7/3.
Answer: (x + 2)/(36(x^2 + 2)) + (x + 14)/(6(x^2 + 2)^2) - 1/(36(x

- 2)).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q4

4. Resolve 8x^2/((x^2 + 1)^2 (1 - x)) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write 8x^2/((x^2 + 1)^2 (1 - x)) = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 +

1)^2 + E/(1 - x).
Step 2: Identity: 8x^2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 1)(1 - x) + (Cx + D)(1 - x)

+ E(x^2 + 1)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 1: 8 = E(4), so E = 2.
Equating x^4 coefficients: 0

= -A + E, so A = 2.
Equating x^3 coefficients: 0 = A - B, so B = 2. Expanding (Ax +

B)(x^2 + 1)(1 - x) + (Cx + D)(1 - x) + E(x^2 + 1)^2: the x^2 coefficient is -A + B -

C + 2E = -C + 4 = 8, so C = -4; the x coefficient is A - B - C + D?
The full expansion

gives D = -4.
Answer: 2(x + 1)/(x^2 + 1) - 4(x + 1)/(x^2 + 1)^2 + 2/(1 - x). FLAG:

the printed key's form, 1/(1 - x) + 1/(1 + x) + 2/(x^2 + 1) - 4/(x^2 + 1)^2, does not

recombine to the printed fraction (it differs by 8x^3/((x^2 + 1)^2 (1 - x^2))), so

the key is misprinted here; the answer above recombines exactly.

Q5

5. Resolve (4x^4 + 3x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x)/((x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)^2) into partial

fractions

Step 1: Write the fraction as (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 +

E/(x - 1).
Step 2: Identity: 4x^4 + 3x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x = (Ax + B)(x^2 + x + 1)(x - 1)

+ (Cx + D)(x - 1) + E(x^2 + x + 1)^2.
Step 3: Put x = 1: 4 + 3 + 6 + 5 = 18 = E(9),

so E = 2.
Equating x^4 coefficients: 4 = A + E, so A = 2.
Expanding (Ax + B)(x^3 -

1) + (Cx + D)(x - 1) + E(x^2 + x + 1)^2: the x^3 coefficient is B + 2E = 3, so B =

-1; the x^2 coefficient is C + 3E = 6, so C = 0; the x coefficient is -A + D - C + 2E =

D + 2 = 5, so D = 3.
Answer: (2x - 1)/(x^2 + x + 1) + 3/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 + 2/(x -

1).
This agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417).

Q6

6. Resolve (2x^4 - 3x^3 - 4x)/((x^2 + 2)^2 (x + 1)^2) into partial fractions

Step 1: Write the fraction as (Ax + B)/(x^2 + 2) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 + 2)^2 + E/(x + 1)

+ F/(x + 1)^2.
Step 2: Identity: 2x^4 - 3x^3 - 4x = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 2)(x + 1)^2 +

(Cx + D)(x + 1)^2 + E(x^2 + 2)^2 (x + 1) + F(x^2 + 2)^2.
Step 3: Put x = -1: 2 +

3 + 4 = 9 = F(9), so F = 1.
Equating x^5 coefficients: 0 = A + E. Equating x^4

coefficients: 2 = 2A + B + 4E?
Solving the full system gives A = 1, B = 0, C = -2, D

= 0, E = -1.
Answer: x/(x^2 + 2) - 2x/(x^2 + 2)^2 - 1/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 1)^2. This

agrees with the book's Answers (p. 417) (the key writes -1/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 1)^2 +

x/(x^2 + 2) - 2x/(x^2 + 2)^2).

mcqs.q: In resolving (x^3 + 2x + 2)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2, what is A?
mcqs.why: x^3 + 2x + 2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + x + 1) + Cx + D. Equating x^3 coefficients: A = 1 (then B = -1, C = 2, D = 3).

mcqs.q: In resolving (x^3 + 2x + 2)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2 = (Ax + B)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (Cx + D)/(x^2 + x + 1)^2, what is D?
mcqs.why: x^3 + 2x + 2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + x + 1) + Cx + D with A = 1 and B = -1 (from the x^2 coefficients: A + B = 0). Equating constants: B + D = 2, so D = 2 - B = 2 + 1 = 3.
With A = B = -1/4 and E = 1/4, expanding the identity x^2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 1)(x - 1) + (Cx + D)(x - 1) + E(x^2 + 1)^2, the x^2 coefficient is A - B + C + 2E = C + 1/2 = 1, so C = 1/2 (and D = 1/2).
With A = B = 2 and E = 2, expanding 8x^2 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 1)(1 - x) + (Cx + D)(1 - x) + E(x^2 + 1)^2, the x^2 coefficient is -A + B - C + 2E = -C + 4 = 8, so C = -4 (and D = -4).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Write the first four terms of the following sequences, if i) a_n = 2n - 3 ii) a_n =

(-1)^n n^2 iii) a_n = (-1)^n (2n - 3) iv) a_n = 3n - 5 v) a_n = n/(2n + 1) vi) a_n =

1/2^n vii) a_n - a_{n-1} = n + 2, a_1 = 2 viii) a_n = n a_{n-1}, a_1 = 1 ix) a_n = (n

+ 1) a_{n-1}, a_1 = 1 x) a_n = 1/(a + (n - 1)d)

i) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4: -1, 1, 3, 5. ii) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4: -1, 4, -9, 16. iii) Putting n

= 1, 2, 3, 4: 1, 1, -3, 5. iv) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4: -2, 1, 4, 7. v) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4:

1/3, 2/5, 3/7, 4/9. vi) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16. vii) a_1 = 2; a_2 =

a_1 + 4 = 6; a_3 = a_2 + 5 = 11; a_4 = a_3 + 6 = 17.
So the first four terms are 2,

6, 11, 17. viii) a_1 = 1; a_2 = 2 x 1 = 2; a_3 = 3 x 2 = 6; a_4 = 4 x 6 = 24. So the

first four terms are 1, 2, 6, 24. ix) a_1 = 1; a_2 = 3 x 1 = 3; a_3 = 4 x 3 = 12; a_4 =

5 x 12 = 60.
So the first four terms are 1, 3, 12, 60. x) Putting n = 1, 2, 3, 4: 1/a,

1/(a + d), 1/(a + 2d), 1/(a + 3d).

Q2

2. Find the indicated terms of the following sequences: i) 2, 6, 11, 17, ... a_7 ii) 1, 3,

12, 60, ... a_6 iii) 1, 3/2, 5/4, 7/8, ... a_7 iv) 1, 1, -3, 5, -7, 9, ... a_8 v) 1, -3, 5, -7, 9,

-11, ... a_8

i) The differences are 4, 5, 6, ..., so a_n = (n^2 + 5n - 2)/2 (check: n = 1 gives 2, n

= 2 gives 6, n = 3 gives 11, n = 4 gives 17).
Hence a_7 = (49 + 35 - 2)/2 = 41. ii)

Each term is obtained by multiplying by 3, 4, 5, ..., so a_5 = 60 x 6 = 360 and a_6 =

360 x 7 = 2520. iii) The numerators are 1, 3, 5, 7, ... and the denominators are 1, 2,

4, 8, ..., so a_n = (2n - 1)/2^(n-1).
Hence a_7 = 13/64. iv) From the second term

onwards the terms are (-1)^n (2n - 3) (check: n = 2 gives 1, n = 3 gives -3, n = 4

gives 5, n = 5 gives -7, n = 6 gives 9), and a_1 = 1.
Hence a_8 = (2 x 8 - 3) = 13. v)

Here a_n = (-1)^(n+1) (2n - 1), so a_8 = -(2 x 8 - 1) = -15.

Q3

3. Find the next two terms of the following sequences: i) 7, 9, 12, 16, ... ii) 1, 3, 7,

15, 31, ... iii) -1, 2, 12, 40, ... iv) 1, -3, 5, -7, 9, -11, ...

i) The differences are 2, 3, 4, ..., so the next differences are 5 and 6, giving 16 + 5 =

21 and 21 + 6 = 27. ii) The differences are 2, 4, 8, 16, ..., so the next differences

are 32 and 64, giving 31 + 32 = 63 and 63 + 64 = 127. iii) The terms satisfy

a_{n+1} = 2a_n + 2^(n+1) (check: 2 x (-1) + 4 = 2, 2 x 2 + 8 = 12, 2 x 12 + 16 =

40), so the next terms are 2 x 40 + 32 = 112 and 2 x 112 + 64 = 288. iv) Here a_n

= (-1)^(n+1) (2n - 1), so the next terms are a_7 = -13 and a_8 = 15. FLAG: the

printed key writes these as 13, -15, with the signs reversed; the sequence 1, -3, 5,

-7, 9, -11 continues with -13, 15.

mcqs.q: If a_n = 2n - 3, what are the first four terms?
If a_n = (-1)^n n^2, what are the first four terms?
If a_n = n/(2n + 1), what are the first four terms?
If a_n = 1/2^n, what are the first four terms?
If a_n - a_{n-1} = n + 2 and a_1 = 2, what are the first four terms?
If a_n = n a_{n-1} and a_1 = 1, what are the first four terms?
For the sequence 2, 6, 11, 17, ... with a_n = (n^2 + 5n - 2)/2, what is a_7?
mcqs.why: a_7 = (7^2 + 5(7) - 2)/2 = (49 + 35 - 2)/2 = 82/2 = 41, using the formula given in the notes.

mcqs.q: For the sequence 1, 3, 12, 60, ... where each term is obtained by multiplying by 3, 4, 5, ..., what is a_6?
mcqs.why: a_5 = 60 x 6 = 360 and a_6 = 360 x 7 = 2520, continuing the multipliers 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

mcqs.q: For the sequence 1, 3/2, 5/4, 7/8, ... with a_n = (2n - 1)/2^(n-1), what is a_7?
mcqs.why: a_7 = (2(7) - 1)/2^(7-1) = 13/2^6 = 13/64, since numerators are odd numbers and denominators are powers of 2.

mcqs.q: For the sequence 1, -3, 5, -7, 9, -11, ... with a_n = (-1)^(n+1) (2n - 1), what is a_8?
mcqs.why: a_8 = (-1)^(8+1) (2 x 8 - 1) = (-1)^9 x 15 = -15. This matches the notes' own working for this sequence in Q2(v) of the same exercise, where a_8 = -(2 x 8 - 1) = -15.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Write the first four terms of the following arithmetic sequences, if i) a_1 = 5 and

other three consecutive terms are 23, 26, 29 ii) a_5 = 17 and a_9 = 37 iii) 3a_7 =

7a_4 and a_10 = 33

i) The three consecutive terms 23, 26, 29 give the common difference d = 3. With

a_1 = 5, the first four terms are 5, 8, 11, 14. ii) a_9 - a_5 = 4d = 37 - 17 = 20, so d

= 5.
Then a_1 = a_5 - 4d = 17 - 20 = -3, so the first four terms are -3, 2, 7, 12. iii)

3(a_1 + 6d) = 7(a_1 + 3d) gives -4a_1 = 3d, i.e. a_1 = -3d/4.
Also a_10 = a_1 + 9d

= 33, so -3d/4 + 9d = 33, i.e.
33d/4 = 33, so d = 4 and a_1 = -3. Hence the first

four terms are -3, 1, 5, 9.

Q2-5

2. If a_{n-3} = 2n - 5, find the nth term of the sequence. 3. If the 5th term of an A.P.

is 16 and the 20th term is 46, what is its 12th term? 4. Find the 13th term of the

sequence x, 1, 2 - x, 3 - 2x, ... 5. Find the 18th term of the A.P. if its 6th term is 19

and the 9th term is 31.

2.
Put m = n - 3, so n = m + 3 and a_m = 2(m + 3) - 5 = 2m + 1. Hence a_n = 2n +

1.
3. a_20 - a_5 = 15d = 46 - 16 = 30, so d = 2.
Then a_12 = a_5 + 7d = 16 + 14 =

30. 4.
The common difference is 1 - x, so a_13 = x + 12(1 - x) = 12 - 11x. 5. a_9 -

a_6 = 3d = 31 - 19 = 12, so d = 4.
Then a_18 = a_6 + 12d = 19 + 48 = 67.

Q6-9

6. Which term of the A.P. 5, 2, -1, ... is -85? 7. Which term of the A.P. -2, 4, 10, ... is

148? 8. How many terms are there in the A.P. in which a_1 = 11, a_n = 68, d = 3? 9.

If the nth term of the A.P. is 3n - 1, find the A.P. 10.
Determine whether i) -19, ii) 2

are the terms of the A.P. 17, 13, 9, ... or not.

6. Here d = -3.
Setting 5 + (n - 1)(-3) = -85 gives (n - 1)(-3) = -90, so n - 1 = 30 and

n = 31.
So -85 is the 31st term. 7. Here d = 6.
Setting -2 + (n - 1)6 = 148 gives (n -

1)6 = 150, so n - 1 = 25 and n = 26.
So 148 is the 26th term. 8. Setting 11 + (n -

1)3 = 68 gives (n - 1)3 = 57, so n - 1 = 19 and n = 20.
So there are 20 terms. 9.

Putting n = 1, 2, 3, ...: 2, 5, 8, ...
So the A.P. is 2, 5, 8, 11, ... 10. Here d = -4. i)

Setting 17 + (n - 1)(-4) = -19 gives (n - 1)(-4) = -36, so n = 10: -19 is the 10th term.

ii) Setting 17 + (n - 1)(-4) = 2 gives (n - 1)(-4) = -15, so n - 1 = 15/4, which is not an

integer: 2 is not a term of the A.P.

11.
If l, m, n are the pth, qth and rth terms of an A.P., show that i) l(q - r) + m(r - p)

+ n(p - q) = 0 ii) p(m - n) + q(n - l) + r(l - m) = 0 12.
Find the nth term of the

sequence, (4/3)^2, (7/3)^2, (10/3)^2, ... 13.
If 1/a, 1/b and 1/c are in A.P., show that

b = 2ac/(a + c) 14.
If 1/a, 1/b and 1/c are in A.P., show that the common difference

is (a - c)/(2ac)

11.
Write l = a + (p - 1)d, m = a + (q - 1)d, n = a + (r - 1)d. i) l(q - r) + m(r - p) +

n(p - q) = a[(q - r) + (r - p) + (p - q)] + d[(p - 1)(q - r) + (q - 1)(r - p) + (r - 1)(p - q)]

= 0 + d[0] = 0, since the bracket expands to pq - pr - q + r + qr - pq - r + p + rp -

rq - p + q = 0. ii) m - n = (q - r)d, n - l = (r - p)d, l - m = (p - q)d, so p(m - n) + q(n -

l) + r(l - m) = d[p(q - r) + q(r - p) + r(p - q)] = d[0] = 0. 12.
The bases 4/3, 7/3, 10/3,

... are in A.P. with first term 4/3 and common difference 1, so the nth base is (3n +

1)/3.
Hence the nth term is ((3n + 1)/3)^2. 13.
Since 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in A.P., 2/b =

1/a + 1/c = (a + c)/(ac), so b = 2ac/(a + c). 14.
The common difference is 1/b - 1/a

= (a + c)/(2ac) - 1/a = (a - c)/(2ac).

mcqs.q: An A.P. has a_1 = 5 and three consecutive terms 23, 26, 29, so d = 3. What are its first four terms?
If a_5 = 17 and a_9 = 37 in an A.P., what is a_1?
If 3a_7 = 7a_4 and a_10 = 33 in an A.P., what are the first four terms?
If a_{n-3} = 2n - 5, what is the nth term a_n?
mcqs.why: Put m = n - 3, so n = m + 3 and a_m = 2(m + 3) - 5 = 2m + 1. Hence a_n = 2n + 1.

mcqs.q: The 5th term of an A.P. is 16 and the 20th term is 46. What is its 12th term?
What is the 13th term of the sequence x, 1, 2 - x, 3 - 2x, ... ?
mcqs.why: Common difference d = 1 - x. So a_13 = x + 12(1 - x) = x + 12 - 12x = 12 - 11x.

mcqs.q: Which term of the A.P. 5, 2, -1, ... is -85?
Which term of the A.P. -2, 4, 10, ... is 148?
How many terms are in the A.P. with a_1 = 11, a_n = 68 and d = 3?
For the A.P. 17, 13, 9, ... which statement is correct?
options: -19 is the 10th term and 2 is the 11th term
-19 is not a term and 2 is the 10th term
-19 is the 9th term and 2 is a term
-19 is the 10th term and 2 is not a term
mcqs.why: d = -4. For -19: 17 + (n-1)(-4) = -19 gives n = 10. For 2: (n-1)(-4) = -15 gives n-1 = 15/4, not an integer, so 2 is not a term.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-6

1. Find A.M. between i) 3 sqrt(5) and 5 sqrt(5) ii) x - 3 and x + 5 iii) 1 - x + x^2 and

1 + x + x^2 2. If 5, 8 are two A.Ms between a and b, find a and b. 3. Find 6 A.Ms.

between 2 and 5. 4. Find four A.Ms. between sqrt(2) and 12/sqrt(2). 5. Insert 7 A.Ms.

between 4 and 8. 6. Find three A.Ms between 3 and 11.

1. i) (3 sqrt(5) + 5 sqrt(5))/2 = 4 sqrt(5). ii) ((x - 3) + (x + 5))/2 = x + 1. iii) ((1 - x +

x^2) + (1 + x + x^2))/2 = 1 + x^2. 2.
Since a, 5, 8, b are in A.P., the common

difference is 8 - 5 = 3, so a = 5 - 3 = 2 and b = 8 + 3 = 11. 3. The common

difference is (5 - 2)/7 = 3/7, so the six A.Ms are 17/7, 20/7, 23/7, 26/7, 29/7, 32/7. 4.

Since 12/sqrt(2) = 6 sqrt(2), the common difference is (6 sqrt(2) - sqrt(2))/5 =

sqrt(2), so the four A.Ms are 2 sqrt(2), 3 sqrt(2), 4 sqrt(2), 5 sqrt(2). 5. The common

difference is (8 - 4)/8 = 1/2, so the seven A.Ms are 9/2, 5, 11/2, 6, 13/2, 7, 15/2. 6.

The common difference is (11 - 3)/4 = 2, so the three A.Ms are 5, 7, 9.

Q7-8

7. Find n so that (a^n + b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) may be the A.M. between a and

b. 8. Show that the sum of n A.Ms. between a and b is equal to n times their A.M.

7.
Setting (a^n + b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) = (a + b)/2 gives 2(a^n + b^n) = (a +

b)(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)), i.e.
2a^n + 2b^n = a^n + ab^(n-1) + a^(n-1)b + b^n, i.e.

a^n + b^n - ab^(n-1) - a^(n-1)b = 0, i.e.
(a - b)(a^(n-1) - b^(n-1)) = 0. For a != b

this gives a^(n-1) = b^(n-1), so n - 1 = 0 and n = 1. 8.
The n A.Ms are a + d, a +

2d, ..., a + nd, where d = (b - a)/(n + 1).
Their sum is na + d(1 + 2 + ... + n) = na +

(b - a)n/2 = n(a + b)/2 = n times the A.M. (a + b)/2, as required.

mcqs.q: What is the A.M. between 3 sqrt(5) and 5 sqrt(5)?
What is the A.M. between x - 3 and x + 5?
What is the A.M. between 1 - x + x^2 and 1 + x + x^2?
If 5 and 8 are two A.Ms between a and b, what are a and b?
mcqs.why: a, 5, 8, b are in A.P. with d = 8 - 5 = 3, so a = 5 - 3 = 2 and b = 8 + 3 = 11.

mcqs.q: What are the six A.Ms between 2 and 5?
What are the four A.Ms between sqrt(2) and 12/sqrt(2)?
mcqs.why: 12/sqrt(2) = 6 sqrt(2). d = (6 sqrt(2) - sqrt(2))/5 = sqrt(2). Means: 2 sqrt(2), 3 sqrt(2), 4 sqrt(2), 5 sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: What is the common difference when 7 A.Ms are inserted between 4 and 8?
mcqs.why: With 7 means there are 8 steps: d = (8 - 4)/8 = 4/8 = 1/2. The means are 9/2, 5, 11/2, 6, 13/2, 7, 15/2.

mcqs.q: What are the three A.Ms between 3 and 11?
For what value of n is (a^n + b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) the A.M. between a and b (a != b)?
mcqs.why: Setting it equal to (a+b)/2 gives (a - b)(a^(n-1) - b^(n-1)) = 0. For a != b, a^(n-1) = b^(n-1), so n - 1 = 0 and n = 1.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of n A.Ms between a and b?
mcqs.why: The means sum to na + d(1+...+n) with d = (b-a)/(n+1), which simplifies to n(a+b)/2, i.e. n times their A.M. (a+b)/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-2

1. Find the sum of all the integral multiples of 3 between 4 and 97. 2. Sum the

series i) -3 + (-1) + 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + a_16 ii) 3/sqrt(2) + 2 sqrt(2) + 5/sqrt(2) + ... +

a_13 iii) 1.11 + 1.41 + 1.71 + ... + a_10 iv) -8 - 3 1/2 + 1 + ... + a_11 v) (x - a) + (x

+ a) + (x + 3a) + ... to n terms vi) 1/(1 - sqrt(x)) + 1/(1 - x) + 1/(1 + sqrt(x)) + ... to

n terms vii) 1/(1 + sqrt(x)) + 1/(1 - x) + 1/(1 - sqrt(x)) + ... to n terms

1.
The multiples are 6, 9, ..., 96: an A.P. with a = 6, d = 3 and 96 = 6 + 30 x 3, so n

= 31.
Sum = (31/2)(6 + 96) = 31 x 51 = 1581.
2. i) Here a = -3, d = 2, a_16 = -3 +

15 x 2 = 27.
Sum = (16/2)(-3 + 27) = 192. ii) The terms are 3/sqrt(2), 4/sqrt(2),

5/sqrt(2), ..., so d = 1/sqrt(2) and a_13 = 15/sqrt(2).
Sum = (13/2)(3/sqrt(2) +

15/sqrt(2)) = 117/sqrt(2). iii) Here a = 1.11, d = 0.30, a_10 = 1.11 + 9 x 0.30 =

3.81.
Sum = 5(1.11 + 3.81) = 24.6. iv) Here a = -8, d = 4.5, a_11 = -8 + 10 x 4.5 =

37.
Sum = (11/2)(-8 + 37) = 319/2 = 159.5. v) Here a = x - a, d = 2a. Sum =

(n/2)[2(x - a) + (n - 1)2a] = n[x + (n - 2)a]. vi) The common difference is -sqrt(x)/(1 -

x) (check: 1/(1 - x) - 1/(1 - sqrt(x)) = -sqrt(x)/(1 - x), and the same for the next pair).

Sum = (n/2)[2/(1 - sqrt(x)) + (n - 1)(-sqrt(x)/(1 - x))] = (n/2)[(2 + (3 - n)sqrt(x))/(1 -

x)]. vii) The common difference is +sqrt(x)/(1 - x), so similarly the sum is (n/2)[(2 +

(n - 3)sqrt(x))/(1 - x)].

Q3-8

3. How many terms of the series i) -7 + (-5) + (-3) + ... amount to 65? ii) -7 + (-4) +

(-1) + ... amount to 114? 4. Sum the series i) 3 + 5 - 7 + 9 + 11 - 13 + ... to 3n

terms ii) 1 + 4 - 7 + 10 + 13 - 16 + ... to 3n terms 5. Find the sum of 20 terms of

the series whose rth term is 3r + 1. 6. If S_n = n(2n - 1), then find the series. 7. The

ratio of the sums of n terms of two series in A.P. is 3n + 2 : n + 1. Find the ratio of

their 8th terms. 8. If S_2, S_3, S_5 are the sums of 2n, 3n, 5n terms of an A.P., show

that S_5 = 5(S_3 - S_2).

3. i) Here a = -7, d = 2: S_n = (n/2)[-14 + 2(n - 1)] = n(n - 8) = 65, i.e. n^2 - 8n - 65

= (n - 13)(n + 5) = 0, so n = 13 terms. ii) Here a = -7, d = 3: S_n = (n/2)[-14 + 3(n -

1)] = n(3n - 17)/2 = 114, i.e.
3n^2 - 17n - 228 = 0, i.e.
(3n + 19)(n - 12) = 0, so n =

12 terms.
4. i) Grouping in threes: (3 + 5 - 7) = 1, (9 + 11 - 13) = 7, (15 + 17 - 19)

= 13, ...: an A.P. with first term 1 and common difference 6. Sum of n groups =

(n/2)[2 + 6(n - 1)] = n(3n - 2). ii) Grouping in threes: (1 + 4 - 7) = -2, (10 + 13 - 16)

= 7, (19 + 22 - 25) = 16, ...: an A.P. with first term -2 and common difference 9.

Sum of n groups = (n/2)[-4 + 9(n - 1)] = (n/2)(9n - 13). 5.
S_20 = sum_{r=1}^{20}

(3r + 1) = 3(20 x 21/2) + 20 = 630 + 20 = 650.
6. a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = n(2n - 1) -

(n - 1)(2n - 3) = 4n - 3.
So the series is 1, 5, 9, 13, ... 7.
For an A.P., the nth term is

S_{2n-1}/(2n - 1) (since S_{2n-1} = (2n - 1)a_n).
Hence the ratio of the 8th terms is

S_15/S'_15 = (3 x 15 + 2)/(15 + 1) = 47/16. 8.
S_2 = n[2a + (2n - 1)d], S_3 =

(3n/2)[2a + (3n - 1)d], S_5 = (5n/2)[2a + (5n - 1)d].
Then S_3 - S_2 = 3na + (9n^2 -

3n)d/2 - 2na - (2n^2 - n)d = na + (5n^2 - n)d/2 = (n/2)[2a + (5n - 1)d] = S_5/5, so

S_5 = 5(S_3 - S_2), as required.

Q9-13

9. Obtain the sum of all integers in the first 1000 integers which are neither divisible

by 5 nor by 2. 10. S_8 and S_9 are the sums of the first eight and nine terms of an

A.P., find S_9 if 50S_9 = 63S_8 and a_1 = 2. (Hint: S_9 = S_8 + a_9) 11. The sum of

9 terms of an A.P. is 171 and its eighth term is 31. Find the series. 12. The sum of

S_9 and S_7 is 203 and S_9 - S_7 = 49, S_7 and S_9 being the sums of the first 7

and 9 terms of an A.P. respectively. Determine the series. 13. S_7 and S_9 are the

sums of the first 7 and 9 terms of an A.P. respectively. If S_9/S_7 = 18/11 and a_7 =

20, find the series.

9.
Sum of 1 to 1000 = 500500.
Sum of even numbers = 2 + 4 + ... + 1000 =

250500.
Sum of multiples of 5 = 5 + 10 + ... + 1000 = 100500.
Sum of multiples of

10 = 50500.
By inclusion-exclusion, the required sum = 500500 - 250500 - 100500

+ 50500 = 200000. 10.
S_8 = 4(4 + 7d) = 16 + 28d and S_9 = (9/2)(4 + 8d) = 18

+ 36d.
Then 50(18 + 36d) = 63(16 + 28d), i.e.
900 + 1800d = 1008 + 1764d, so

36d = 108 and d = 3.
Hence S_9 = 18 + 108 = 126. 11.
S_9 = (9/2)(2a + 8d) = 171

gives a + 4d = 19; and a_8 = a + 7d = 31.
Subtracting gives 3d = 12, so d = 4 and

a = 3.
Hence the series is 3, 7, 11, ... 12.
Solving S_9 + S_7 = 203 and S_9 - S_7 =

49 gives S_9 = 126 and S_7 = 77.
From S_7 = (7/2)(2a + 6d) = 77: a + 3d = 11.

From S_9 = (9/2)(2a + 8d) = 126: a + 4d = 14.
Hence d = 3 and a = 2, so the series

is 2, 5, 8, 11, ... 13.
From a_7 = a + 6d = 20 and S_9/S_7 = [9(a + 4d)]/[7(a + 3d)]

= 18/11, we get 11(a + 4d) = 14(a + 3d), i.e. 2d = 3a.
With a + 6d = 20 this gives

d = 3 and a = 2, so the series is 2, 5, 8, 11, ...

Q14-18

14. The sum of three numbers in an A.P. is 24 and their product is 440. Find the

numbers. 15. Find four numbers in A.P. whose sum is 32 and the sum of whose

squares is 276. 16. Find the five numbers in A.P. whose sum is 25 and the sum of

whose squares is 135. 17. The sum of the 6th and 8th terms of an A.P. is 40 and the

product of 4th and 7th terms is 220. Find the A.P. 18. If a^2, b^2 and c^2 are in

A.P., show that 1/(b + c), 1/(c + a), 1/(a + b) are in A.P.

14.
Let the numbers be a - d, a, a + d: their sum is 3a = 24, so a = 8. Their product

is 8(64 - d^2) = 440, so 64 - d^2 = 55 and d^2 = 9, i.e. d = +- 3. Hence the

numbers are 5, 8, 11 or 11, 8, 5. 15.
Let the numbers be a - 3d, a - d, a + d, a + 3d:

their sum is 4a = 32, so a = 8.
The sum of their squares is 4a^2 + 20d^2 = 256 +

20d^2 = 276, so d^2 = 1 and d = +- 1.
Hence the numbers are 5, 7, 9, 11 or 11, 9,

7, 5. 16.
Let the numbers be a - 2d, a - d, a, a + d, a + 2d: their sum is 5a = 25, so a

= 5.
The sum of their squares is 5a^2 + 10d^2 = 125 + 10d^2 = 135, so d^2 = 1

and d = +- 1.
Hence the numbers are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. 17. a_6 + a_8 =

2a + 12d = 40, so a + 6d = 20.
Also a_7 = a + 6d = 20, and a_4 x a_7 = 220 gives

a_4 = 11, i.e. a + 3d = 11.
Hence 3d = 9, so d = 3 and a = 2.
So the A.P. is 2, 5, 8,

11, ... 18.
We need 2/(c + a) = 1/(b + c) + 1/(a + b) = (a + 2b + c)/((a + b)(b + c)),

i.e.
2(a + b)(b + c) = (c + a)(a + c + 2b).
Expanding: the left side is 2ab + 2b^2 +

2ac + 2bc and the right side is a^2 + 2ac + c^2 + 2ab + 2bc. The two sides are

equal exactly when a^2 + c^2 = 2b^2, which is the given A.P. condition. Hence

1/(b + c), 1/(c + a), 1/(a + b) are in A.P., as required.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-5

1. A man deposits in a bank Rs. 10 in the first month; Rs. 15 in the second month;

Rs. 20 in the third month and so on. Find how much he will have deposited in the

bank by the 9th month. 2. 378 trees are planted in rows in the shape of an isosceles

triangle, the numbers in successive rows decreasing by one from the base to the

top. How many trees are there in the row which forms the base of the triangle? 3. A

man borrows Rs. 1100 and agree to repay with a total interest of Rs. 230 in 14

installments, each installment being less than the preceding by Rs. 10. What should

be his first installment? 4. A clock strikes once when its hour hand is at one, twice

when it is at two and so on. How many times does the clock strike in twelve hours?

5. A student saves Rs. 12 at the end of the first week and goes on increasing his

saving Rs. 4 weekly. After how many weeks will he be able to save Rs. 2100?

1.
The deposits form an A.P. with a = 10 and d = 5.
The total by the 9th month is

S_9 = (9/2)[20 + 8 x 5] = (9/2)(60) = Rs. 270. 2.
If the base row has n trees, the

rows have n, n - 1, ..., 1 trees, so n(n + 1)/2 = 378, i.e. n^2 + n - 756 = (n + 28)(n -

27) = 0, so n = 27 trees. 3.
The total repaid is 1100 + 230 = Rs. 1330. With d = -10

and n = 14: S_14 = 7[2a - 130] = 1330, so 2a - 130 = 190 and a = Rs. 160. So the

first installment is Rs. 160. 4.
The number of strikes is 1 + 2 + ... + 12 = 12 x 13/2

= 78. 5.
The weekly savings form an A.P. with a = 12 and d = 4. Setting S_n =

(n/2)[24 + 4(n - 1)] = 2n(n + 5) = 2100 gives n(n + 5) = 1050, i.e. n^2 + 5n - 1050

= (n + 35)(n - 30) = 0, so n = 30 weeks.

Q6-8

6. An object falling from rest, falls 9 meters during the first second, 27 meters

during the next second, 45 meters during the third second and so on. i) How far will

it fall during the fifth second? ii) How far will it fall up to the fifth second? 7. An

investor earned Rs. 6000 for year 1980 and Rs. 12000 for year 1990 on the same

investment. If his earning have increased by the same amount each year, how

much income he has received from the investment over the past eleven years? 8.

The sum of interior angles of polygons having sides 3, 4, 5, ... etc. form an A.P. Find

Q9-10

the sum of the interior angles for a 16 sided polygon. 9. The prize money Rs. 60,000

will be distributed among the eight teams according to their positions determined in

the match-series. The award increases by the same amount for each higher

position. If the last place team is given Rs. 4000, how much will be awarded to the

first place team? 10. An equilateral triangular base is filled by placing eight balls in

the first row, 7 balls in the second row and so on with one ball in the last row. After

this base layer, second layer is formed by placing 7 balls in its first row, 6 balls in its

second row and so on with one ball in its last row. Continuing this process, a

pyramid of balls is formed with one ball on top. How many balls are there in the

pyramid?

6.
The distances form an A.P. with a = 9 and d = 18. i) During the fifth second: a_5

= 9 + 4 x 18 = 81 meters. ii) Up to the fifth second: S_5 = (5/2)[18 + 4 x 18] =

(5/2)(90) = 225 meters. 7.
The yearly earnings form an A.P. with first term 6000

(1980) and 11th term 12000 (1990).
The total over the eleven years is S_11 =

(11/2)(6000 + 12000) = Rs. 99000. 8.
The sums of interior angles are 180, 360,

540, ... degrees: an A.P. with a = 180 and d = 180.
For a 16-sided polygon (the 14th

term, since 3 sides give the 1st term): a_14 = 180 + 13 x 180 = 2520 degrees = 14

pi radians. 9.
The awards form an A.P. with last term 4000 and S_8 = 60000. Writing

the awards from last place to first place: a = 4000, so 4[8000 + 7d] = 60000, i.e.

8000 + 7d = 15000 and d = 1000.
Hence the first place award is 4000 + 7 x 1000

= Rs. 11000. 10.
The bottom layer has 8 + 7 + ... + 1 = 36 balls; the next layer has

7 + 6 + ... + 1 = 28 balls; then 21, 15, 10, 6, 3, 1 balls.
Total = 36 + 28 + 21 + 15

+ 10 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 120 balls.

mcqs.q: A man deposits Rs. 10, Rs. 15, Rs. 20, ... in successive months. How much has he deposited by the 9th month?
378 trees are planted in rows forming an isosceles triangle, rows decreasing by one from base to top. How many trees are in the base row?
mcqs.why: If base has n trees, total = n(n+1)/2 = 378, so n^2 + n - 756 = (n+28)(n-27) = 0, giving n = 27.

mcqs.q: A man borrows Rs. 1100 and repays with total interest Rs. 230 in 14 installments, each Rs. 10 less than the preceding. What is the first installment?
A clock strikes once at one, twice at two, and so on. How many times does it strike in twelve hours?
A student saves Rs. 12 in the first week, increasing by Rs. 4 weekly. After how many weeks will he save Rs. 2100 in total?
An object falls 9 m in the first second, 27 m in the next, 45 m in the third, and so on. How far does it fall during the fifth second?
For the same falling object (9 m, 27 m, 45 m, ...), how far does it fall up to the fifth second?
The sums of interior angles of polygons with 3, 4, 5, ... sides form an A.P. What is the sum for a 16-sided polygon?
mcqs.why: Angles are 180, 360, 540, ... with a = 180, d = 180. 16 sides is the 14th term: a_14 = 180 + 13(180) = 2520 degrees.

mcqs.q: Prize money Rs. 60,000 is shared among eight teams in A.P. by position. The last place team gets Rs. 4000. How much does the first place team get?
mcqs.why: From last to first: a = 4000, S_8 = 4[8000 + 7d] = 60000 gives d = 1000. First place = 4000 + 7(1000) = 11000 rupees.

mcqs.q: A pyramid is built with layers of 36, 28, 21, 15, 10, 6, 3, 1 balls. How many balls are in the pyramid?

lessons.title: Exercise 6.6
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-6

1. Find the 5th term of the G.P.: 3, 6, 12, ... 2. Find the 11th term of the sequence, 1

+ i, 2, 4/(1 + i) 3. Find the 12th term of 1 + i, 2i, -2 + 2i, ... 4. Find the 11th term of

the sequence, 1 + i, 2, 2(1 - i) 5. If an automobile depreciates in values 5% every

year, at the end of 4 years what is the value of the automobile purchased for Rs.

12,000? 6. Which term of the sequence: x^2 - y^2, x + y, (x + y)/(x - y), ... is (x +

y)/(x - y)^9?

1.
Here a = 3 and r = 2, so a_5 = 3 x 2^4 = 48. 2.
Here r = 2/(1 + i) = 1 - i, so a_11

= (1 + i)(1 - i)^10.
Since (1 - i)^2 = -2i, (1 - i)^10 = (-2i)^5 = -32i, so a_11 = (1 +

i)(-32i) = 32(1 - i). 3.
Here r = 2i/(1 + i) = 1 + i, so a_12 = (1 + i)(1 + i)^11 = (1 +

i)^12 = ((1 + i)^2)^6 = (2i)^6 = -64. 4.
Here r = 2/(1 + i) = 1 - i, so a_11 = (1 +

i)(1 - i)^10 = 32(1 - i), as in Q2. 5.
The value after 4 years is 12000 x (0.95)^4 =

12000 x 0.81450625 = 9774.075, i.e. about Rs. 9774. 6.
Here a_1 = (x - y)(x + y)

and r = 1/(x - y), so a_n = (x + y)/(x - y)^(n-2).
Setting this equal to (x + y)/(x -

y)^9 gives n - 2 = 9, so n = 11.
Hence it is the 11th term.

Q7-8

7. If a, b, c, d are in G.P., prove that i) a - b, b - c, c - d are in G.P. ii) a^2 - b^2, b^2 -

c^2, c^2 - d^2 are in G.P. iii) a^2 + b^2, b^2 + c^2, c^2 + d^2 are in G.P. 8.

Show that the reciprocals of the terms of the geometric sequence a_1, a_1 r^2, a_1

r^4, ... form another geometric sequence.

7.
Write b = ar, c = ar^2, d = ar^3. i) a - b = a(1 - r), b - c = ar(1 - r), c - d = ar^2(1

- r): a G.P. with common ratio r. ii) a^2 - b^2 = a^2(1 - r^2), b^2 - c^2 = a^2

r^2(1 - r^2), c^2 - d^2 = a^2 r^4(1 - r^2): a G.P. with common ratio r^2. iii) a^2

+ b^2 = a^2(1 + r^2), b^2 + c^2 = a^2 r^2(1 + r^2), c^2 + d^2 = a^2 r^4(1

+ r^2): a G.P. with common ratio r^2. 8.
The reciprocals are 1/a_1, 1/(a_1 r^2),

1/(a_1 r^4), ...: each term is 1/r^2 times the preceding term, so they form a G.P.

with common ratio 1/r^2.

Q9-12

9. Find the nth term of the geometric sequence if: a_5/a_3 = 4/9 and a_2 = 4/9 10.

Find three consecutive numbers in G.P. whose sum is 26 and their product is 216.

11. If the sum of the four consecutive terms of a G.P. is 80 and A.M. of the second

and the fourth of them is 30. Find the terms. 12. If 1/a, 1/b and 1/c are in G.P., show

that the common ratio is +- sqrt(a/c)

9.
Since a_5/a_3 = r^2 = 4/9, r = 2/3 or r = -2/3.
Also a_2 = a_1 r = 4/9. For r = 2/3:

a_1 = 2/3 and a_n = (2/3)^n.
For r = -2/3: a_1 = -2/3 and a_n = (-2/3)^n = (-1)^n

(2/3)^n.
(The printed key gives the second form.) 10.
Let the numbers be a/r, a, ar:

their product is a^3 = 216, so a = 6.
Their sum is 6(1/r + 1 + r) = 26, i.e. 1/r + r =

10/3, i.e. r^2 - (10/3)r + 1 = 0, so r = 3 or r = 1/3.
Hence the numbers are 2, 6, 18

or 18, 6, 2. 11.
Let the terms be a, ar, ar^2, ar^3: a(1 + r + r^2 + r^3) = 80 and

(ar + ar^3)/2 = 30, i.e. ar(1 + r^2) = 60.
Dividing: (1 + r)/r = 80/60 = 4/3, so 3 +

3r = 4r and r = 3.
Then a(1 + 3)(1 + 9) = 80, so a = 2.
Hence the terms are 2, 6,

18, 54. 12.
Since 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in G.P., (1/b)^2 = (1/a)(1/c), so b^2 = ac and b =

+- sqrt(ac).
The common ratio is (1/b)/(1/a) = a/b = a/(+- sqrt(ac)) = +- sqrt(a/c).

Q13-14

13. If the numbers 1, 4 and 3 are subtracted from three consecutive terms of an

A.P., the resulting numbers are in G.P. Find the numbers if their sum is 21. 14. If

three consecutive numbers in A.P. are increased by 1, 4, 15 respectively, the

resulting numbers are in G.P. Find the original numbers if their sum is 6.

13.
Let the A.P. terms be a - d, a, a + d: their sum is 3a = 21, so a = 7. After

subtracting: 6 - d, 3, 4 + d are in G.P., so 3^2 = (6 - d)(4 + d), i.e. 9 = 24 + 2d -

d^2, i.e. d^2 - 2d - 15 = (d - 5)(d + 3) = 0, so d = 5 or d = -3. Hence the numbers

are 2, 7, 12 or 10, 7, 4. 14.
Let the A.P. terms be a - d, a, a + d: their sum is 3a = 6,

so a = 2.
After increasing: 3 - d, 6, 17 + d are in G.P., so 6^2 = (3 - d)(17 + d), i.e.

36 = 51 - 14d - d^2, i.e. d^2 + 14d - 15 = (d + 15)(d - 1) = 0, so d = 1 or d = -15.

Hence the original numbers are 1, 2, 3 or 17, 2, -13.

mcqs.q: What is the 5th term of the G.P. 3, 6, 12, ... ?
What is the 11th term of the sequence 1 + i, 2, 4/(1 + i), ... ?
What is the 12th term of 1 + i, 2i, -2 + 2i, ... ?
An automobile worth Rs. 12,000 depreciates 5% every year. What is its value at the end of 4 years?
Which term of x^2 - y^2, x + y, (x + y)/(x - y), ... is (x + y)/(x - y)^9?
mcqs.why: a_1 = (x-y)(x+y) and r = 1/(x-y), so a_n = (x+y)/(x-y)^(n-2). Setting n - 2 = 9 gives n = 11.

mcqs.q: If a, b, c, d are in G.P. with ratio r, what is the common ratio of a - b, b - c, c - d?
mcqs.why: Write b = ar, c = ar^2, d = ar^3: a-b = a(1-r), b-c = ar(1-r), c-d = ar^2(1-r), a G.P. with ratio r.

mcqs.q: The reciprocals of a_1, a_1 r^2, a_1 r^4, ... form a G.P. with what common ratio?
mcqs.why: Reciprocals are 1/a_1, 1/(a_1 r^2), 1/(a_1 r^4), ... Each term is 1/r^2 times the preceding term, so ratio = 1/r^2.

mcqs.q: Three consecutive numbers in G.P. have sum 26 and product 216. What are they?
mcqs.why: Let numbers be a/r, a, ar: product a^3 = 216 gives a = 6. Sum 6(1/r + 1 + r) = 26 gives r = 3 or 1/3. Numbers: 2, 6, 18 (or reverse).

mcqs.q: Four consecutive terms of a G.P. have sum 80 and the A.M. of the second and fourth is 30. What are the terms?
If 1/a, 1/b and 1/c are in G.P., what is the common ratio?
mcqs.why: From (1/b)^2 = (1/a)(1/c), b^2 = ac. Ratio = (1/b)/(1/a) = a/b = a/(+- sqrt(ac)) = +- sqrt(a/c).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.7
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-2

1. Find G.M. between i) -2 and 8 ii) -2i and 8i 2. Insert two G.Ms. between i) 1 and 8

ii) 2 and 16 3.
Insert three G.Ms. between i) 1 and 16 ii) 2 and 32 4. Insert four real

geometric means between 3 and 96.

1. i) The G.M. is +- sqrt((-2)(8)) = +- sqrt(-16) = +- 4i. ii) The G.M. is +-

sqrt((-2i)(8i)) = +- sqrt(16) = +- 4.
2. i) With two means, r^3 = 8/1 = 8, so r = 2

and the means are 2, 4. ii) With two means, r^3 = 16/2 = 8, so r = 2 and the means

Q3-8

are 4, 8. 3. i) With three means, r^4 = 16, so r = 2, -2, 2i or -2i, giving the sets (2,

4, 8), (-2, 4, -8), (2i, -4, -8i) and (-2i, -4, 8i). ii) With three means, r^4 = 32/2 = 16,

so r = 2, -2, 2i or -2i, giving the sets (4, 8, 16), (-4, 8, -16), (4i, -8, -16i) and (-4i, -8,

16i). 4. With four real means, r^5 = 96/3 = 32, so r = 2 and the means are 6, 12,

24, 48. FLAG: the printed key appears to read 8, 12, 24, 48 for this part, but the first

mean must be 3 x 2 = 6 (the full sequence is 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, with common

ratio 2 throughout); the key's first value is treated as a misprint.

5. If both x and y are positive distinct real numbers, show that the geometric mean

between x and y is less than their arithmetic mean. 6. For what value of n, (a^n +

b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) is the positive geometric mean between a and b? 7. The

A.M. of two positive integral numbers exceeds their (positive) G.M. by 2 and their

sum is 20, find the numbers. 8. The A.M. between two numbers is 5 and their

(positive) G.M. is 4. Find the numbers.

5.
Since x != y, (sqrt(x) - sqrt(y))^2 > 0, i.e. x + y > 2 sqrt(xy), i.e. (x + y)/2 >

sqrt(xy).
So the geometric mean sqrt(xy) is less than the arithmetic mean (x + y)/2,

as required. 6.
Setting (a^n + b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) = sqrt(ab) gives a^n +

b^n = sqrt(ab)(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)), i.e. a^n - a^(n-1/2) b^(1/2) - a^(1/2) b^(n-1/2)

+ b^n = 0, i.e.
(a^(n-1/2) - b^(n-1/2))(sqrt(a) - sqrt(b)) = 0.
For a != b this gives

a^(n-1/2) = b^(n-1/2), so n - 1/2 = 0 and n = 1/2. 7.
Let the numbers be x and y: (x

+ y)/2 - sqrt(xy) = 2 and x + y = 20, so sqrt(xy) = 8 and xy = 64. Hence x and y are

the roots of t^2 - 20t + 64 = (t - 16)(t - 4) = 0, so the numbers are 16 and 4. 8. Let

the numbers be x and y: x + y = 10 and xy = 16.
Hence x and y are the roots of t^2

- 10t + 16 = (t - 8)(t - 2) = 0, so the numbers are 8 and 2.

mcqs.q: What is the G.M. between -2 and 8?
What is the G.M. between -2i and 8i?
What are the two G.Ms between 1 and 8?
mcqs.why: With two means, r^3 = 8/1 = 8, so r = 2. Means: 1 x 2 = 2 and 2 x 2 = 4.

mcqs.q: What are the two G.Ms between 2 and 16?
mcqs.why: With two means, r^3 = 16/2 = 8, so r = 2. Means: 2 x 2 = 4 and 4 x 2 = 8.

mcqs.q: With r = 2, what are the three G.Ms between 1 and 16?
mcqs.why: With three means, r^4 = 16. For r = 2 the means are 2, 4, 8. Other roots -2, 2i, -2i give the other sets listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: What are the four real geometric means between 3 and 96?
mcqs.why: r^5 = 96/3 = 32, so r = 2. Means: 3x2 = 6, 12, 24, 48. The printed key appears to read 8 for the first mean; the notes flag this as a misprint because the sequence must be 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96 with ratio 2 throughout.

mcqs.q: For what value of n is (a^n + b^n)/(a^(n-1) + b^(n-1)) the positive G.M. between a and b (a != b)?
mcqs.why: Setting it equal to sqrt(ab) gives (a^(n-1/2) - b^(n-1/2))(sqrt(a)-sqrt(b)) = 0. For a != b, n - 1/2 = 0, so n = 1/2.

mcqs.q: The A.M. of two positive integers exceeds their positive G.M. by 2 and their sum is 20. What are the numbers?
mcqs.why: (x+y)/2 - sqrt(xy) = 2 with x+y = 20 gives sqrt(xy) = 8, xy = 64. Roots of t^2 - 20t + 64 = (t-16)(t-4) = 0 are 16 and 4.

mcqs.q: The A.M. between two numbers is 5 and their positive G.M. is 4. What are the numbers?
mcqs.why: x + y = 10 and xy = 16. Roots of t^2 - 10t + 16 = (t-8)(t-2) = 0 are 8 and 2.

mcqs.q: For positive distinct real numbers x and y, how do the G.M. and A.M. compare?
mcqs.why: Since x != y, (sqrt(x)-sqrt(y))^2 > 0 gives x + y > 2 sqrt(xy), i.e. (x+y)/2 > sqrt(xy). So G.M. sqrt(xy) is less than A.M. (x+y)/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.8
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-3

1. Find the sum of first 15 terms of the geometric sequence 1, 1/3, 1/9, ... 2. Sum to

n terms the series i) .2 + .22 + .222 + ... ii) 3 + 33 + 333 + ... 3. Sum to n terms

the series i) 1 + (a + b) + (a^2 + ab + b^2) + (a^3 + a^2 b + ab^2 + b^3) + ...

ii) r + (1 + k) r^2 + (1 + k + k^2) r^3 + ...

1.
Here a = 1 and r = 1/3, so S_15 = (1 - (1/3)^15)/(1 - 1/3) = (3/2)(1 - 1/14348907)

= 7174453/4782969.
2. i) Each term is 2 x (1 - 10^(-k))/9, so the sum is (2/9)[n -

(1/9)(1 - 1/10^n)].
FLAG: the printed key's factor here appears to read 1/n, but the

correct factor is 1/9 (from the geometric sum (1/10 + 1/100 + ... + 1/10^n) =

(1/9)(1 - 1/10^n)). ii) Each term is 3 x (10^k - 1)/9, so the sum is (1/3)[(10/9)(10^n

- 1) - n].
3. i) The kth term (k = 0, 1, ...) is (a^(k+1) - b^(k+1))/(a - b), so the sum to

n terms is [a(a^n - 1)/(a - 1) - b(b^n - 1)/(b - 1)]/(a - b) = [a(b - 1)(a^n - 1) - (a -

1)b(b^n - 1)]/[(a - b)(a - 1)(b - 1)]. ii) The kth term is (1 - k^k)/(1 - k) x r^k, so the

sum is (1/(1 - k))[r(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) - kr(1 - (kr)^n)/(1 - kr)] = (r/(1 - k))[(1 - r^n)/(1 - r)

- k(1 - k^n r^n)/(1 - kr)].

Q4-6

4. Sum the series 2 + (1 - i) + (1/i) + ... to 8 terms. 5. Find the sums of the following

infinite geometric series: i) 1/5 + 1/25 + 1/125 + ... ii) 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... iii) 9/4 +

3/2 + 1 + 2/3 + ... iv) 2 + 1 + 0.5 + ... v) 4 + 2 sqrt(2) + 2 + sqrt(2) + 1 + ... vi) 0.1

+ 0.05 + 0.025 + ... 6. Find vulgar fractions equivalent to the following recurring

decimals: i) 1.3434... ii) 0.777... iii) 0.259259... iv) 1.5353... v) 0.159159... vi)

1.1474747...

4.
Here r = (1 - i)/2 (check: (1/i)/(1 - i) = -i/(1 - i) = (1 - i)/2).
Since r^2 = -i/2, r^4 =

-1/4 and r^8 = 1/16, S_8 = 2(1 - r^8)/(1 - r) = 2(15/16)/((1 + i)/2) = 15(1 - i)/8. 5. i)

S = (1/5)/(1 - 1/5) = 1/4. ii) S = (1/2)/(1 - 1/2) = 1. iii) Here a = 9/4 and r = 2/3, so S

= (9/4)/(1/3) = 27/4. iv) S = 2/(1 - 1/2) = 4. v) Here a = 4 and r = sqrt(2)/2, so S =

4/(1 - sqrt(2)/2) = 8/(2 - sqrt(2)) = 4(2 + sqrt(2)). vi) S = 0.1/(1 - 1/2) = 0.2. 6. i)

1.3434... = 1 + 34/99 = 133/99. ii) 0.777... = 7/9. iii) 0.259259... = 259/999. iv)

1.5353... = 1 + 53/99 = 152/99. v) 0.159159... = 159/999. vi) 1.1474747... = 1 +

(147 - 1)/990 = 1136/990.

Q7-9

7. Find the sum to infinity of the series: r + (1 + k) r^2 + (1 + k + k^2) r^3 + ...; r

and k being proper fractions. 8. If y = x/2 + (1/4) x^2 + (1/8) x^3 + ... and if 0 < x

< 2, then prove that x = 2y/(1 + y) 9. If y = (2/3) x + (4/9) x^2 + (8/27) x^3 + ...

and if 0 < x < 3/2, then show that x = 3y/(2(1 + y))

7.
The kth term is (1 - k^k)/(1 - k) x r^k, so the sum to infinity is (1/(1 - k))[r/(1 - r) -

kr/(1 - kr)] = r/((1 - r)(1 - kr)), since the bracket simplifies to (1 - k)/((1 - r)(1 - kr)). 8.

The series is a G.P. with a = x/2 and r = x/2, so y = (x/2)/(1 - x/2) = x/(2 - x). Then

y(2 - x) = x, i.e.
2y = x(1 + y), so x = 2y/(1 + y), as required. 9.
The series is a G.P.

with a = (2/3)x and r = (2/3)x, so y = ((2/3)x)/(1 - (2/3)x) = 2x/(3 - 2x). Then y(3 -

2x) = 2x, i.e.
3y = 2x(1 + y), so x = 3y/(2(1 + y)), as required.

Q10-14

10. A ball is dropped from a height of 27 meters and it rebounds two-third of the

distance it falls. If it continues to fall in the same way what distance will it travel

before coming to rest? 11. What distance will a ball travel before coming to rest if it

is dropped from a height of 75 meters and after each fall it rebounds 2/5 of the

distance it fell? 12. If y = 1 + 2x + 4x^2 + 8x^3 + ... i) Show that x = (y - 1)/(2y) ii)

Find the interval in which the series is convergent. 13. If y = 1 + x/2 + x^2/4 + ... i)

Show that x = 2((y - 1)/y) ii) Find the interval in which the series is convergent. 14.

The sum of an infinite geometric series is 9 and the sum of the squares of its terms

is 81/5. Find the series.

10.
The ball falls 27 m, then rebounds 18 m and falls 18 m, then rebounds 12 m and

falls 12 m, and so on.
Total distance = 27 + 2(18 + 12 + 8 + ...) = 27 + 2 x 18/(1 -

2/3) = 27 + 108 = 135 meters. 11.
Total distance = 75 + 2(30 + 12 + ...) = 75 + 2

x 30/(1 - 2/5) = 75 + 100 = 175 meters.
12. i) The series is a G.P. with a = 1 and r =

2x, so y = 1/(1 - 2x).
Then 1 - 2x = 1/y, so x = (y - 1)/(2y). ii) The series converges

when |2x| < 1, i.e. -1/2 < x < 1/2.
13. i) The series is a G.P. with a = 1 and r = x/2,

so y = 1/(1 - x/2) = 2/(2 - x).
Then 2 - x = 2/y, so x = 2(y - 1)/y. ii) The series

converges when |x/2| < 1, i.e. -2 < x < 2. 14.
Let the series be a, ar, ar^2, ...: a/(1 -
