mcqs.why: (1 - x)^(1/2) = 1 - x/2 - x^2/8 - x^3/16 + ..., valid for |x| < 1, so the coefficient of x^2 is -1/8.

mcqs.q: In the expansion of (1 + 2x)^(-1) up to 4 terms, what is the coefficient of x^2 ?
mcqs.why: (1 + 2x)^(-1) = 1 - 2x + 4x^2 - 8x^3 + ..., valid for |x| < 1/2, so the coefficient of x^2 is 4.

mcqs.q: Using the binomial theorem, sqrt(99) to three places of decimals is approximately what?
mcqs.why: sqrt(99) = 10(1 - 0.01)^(1/2) is approximately 10(1 - 0.005 - 0.0000125) = 10 x 0.9949875 = 9.949875, which is 9.950 to three decimal places.

mcqs.q: Using the binomial theorem, (65)^(1/3) to three places of decimals is approximately what?
mcqs.why: (65)^(1/3) = 4(1 + 1/64)^(1/3) is approximately 4(1 + 1/192) = 4 x 1.005208 = 4.0208, which is 4.021 to three decimal places.

mcqs.q: Using the binomial theorem, sqrt(7)/sqrt(8) to three places of decimals is approximately what?
mcqs.why: sqrt(7)/sqrt(8) = (1 - 1/8)^(1/2) is approximately 1 - 1/16 - 1/512 = 1 - 0.0625 - 0.001953 = 0.935547, about 0.935 to three decimal places (the notes give 0.935).

mcqs.q: For n >= 1, the coefficient of x^n in the expansion of (1 + x)^2 / (1 - x)^2 is which expression?
mcqs.why: (1 - x)^(-2) = sum (r + 1)x^r. Multiplying by (1 + 2x + x^2), the coefficient of x^n is (n + 1) + 2n + (n - 1) = 4n for n >= 1, as derived in the notes.

mcqs.q: If x is so small that its square and higher powers can be neglected, (1 - x)/sqrt(1 + x) is approximately equal to which expression?
mcqs.why: (1 - x)(1 + x)^(-1/2) is approximately (1 - x)(1 - x/2) = 1 - (3/2)x + x^2/2, and neglecting x^2 and higher powers leaves 1 - (3/2)x.
This is (1 + x)^(-1/2) with x = 1/4, so the sum is (1 + 1/4)^(-1/2) = (5/4)^(-1/2) = 2/sqrt(5), as identified in the notes.
This is (1 - x)^(-1/2) with x = 1/2 substituted, so the sum is (1 - 1/2)^(-1/2) = (1/2)^(-1/2) = sqrt(2), as shown in the notes.
The r-th term equals C(2r,r)(1/6)^r, so y = (1 - 4/6)^(-1/2) - 1 = (1/3)^(-1/2) - 1 = sqrt(3) - 1, which is why y satisfies y^2 + 2y - 2 = 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Express the following sexagesimal measures of angles in radians: i) 30 deg ii) 45

deg iii) 60 deg iv) 75 deg v) 90 deg vi) 105 deg vii) 120 deg viii) 135 deg ix) 150

deg x) 10 deg 15' xi) 35 deg 20' xii) 75 deg 6' 30'' xiii) 120' 40'' xiv) 154 deg 20'' xv)

0 deg xvi) 3''

Multiply by pi/180. i) 30 pi/180 = pi/6. ii) 45 pi/180 = pi/4. iii) 60 pi/180 = pi/3. iv) 75

pi/180 = 5pi/12. v) 90 pi/180 = pi/2. vi) 105 pi/180 = 7pi/12. vii) 120 pi/180 = 2pi/3.

viii) 135 pi/180 = 3pi/4. ix) 150 pi/180 = 5pi/6. x) 10 deg 15' = 10.25 deg = (41/4)

pi/180 = 41pi/720. xi) 35 deg 20' = (106/3) deg, giving (106/3) pi/180 = 53pi/270.

xii) 75 deg 6' 30'' = (9013/120) deg, giving 9013pi/21600. xiii) 120' 40'' = (181/90)

deg, giving 181pi/16200.
FLAG: the printed key appears to read 181pi/15200 for this

part, but (181/90) x (pi/180) = 181pi/16200, so 15200 is arithmetically impossible

and is treated as a misprint (or a scan misread of 16200). xiv) 154 deg 20'' =

(138605/900) deg, giving 27721pi/32400. xv) 0 deg = 0. xvi) 3'' = (1/1200) deg,

giving pi/216000.

Q2

2. Convert the following radian measures of angles into the measures of

sexagesimal system: i) pi/8 ii) pi/6 iii) pi/4 iv) pi/3 v) pi/2 vi) 2pi/3 vii) 3pi/4 viii) 5pi/6

ix) 7pi/12 x) 9pi/5 xi) 11pi/27 xii) 13pi/16 xiii) 17pi/24 xiv) 25pi/36 xv) 19pi/32

Multiply by 180/pi. i) (pi/8)(180/pi) = 22.5 deg = 22 deg 30'. ii) 30 deg. iii) 45 deg.

iv) 60 deg. v) 90 deg. vi) 120 deg. vii) 135 deg. viii) 150 deg. ix) 105 deg. x) 324

deg. xi) (11pi/27)(180/pi) = 220/3 deg = 73 deg 20'. xii) (13pi/16)(180/pi) = 585/4

deg = 146 deg 15'. xiii) (17pi/24)(180/pi) = 127.5 deg = 127 deg 30'. FLAG: the

printed key reads 127 deg 37' 59'' for this part, but 17 x 180/24 = 127.5 exactly, so

127 deg 30' is the correct value and the key's figure is flagged. xiv) 125 deg. xv)

(19pi/32)(180/pi) = 106.875 deg = 106 deg 52' 30''.

Q3

3. What is the circular measure of the angle between the hands of a watch at 4

O'clock?

At 4 O'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 4, i.e. 4

hour-divisions apart. Each hour-division is 30 deg, so the angle is 4 x 30 deg = 120

deg = 120 pi/180 = 2pi/3 radians. Answer: 2pi/3.

Q4

4. Find theta, when: i) l = 1.5 cm, r = 2.5 cm ii) l = 3.2 m, r = 2 m

Use theta = l/r. i) theta = 1.5/2.5 = 0.6 rad. ii) theta = 3.2/2 = 1.6 rad. Answers: i)

0.6 rad ii) 1.6 rad.

Q5-8

5. Find l, when: i) theta = pi radians, r = 6 cm ii) theta = 65 deg 20', r = 18 mm

Use l = r theta. i) l = 6 x pi = 6pi = 18.85 cm (the printed key reads 18.86 cm, a

0.01 rounding difference; 6 x 3.1416 = 18.8496). ii) 65 deg 20' = (196/3) deg =

49pi/135 = 1.1404 rad, so l = 18 x 1.1404 = 20.5 mm. Answers: i) 18.85 cm ii) 20.5

mm.

6. Find r, when: i) l = 5 cm, theta = 1/2 radian ii) l = 56 cm, theta = 45 deg

Use r = l/theta. i) r = 5/(1/2) = 10 cm. ii) 45 deg = pi/4 rad, so r = 56/(pi/4) = 224/pi

= 71.3 cm. Answers: i) 10 cm ii) 71.3 cm.

7. What is the length of the arc intercepted on a circle of radius 14 cms by the arms

of a central angle of 45 deg?

45 deg = pi/4 rad, so l = r theta = 14 x pi/4 = 3.5pi = 10.99 cm. Answer: 10.99 cm.

8. Find the radius of the circle, in which the arms of a central angle of measure 1

radian cut off an arc of length 35 cm.

r = l/theta = 35/1 = 35 cm. Answer: 35 cm.

Q9-10

9. A railway train is running on a circular track of radius 500 meters at the rate of 30

km per hour. Through what angle will it turn in 10 sec.?

Speed = 30 km/h = 30000/3600 = 8.333 m/s. Distance covered in 10 s = 8.333 x

10 = 83.33 m. Hence theta = l/r = 83.33/500 = 1/6 rad. Answer: 1/6 rad.

10. A horse is tethered to a peg by a rope of 9 meters length and it can move in a

circle with the peg as centre. If the horse moves along the circumference of the

circle, keeping the rope tight, how far will it have gone when the rope has turned

through an angle of 70 deg?

70 deg = 7pi/18 rad, so the distance = r theta = 9 x 7pi/18 = 3.5pi = 10.9966 m.

Answer: 10.9966 m.

Q11-13

11. The pendulum of a clock is 20 cm long and it swings through an angle of 20 deg

each second. How far does the tip of the pendulum move in 1 second?

20 deg = pi/9 rad, so the tip moves l = r theta = 20 x pi/9 = 6.983 cm. Answer:

6.983 cm.

12. Assuming the average distance of the earth from the sun to be 148 x 10^6 km

and the angle subtended by the sun at the eye of a person on the earth of measure

9.3 x 10^(-3) radian. Find the diameter of the sun.

Diameter = distance x angle = 148 x 10^6 x 9.3 x 10^(-3) = 148 x 9.3 x 10^3 =

1376400 km. Answer: 1376400 km. FLAG: the printed key reads 1390000 km, which

would require an angle of about 9.4 x 10^(-3) rad (or a distance of about 149.5 x

10^6 km); from the printed givens the product is 1376400 km, and the key's figure

is flagged.

13. A circular wire of radius 6 cm is cut straightened and then bent so as to lie along

the circumference of a hoop of radius 24 cm. Find the measure of the angle which it

subtends at the centre of the hoop.

The wire's length is its circumference = 2pi x 6 = 12pi cm.
On the hoop of radius 24

cm it subtends theta = l/r = 12pi/24 = pi/2 rad. Answer: pi/2 rad.

Q14

14. Show that the area of a sector of a circular region of radius r is (1/2) r^2 theta,

where theta is the circular measure of the central angle of the sector.

The area of the whole circle is pi r^2, corresponding to the central angle 2pi. The

sector's area is the same fraction of the whole area as its angle is of 2pi: area =

(theta/(2pi)) x pi r^2 = (1/2) r^2 theta, as required.

Q15

15. Two cities A and B lie on the equator such that their longitudes are 45 deg E and

25 deg W respectively. Find the distance between the two cities, taking radius of the

earth as 6400 kms.

The angular separation is 45 deg + 25 deg = 70 deg = 7pi/18 rad. Hence the

distance along the equator = r theta = 6400 x 7pi/18 = 6400 x 1.2217 = 7819 km.

Answer: 7819 km.

Q16-17

16. The moon subtends an angle of 0.5 deg at the eye of an observer on earth. The

distance of the moon from the earth is 3.844 x 10^5 km approx. What is the length

of the diameter of the moon?

0.5 deg = pi/360 = 0.008727 rad. Hence the diameter = distance x angle = 3.844 x

10^5 x 0.008727 = 3354.53 km. Answer: 3354.53 km.

17. The angle subtended by the earth at the eye of a spaceman, landed on the

moon, is 1 deg 54'. The radius of the earth is 6400 km. Find the approximate

distance between the moon and the earth.

The angle subtended by the earth's diameter is 1 deg 54' = 1.9 deg = 0.03316 rad.

Hence the distance = diameter/angle = 12800/0.03316 = 386007 km approx.

(Equivalently, using the radius and the half-angle: 6400/tan 0 deg 57' = 386007

km.) Answer: 386007 km approx.

mcqs.q: Express 75 deg in radians.
mcqs.why: Multiply by pi/180: 75 x pi/180 = 75pi/180, and dividing numerator and denominator by 15 gives 5pi/12.

mcqs.q: Express 120' 40'' in radians, using the corrected value given in the notes.
Convert pi/8 radians into the sexagesimal system.
mcqs.why: Multiply by 180/pi: (pi/8) x (180/pi) = 180/8 = 22.5 deg, and 0.5 deg = 30', so the measure is 22 deg 30'.

mcqs.q: Convert 17pi/24 radians into degrees, using the corrected value given in the notes.
mcqs.why: Multiply by 180/pi: (17pi/24) x (180/pi) = 17 x 180/24 = 127.5 deg = 127 deg 30'. The printed key figure 127 deg 37' 59'' is wrong because 127.5 is exact.

mcqs.q: What is the circular measure of the angle between the hands of a watch at 4 O'clock?
mcqs.why: The hands are 4 hour-divisions apart and each division is 30 deg, so the angle is 4 x 30 deg = 120 deg = 120 x pi/180 = 2pi/3 radians.

mcqs.q: Find theta when l = 1.5 cm and r = 2.5 cm.
mcqs.why: Use theta = l/r. Substituting, theta = 1.5/2.5 = 15/25 = 0.6, so theta = 0.6 rad.

mcqs.q: Find l when theta = pi radians and r = 6 cm.
mcqs.why: Use l = r theta. Substituting, l = 6 x pi = 6pi = 6 x 3.1416 = 18.8496 cm, which rounds to 18.85 cm.

mcqs.q: Find r when l = 56 cm and theta = 45 deg.
mcqs.why: 45 deg = pi/4 rad, and r = l/theta = 56/(pi/4) = 224/pi = 224/3.1416 = 71.3 cm approximately.

mcqs.q: The distance of the earth from the sun is 148 x 10^6 km and the sun subtends 9.3 x 10^(-3) radian at the eye. Find the diameter of the sun, using the value computed in the notes.
mcqs.why: Diameter = distance x angle = 148 x 10^6 x 9.3 x 10^(-3) = 148 x 9.3 x 10^3 = 1376400 km. The printed key 1390000 km does not follow from these givens and is flagged in the notes.

mcqs.q: The moon subtends 0.5 deg at the eye and its distance from the earth is 3.844 x 10^5 km. Find the diameter of the moon.
mcqs.why: 0.5 deg = pi/360 = 0.008727 rad, so diameter = distance x angle = 3.844 x 10^5 x 0.008727 = 3354.53 km.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Find the signs of the following: i) sin 160 deg ii) cos 190 deg iii) tan 115 deg iv)

sec 245 deg v) cot 80 deg vi) cosec 297 deg

i) 160 deg lies in quadrant II, where sine is positive: +ve. ii) 190 deg lies in quadrant

III, where cosine is negative: -ve. iii) 115 deg lies in quadrant II, where tangent is

negative: -ve. iv) 245 deg lies in quadrant III, where secant (1/cos) is negative: -ve.

v) 80 deg lies in quadrant I, where all ratios are positive: +ve. vi) 297 deg lies in

quadrant IV, where cosecant (1/sin) is negative: -ve.
Answers: i) +ve ii) -ve iii) -ve iv)

-ve v) +ve vi) -ve.

Q2

2. Fill in the blanks: i) sin(-310 deg) = ... sin 310 deg ii) cos(-75 deg) = ... cos 75 deg

iii) tan(-182 deg) = ... tan 182 deg iv) cot(-173 deg) = ... cot 173 deg v) sec(-216

deg) = ... sec 216 deg vi) cosec(-15 deg) = ... cosec 15 deg

Sine, tangent, cotangent and cosecant are odd functions (f(-x) = -f(x)); cosine and

secant are even (f(-x) = f(x)).
Hence: i) sin(-310 deg) = - sin 310 deg. ii) cos(-75

deg) = + cos 75 deg. iii) tan(-182 deg) = - tan 182 deg. iv) cot(-173 deg) = - cot

173 deg. v) sec(-216 deg) = + sec 216 deg. vi) cosec(-15 deg) = - cosec 15 deg.

Answers: i) - ii) + iii) - iv) - v) + vi) -.

Q3

3. In which quadrant are the terminal arms of the angle lie when i) sin theta < 0 and

cos theta > 0 ii) cot theta > 0 and cosec theta > 0 iii) tan theta < 0 and cos theta >

0 iv) sec theta < 0 and sin theta < 0 v) cot theta > 0 and sin theta < 0 vi) cos theta

< 0 and tan theta < 0?

i) sin < 0 in III, IV; cos > 0 in I, IV: common quadrant IV. ii) cot > 0 in I, III; cosec > 0

in I, II: common quadrant I. iii) tan < 0 in II, IV; cos > 0 in I, IV: common quadrant IV.

iv) sec < 0 in II, III; sin < 0 in III, IV: common quadrant III. v) cot > 0 in I, III; sin < 0

in III, IV: common quadrant III. vi) cos < 0 in II, III; tan < 0 in II, IV: common quadrant

II. Answers: i) IV ii) I iii) IV iv) III v) III vi) II.

Q4

4. Find the values of the remaining trigonometric functions: i) sin theta = 12/13 and

the terminal arm of the angle is in quad. I ii) cos theta = 9/41 and the terminal arm

of the angle is in quad. IV iii) cos theta = -sqrt(3)/2 and the terminal arm of the

angle is in quad. III iv) tan theta = -1/3 and the terminal arm of the angle is in quad.

II v) sin theta = -1/sqrt(2) and the terminal arm of the angle is not in quad. III

i) In quad.
I all ratios are positive. cos theta = sqrt(1 - (12/13)^2) = 5/13. tan theta

= (12/13)/(5/13) = 12/5. cosec theta = 13/12. sec theta = 13/5. cot theta = 5/12. ii)

In quad.
IV cosine is positive and sine negative. sin theta = -sqrt(1 - (9/41)^2) =

-40/41. tan theta = (-40/41)/(9/41) = -40/9. cosec theta = -41/40. sec theta = 41/9.

cot theta = -9/40. iii) In quad.
III sine and cosine are negative, tangent positive. sin

theta = -sqrt(1 - 3/4) = -1/2. tan theta = (-1/2)/(-sqrt(3)/2) = 1/sqrt(3). cosec theta

= -2. sec theta = -2/sqrt(3). cot theta = sqrt(3). iv) In quad.
II sine is positive and

cosine negative.
From tan theta = -1/3, take opposite 1, adjacent -3, hypotenuse

sqrt(10): sin theta = 1/sqrt(10), cos theta = -3/sqrt(10). cosec theta = sqrt(10). sec

theta = -sqrt(10)/3. cot theta = -3. v) sin theta negative means quad. III or IV; not

III, so quad.
IV. cos theta = sqrt(1 - 1/2) = 1/sqrt(2). tan theta =

(-1/sqrt(2))/(1/sqrt(2)) = -1. cosec theta = -sqrt(2). sec theta = sqrt(2). cot theta =

-1.

Q5-7

5. If cot theta = 15/8 and the terminal arm of the angle is not in quad. I, find the

values of cos theta and cosec theta.

Cotangent is positive in quads. I and III; not I, so the terminal arm is in quad. III,

where sine and cosine are negative. From cot theta = 15/8, take adjacent 15,

opposite 8, hypotenuse 17: cos theta = -15/17 and sin theta = -8/17, so cosec theta

= -17/8. Answers: cos theta = -15/17, cosec theta = -17/8.

6. If cosec theta = (m^2 + 1)/(2m) and m > 0 (0 < theta < pi/2), find the values of

the remaining trigonometric ratios.

sin theta = 1/cosec theta = 2m/(m^2 + 1). Then cos theta = sqrt(1 - sin^2 theta) =

sqrt(((m^2 + 1)^2 - 4m^2)/(m^2 + 1)^2) = (m^2 - 1)/(m^2 + 1), taking the

positive root since theta is in quad. I. Hence tan theta = sin theta/cos theta =

2m/(m^2 - 1) and cot theta = (m^2 - 1)/(2m). Answers: sin theta = 2m/(1 + m^2),

cos theta = (m^2 - 1)/(m^2 + 1), tan theta = 2m/(m^2 - 1), cot theta = (m^2 -

1)/(2m). Note: the cosine and tangent forms as printed in the key assume m > 1, so

that (m^2 - 1) is positive as required in quad. I; for 0 < m < 1 the quad. I cosine

would be (1 - m^2)/(m^2 + 1).

7. If tan theta = 1/sqrt(7) and the terminal arm of the angle is not in the III quad.,

find the values of (cosec^2 theta - sec^2 theta)/(cosec^2 theta + sec^2 theta).

Tangent is positive in quads. I and III; not III, so the terminal arm is in quad. I. From

tan theta = 1/sqrt(7), take opposite 1, adjacent sqrt(7), hypotenuse sqrt(8): sin

theta = 1/sqrt(8), cos theta = sqrt(7)/sqrt(8).
Hence cosec^2 theta = 8 and sec^2

theta = 8/7.
The required value = (8 - 8/7)/(8 + 8/7) = (48/7)/(64/7) = 48/64 = 3/4.

Answer: 3/4.

Q8

8. If cot theta = 5/2 and the terminal arm of the angle is in the I quad., find the

value of (3 sin theta + 4 cos theta)/(cos theta - sin theta).

In quad.
I, from cot theta = 5/2, take adjacent 5, opposite 2, hypotenuse sqrt(29):

sin theta = 2/sqrt(29), cos theta = 5/sqrt(29).
Hence (3 sin theta + 4 cos theta)/(cos

theta - sin theta) = (6/sqrt(29) + 20/sqrt(29))/(5/sqrt(29) - 2/sqrt(29)) = 26/3.

Answer: 26/3.
Note: the printed key labels this value '9.'; the exercise as printed on

book pp. 301-302 ends at Question 8, so the key's numbering is treated as a

misnumbering of Question 8.

mcqs.q: Find the sign of sin 160 deg.
mcqs.why: 160 deg lies in quadrant II, and sine is positive in quadrant II, so sin 160 deg has the +ve sign.

mcqs.q: Find the sign of sec 245 deg.
mcqs.why: 245 deg lies in quadrant III, where cosine is negative. Since sec is 1/cos, sec 245 deg is also negative, so its sign is -ve.

mcqs.q: cos(-75 deg) is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Cosine is an even function, so f(-x) = f(x). Hence cos(-75 deg) = +cos 75 deg, with no change of sign.

mcqs.q: cot(-173 deg) is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Cotangent is an odd function, so f(-x) = -f(x). Hence cot(-173 deg) = -cot 173 deg.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the terminal arm lie when sin theta < 0 and cos theta > 0?
mcqs.why: Sin theta < 0 in quadrants III and IV, and cos theta > 0 in quadrants I and IV. The common quadrant is IV.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the terminal arm lie when sec theta < 0 and sin theta < 0?
mcqs.why: Sec theta < 0 in quadrants II and III, and sin theta < 0 in quadrants III and IV. The common quadrant is III.

mcqs.q: If sin theta = 12/13 and the terminal arm is in quadrant I, find cos theta.
mcqs.why: cos theta = sqrt(1 - sin^2 theta) = sqrt(1 - (12/13)^2) = sqrt(1 - 144/169) = sqrt(25/169) = 5/13, positive in quadrant I.

mcqs.q: If cos theta = 9/41 and the terminal arm is in quadrant IV, find sin theta.
mcqs.why: sin theta = -sqrt(1 - cos^2 theta) = -sqrt(1 - (9/41)^2) = -sqrt(1 - 81/1681) = -sqrt(1600/1681) = -40/41, negative in quadrant IV.

mcqs.q: If cot theta = 15/8 and the terminal arm is not in quadrant I, find cosec theta.
mcqs.why: Cotangent is positive in quadrants I and III, so the arm is in quadrant III. With adjacent 15, opposite 8, hypotenuse sqrt(15^2 + 8^2) = 17, sin theta = -8/17, hence cosec theta = -17/8.

mcqs.q: If tan theta = 1/sqrt(7) and the terminal arm is not in quadrant III, find (cosec^2 theta - sec^2 theta)/(cosec^2 theta + sec^2 theta).
mcqs.why: The arm is in quadrant I. With opposite 1, adjacent sqrt(7), hypotenuse sqrt(8): cosec^2 theta = 8 and sec^2 theta = 8/7. The value is (8 - 8/7)/(8 + 8/7) = (48/7)/(64/7) = 48/64 = 3/4.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Verify the following: i) sin 60 deg cos 30 deg - cos 60 deg sin 30 deg = sin 30 deg

ii) sin^2 pi/6 + sin^2 pi/3 + tan^2 pi/4 = 2 iii) 2 sin 45 deg + (1/2) cosec 45 deg =

3/sqrt(2) iv) sin^2 pi/6 : sin^2 pi/4 : sin^2 pi/3 : sin^2 pi/2 = 1 : 2 : 3 : 4

i) L.H.S. = (sqrt(3)/2)(sqrt(3)/2) - (1/2)(1/2) = 3/4 - 1/4 = 1/2 = sin 30 deg. ii) L.H.S.

= (1/2)^2 + (sqrt(3)/2)^2 + 1^2 = 1/4 + 3/4 + 1 = 2. iii) L.H.S. = 2(1/sqrt(2)) +

(1/2)(sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2) + sqrt(2)/2 = 3sqrt(2)/2 = 3/sqrt(2). iv) The values are 1/4,

1/2, 3/4, 1; multiplying by 4 gives 1 : 2 : 3 : 4, as required.

Q2

2. Evaluate the following: i) (tan pi/3 - tan pi/6)/(1 + tan pi/3 tan pi/6) ii) (1 - tan^2

pi/3)/(1 + tan^2 pi/3)

i) This is tan(pi/3 - pi/6) = tan pi/6 = 1/sqrt(3).
Directly: (sqrt(3) - 1/sqrt(3))/(1 +

sqrt(3) x 1/sqrt(3)) = ((3 - 1)/sqrt(3))/2 = 1/sqrt(3). ii) tan pi/3 = sqrt(3), so the

value = (1 - 3)/(1 + 3) = -2/4 = -1/2.
Answers: i) 1/sqrt(3) ii) -1/2.

Q3

3. Verify the following when theta = 30 deg, 45 deg: i) sin 2theta = 2 sin theta cos

theta ii) cos 2theta = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta iii) cos 2theta = 2cos^2 theta - 1

iv) cos 2theta = 1 - 2sin^2 theta v) tan 2theta = 2tan theta/(1 - tan^2 theta)

For theta = 30 deg: i) sin 60 deg = sqrt(3)/2; 2 sin 30 deg cos 30 deg =

2(1/2)(sqrt(3)/2) = sqrt(3)/2. ii) cos 60 deg = 1/2; cos^2 30 deg - sin^2 30 deg =

3/4 - 1/4 = 1/2. iii) 2cos^2 30 deg - 1 = 2(3/4) - 1 = 1/2. iv) 1 - 2sin^2 30 deg = 1 -

2(1/4) = 1/2. v) tan 60 deg = sqrt(3); 2tan 30 deg/(1 - tan^2 30 deg) =

2(1/sqrt(3))/(1 - 1/3) = (2/sqrt(3))/(2/3) = sqrt(3).
For theta = 45 deg: i) sin 90 deg =

1; 2(1/sqrt(2))(1/sqrt(2)) = 1. ii) cos 90 deg = 0; 1/2 - 1/2 = 0. iii) 2(1/2) - 1 = 0. iv)

1 - 2(1/2) = 0. v) tan 90 deg is undefined, and 2tan 45 deg/(1 - tan^2 45 deg) =

2/(1 - 1) is likewise undefined, so both sides are undefined together. All five

identities are verified for both angles.

Q4-5

4. Find x, if tan^2 45 deg - cos^2 60 deg = x sin 45 deg cos 45 deg tan 60 deg.

L.H.S. = 1^2 - (1/2)^2 = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4. R.H.S. = x (1/sqrt(2))(1/sqrt(2))(sqrt(3)) = x

sqrt(3)/2. Hence x = (3/4)/(sqrt(3)/2) = 3/(2sqrt(3)) = sqrt(3)/2. Answer: x =

sqrt(3)/2.

5. Find the values of the trigonometric functions of the following quadrantal angles:

i) -pi ii) -3pi iii) 5pi/2 iv) -9pi/2 v) -15pi vi) 1530 deg vii) -2430 deg viii) 235pi/2 ix)

407pi/2

Reduce each angle to its coterminal angle in [0, 2pi), then read the functions. i) -pi

is coterminal with pi: sin = 0, cos = -1, tan = 0, cosec undefined, sec = -1, cot

undefined. ii) -3pi is coterminal with pi: same values as (i). iii) 5pi/2 is coterminal

with pi/2: sin = 1, cos = 0, tan undefined, cosec = 1, sec undefined, cot = 0. iv)

-9pi/2 is coterminal with 3pi/2: sin = -1, cos = 0, tan undefined, cosec = -1, sec

undefined, cot = 0. v) -15pi is coterminal with pi: same values as (i). vi) 1530 deg =

1440 deg + 90 deg, coterminal with 90 deg = pi/2: same values as (iii). vii) -2430

deg = -2520 deg + 90 deg, coterminal with 90 deg: same values as (iii). viii)

235pi/2 = 116pi + 3pi/2, coterminal with 3pi/2: same values as (iv). ix) 407pi/2 =

202pi + 3pi/2, coterminal with 3pi/2: same values as (iv).
Reduced angles (as given

in the key): i) pi ii) pi iii) pi/2 iv) 3pi/2 v) pi vi) 90 deg vii) 90 deg viii) 3pi/2 ix) 3pi/2.

Q6

6. Find the values of the trigonometric functions of the following angles: i) 390 deg

ii) -330 deg iii) 765 deg iv) -675 deg v) -17pi/3 vi) 13pi/3 vii) 25pi/6 viii) -71pi/6 ix)

-1035 deg

Reduce each angle, then read the functions. i) 390 deg = 360 deg + 30 deg: sin =

1/2, cos = sqrt(3)/2, tan = 1/sqrt(3), cosec = 2, sec = 2/sqrt(3), cot = sqrt(3). ii)

-330 deg = -360 deg + 30 deg: same values as (i). iii) 765 deg = 720 deg + 45 deg:

sin = 1/sqrt(2), cos = 1/sqrt(2), tan = 1, cosec = sqrt(2), sec = sqrt(2), cot = 1. iv)

-675 deg = -720 deg + 45 deg: same values as (iii). v) -17pi/3 = -6pi + pi/3: sin =

sqrt(3)/2, cos = 1/2, tan = sqrt(3), cosec = 2/sqrt(3), sec = 2, cot = 1/sqrt(3). vi)

13pi/3 = 4pi + pi/3: same values as (v). vii) 25pi/6 = 4pi + pi/6: sin = 1/2, cos =

sqrt(3)/2, tan = 1/sqrt(3), cosec = 2, sec = 2/sqrt(3), cot = sqrt(3). viii) -71pi/6 =

-12pi + pi/6: same values as (vii). ix) -1035 deg = -1080 deg + 45 deg: same values

as (iii).
Reduced angles (as given in the key): i) 30 deg ii) 30 deg iii) 45 deg iv) 45

deg v) pi/3 vi) pi/3 vii) pi/6 viii) pi/6 ix) 45 deg.

mcqs.q: Evaluate sin^2 pi/6 + sin^2 pi/3 + tan^2 pi/4.
mcqs.why: sin pi/6 = 1/2, sin pi/3 = sqrt(3)/2 and tan pi/4 = 1, so the sum is (1/2)^2 + (sqrt(3)/2)^2 + 1^2 = 1/4 + 3/4 + 1 = 2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (tan pi/3 - tan pi/6)/(1 + tan pi/3 tan pi/6).
mcqs.why: This is tan(pi/3 - pi/6) = tan pi/6 = 1/sqrt(3). Directly, (sqrt(3) - 1/sqrt(3))/(1 + sqrt(3) x 1/sqrt(3)) = ((3 - 1)/sqrt(3))/2 = 1/sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: Evaluate (1 - tan^2 pi/3)/(1 + tan^2 pi/3).
mcqs.why: tan pi/3 = sqrt(3), so tan^2 pi/3 = 3. The value is (1 - 3)/(1 + 3) = -2/4 = -1/2.

mcqs.q: Find x if tan^2 45 deg - cos^2 60 deg = x sin 45 deg cos 45 deg tan 60 deg.
Find sin(-9pi/2).
mcqs.why: -9pi/2 is coterminal with 3pi/2, since -9pi/2 + 6pi = 3pi/2. The sine of 3pi/2 is -1, so sin(-9pi/2) = -1.

mcqs.q: Find sin 1530 deg.
mcqs.why: 1530 deg = 1440 deg + 90 deg, so 1530 deg is coterminal with 90 deg. Hence sin 1530 deg = sin 90 deg = 1.

mcqs.q: Find cos(-2430 deg).
mcqs.why: -2430 deg = -2520 deg + 90 deg, so -2430 deg is coterminal with 90 deg. Hence cos(-2430 deg) = cos 90 deg = 0.

mcqs.q: Find tan 390 deg.
mcqs.why: 390 deg = 360 deg + 30 deg, so tan 390 deg = tan 30 deg = 1/sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: Find cosec 765 deg.
mcqs.why: 765 deg = 720 deg + 45 deg, so cosec 765 deg = cosec 45 deg = 1/sin 45 deg = 1/(1/sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: Find sec(-17pi/3).
mcqs.why: -17pi/3 = -6pi + pi/3, so the angle is coterminal with pi/3. cos pi/3 = 1/2, hence sec(-17pi/3) = 1/(1/2) = 2.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-11

Prove the following identities, state the domain of theta in each case: 1. tan theta +

cot theta = cosec theta sec theta 2. sec theta cosec theta sin theta cos theta = 1 3.

cos theta + tan theta sin theta = sec theta 4. cosec theta + tan theta sec theta =

cosec theta sec^2 theta 5. sec^2 theta - cosec^2 theta = tan^2 theta - cot^2

theta 6. cot^2 theta - cos^2 theta = cot^2 theta cos^2 theta 7. (sec theta + tan

theta)(sec theta - tan theta) = 1 8. 2cos^2 theta - 1 = 1 - 2sin^2 theta 9. cos^2

theta - sin^2 theta = (1 - tan^2 theta)/(1 + tan^2 theta) 10. (cos theta - sin

theta)/(cos theta + sin theta) = (cot theta - 1)/(cot theta + 1) 11. sin theta/(1 + cos

theta) + cot theta = cosec theta

1.
L.H.S. = sin theta/cos theta + cos theta/sin theta = (sin^2 theta + cos^2

theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = 1/(sin theta cos theta) = cosec theta sec theta.

Domain: sin theta != 0 and cos theta != 0, i.e. theta is not a multiple of pi/2. 2.

L.H.S. = (1/cos theta)(1/sin theta) sin theta cos theta = 1.
Domain: theta is not a

multiple of pi/2. 3.
L.H.S. = cos theta + (sin theta/cos theta) sin theta = (cos^2

theta + sin^2 theta)/cos theta = 1/cos theta = sec theta.
Domain: cos theta != 0,

i.e. theta != (2n + 1)pi/2. 4.
L.H.S. = 1/sin theta + sin theta/cos^2 theta = (cos^2

theta + sin^2 theta)/(sin theta cos^2 theta) = 1/(sin theta cos^2 theta) = cosec

theta sec^2 theta.
Domain: sin theta != 0 and cos theta != 0. 5. L.H.S. = (1 +

tan^2 theta) - (1 + cot^2 theta) = tan^2 theta - cot^2 theta.
Domain: theta is not

a multiple of pi/2. 6.
L.H.S. = cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta - cos^2 theta = cos^2 theta

(1 - sin^2 theta)/sin^2 theta = cos^2 theta x cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta = cot^2

theta cos^2 theta.
Domain: sin theta != 0, i.e. theta != n pi. 7.
L.H.S. = sec^2 theta

- tan^2 theta = 1.
Domain: cos theta != 0. 8.
Both sides equal cos^2 theta - sin^2

theta: 2cos^2 theta - 1 = cos^2 theta - (1 - cos^2 theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2

theta, and 1 - 2sin^2 theta = (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta) - 2sin^2 theta = cos^2

theta - sin^2 theta.
Domain: all theta. 9.
R.H.S. = (1 - sin^2 theta/cos^2 theta)/(1 +

sin^2 theta/cos^2 theta) = (cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta)/(cos^2 theta + sin^2

theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta.
Domain: cos theta != 0. 10.
Dividing numerator

and denominator of the L.H.S. by sin theta gives (cot theta - 1)/(cot theta + 1).

Domain: sin theta != 0 and cos theta + sin theta != 0.
11. sin theta/(1 + cos theta)

= sin theta (1 - cos theta)/(1 - cos^2 theta) = sin theta (1 - cos theta)/sin^2 theta =

(1 - cos theta)/sin theta = cosec theta - cot theta.
Adding cot theta gives cosec

theta.
Domain: sin theta != 0.

Q12-24

12. (cot^2 theta - 1)/(1 + cot^2 theta) = 2cos^2 theta - 1 13. (1 + cos theta)/(1 -

cos theta) = (cosec theta + cot theta)^2 14. (sec theta - tan theta)^2 = (1 - sin

theta)/(1 + sin theta) 15. 2tan theta/(1 + tan^2 theta) = 2 sin theta cos theta 16. (1

- sin theta)/cos theta = cos theta/(1 + sin theta) 17. (tan theta + cot theta)^2 =

sec^2 theta cosec^2 theta 18. (tan theta + sec theta - 1)/(tan theta - sec theta +

1) = tan theta + sec theta 19. 1/(cosec theta - cot theta) - 1/sin theta = 1/sin theta -

1/(cosec theta + cot theta) 20. sin^3 theta - cos^3 theta = (sin theta - cos theta)(1

+ sin theta cos theta) 21. sin^6 theta - cos^6 theta = (sin^2 theta - cos^2 theta)(1

- sin^2 theta cos^2 theta) 22. sin^6 theta + cos^6 theta = 1 - 3sin^2 theta cos^2

theta 23. 1/(1 + sin theta) + 1/(1 - sin theta) = 2sec^2 theta 24. (cos theta + sin

theta)/(cos theta - sin theta) + (cos theta - sin theta)/(cos theta + sin theta) = 2/(1 -

2sin^2 theta)

12.
L.H.S. = (cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta - 1)/(1 + cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta) = (cos^2

theta - sin^2 theta)/(sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta =

2cos^2 theta - 1.
Domain: sin theta != 0. 13.
R.H.S. = (1/sin theta + cos theta/sin

theta)^2 = (1 + cos theta)^2/sin^2 theta = (1 + cos theta)^2/((1 - cos theta)(1 +

cos theta)) = (1 + cos theta)/(1 - cos theta).
Domain: sin theta != 0 and cos theta

!= 1.
14. sec theta - tan theta = (1 - sin theta)/cos theta, so its square is (1 - sin

theta)^2/cos^2 theta = (1 - sin theta)^2/((1 - sin theta)(1 + sin theta)) = (1 - sin

theta)/(1 + sin theta).
Domain: cos theta != 0 and sin theta != -1. 15. L.H.S. = 2(sin

theta/cos theta)/(1 + sin^2 theta/cos^2 theta) = 2 sin theta cos theta/(cos^2 theta

+ sin^2 theta) = 2 sin theta cos theta.
Domain: cos theta != 0. 16.

Cross-multiplying, (1 - sin theta)(1 + sin theta) = 1 - sin^2 theta = cos^2 theta,

which is the numerator of the R.H.S. times cos theta.
Domain: cos theta != 0 and sin

theta != -1. 17.
From Question 1, tan theta + cot theta = 1/(sin theta cos theta) =

sec theta cosec theta; squaring gives sec^2 theta cosec^2 theta. Domain: theta is

not a multiple of pi/2. 18.
Put t = tan theta + sec theta.
Then (tan theta + sec

theta)(tan theta - sec theta) = tan^2 theta - sec^2 theta = -1, so tan theta - sec

theta = -1/t.
Hence the denominator tan theta - sec theta + 1 = 1 - 1/t = (t - 1)/t,

and the numerator is t - 1, so the fraction equals t = tan theta + sec theta. Domain:

cos theta != 0 and tan theta - sec theta + 1 != 0. 19.
Note 1/(cosec theta - cot

theta) = sin theta/(1 - cos theta) = (1 + cos theta)/sin theta = cosec theta + cot

theta.
Hence L.H.S. = (cosec theta + cot theta) - cosec theta = cot theta. Also

1/(cosec theta + cot theta) = sin theta/(1 + cos theta) = (1 - cos theta)/sin theta =

cosec theta - cot theta, so R.H.S. = cosec theta - (cosec theta - cot theta) = cot

theta.
So both sides equal cot theta.
Domain: sin theta != 0. 20.
R.H.S. = (sin theta -

cos theta)(sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta + sin theta cos theta) = sin^3 theta - cos^3

theta by the difference-of-cubes formula a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2).

Domain: all theta.
21. sin^6 theta - cos^6 theta = (sin^2 theta)^3 - (cos^2

theta)^3 = (sin^2 theta - cos^2 theta)(sin^4 theta + sin^2 theta cos^2 theta +

cos^4 theta) = (sin^2 theta - cos^2 theta)((sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta)^2 - sin^2

theta cos^2 theta) = (sin^2 theta - cos^2 theta)(1 - sin^2 theta cos^2 theta).

Domain: all theta.
22. sin^6 theta + cos^6 theta = (sin^2 theta)^3 + (cos^2

theta)^3 = (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta)(sin^4 theta - sin^2 theta cos^2 theta +

cos^4 theta) = (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta)^2 - 3sin^2 theta cos^2 theta = 1 -

3sin^2 theta cos^2 theta.
Domain: all theta. 23.
L.H.S. = (1 - sin theta + 1 + sin

theta)/(1 - sin^2 theta) = 2/cos^2 theta = 2sec^2 theta.
Domain: cos theta != 0.

24.
L.H.S. = ((cos theta + sin theta)^2 + (cos theta - sin theta)^2)/(cos^2 theta -

sin^2 theta) = (2cos^2 theta + 2sin^2 theta)/(cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta) =

2/(cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta) = 2/(1 - 2sin^2 theta).
Domain: cos theta != sin theta

and cos theta != -sin theta.

mcqs.q: tan theta + cot theta is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: tan theta + cot theta = sin theta/cos theta + cos theta/sin theta = (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = 1/(sin theta cos theta) = cosec theta sec theta.

options: theta is not a multiple of pi/2
mcqs.q: For the identity tan theta + cot theta = cosec theta sec theta, the domain of theta is:
mcqs.why: The proof needs both sin theta != 0 and cos theta != 0, so theta must avoid 0, pi/2, pi, 3pi/2 and so on; that is, theta is not a multiple of pi/2.

mcqs.q: cos theta + tan theta sin theta is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: cos theta + tan theta sin theta = cos theta + sin^2 theta/cos theta = (cos^2 theta + sin^2 theta)/cos theta = 1/cos theta = sec theta.

mcqs.q: (sec theta + tan theta)(sec theta - tan theta) is equal to:
mcqs.why: The product is a difference of squares: sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta, and this equals 1 by the identity sec^2 theta = 1 + tan^2 theta.

mcqs.q: 2cos^2 theta - 1 is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Both sides equal cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta: 2cos^2 theta - 1 = cos^2 theta - (1 - cos^2 theta), and 1 - 2sin^2 theta = (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta) - 2sin^2 theta, each giving cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta.

mcqs.q: (cot^2 theta - 1)/(1 + cot^2 theta) is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Writing cot^2 theta = cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta gives (cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta)/(sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta = 2cos^2 theta - 1.

mcqs.q: 1/(1 + sin theta) + 1/(1 - sin theta) is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Adding over the common denominator: (1 - sin theta + 1 + sin theta)/(1 - sin^2 theta) = 2/cos^2 theta = 2 sec^2 theta.

mcqs.q: sin^6 theta + cos^6 theta is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: Treating it as a sum of cubes of sin^2 theta and cos^2 theta gives (sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta)^2 - 3 sin^2 theta cos^2 theta = 1 - 3 sin^2 theta cos^2 theta, since sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1.

mcqs.q: For the identity cot^2 theta - cos^2 theta = cot^2 theta cos^2 theta, the domain of theta is:
mcqs.why: The proof divides by sin^2 theta when writing cot^2 theta = cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta, so it needs sin theta != 0, i.e. theta != n pi.

mcqs.q: (sec theta - tan theta)^2 is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: sec theta - tan theta = (1 - sin theta)/cos theta, so its square is (1 - sin theta)^2/cos^2 theta = (1 - sin theta)^2/((1 - sin theta)(1 + sin theta)) = (1 - sin theta)/(1 + sin theta).

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Trigonometric Identities Sum and Difference of Angles

lessons.title: Exercise 10.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Without using the tables, find the values of: i) sin(-780 deg) ii) cot(-855 deg) iii)

cosec(2040 deg) iv) sec(-960 deg) v) tan(1110 deg) vi) sin(-300 deg)

Reduce each angle by whole revolutions. i) sin(-780 deg) = -sin 780 deg = -sin(780

deg - 720 deg) = -sin 60 deg = -sqrt(3)/2. ii) cot(-855 deg) = -cot 855 deg =

-cot(855 deg - 720 deg) = -cot 135 deg = -(-1) = 1. iii) cosec(2040 deg) =

cosec(2040 deg - 1800 deg) = cosec 240 deg = 1/sin 240 deg = 1/(-sqrt(3)/2) =

-2/sqrt(3). iv) sec(-960 deg) = sec 960 deg = sec(960 deg - 720 deg) = sec 240 deg

= 1/cos 240 deg = 1/(-1/2) = -2. v) tan(1110 deg) = tan(1110 deg - 1080 deg) = tan

30 deg = 1/sqrt(3). vi) sin(-300 deg) = -sin 300 deg = -(-sqrt(3)/2) = sqrt(3)/2.

Answers: i) -sqrt(3)/2 ii) 1 iii) -2/sqrt(3) iv) -2 v) 1/sqrt(3) vi) sqrt(3)/2.

Q2

2. Express each of the following as a trigonometric function of an angle of positive

degree measure of less than 45 deg: i) sin 196 deg ii) cos 147 deg iii) sin 319 deg

iv) cos 254 deg v) tan 294 deg vi) cos 728 deg vii) sin(-625 deg) viii) cos(-435 deg)

ix) sin 150 deg

i) sin 196 deg = -sin(196 deg - 180 deg) = -sin 16 deg. ii) cos 147 deg = -cos(180

deg - 147 deg) = -cos 33 deg. iii) sin 319 deg = -sin(360 deg - 319 deg) = -sin 41

deg. iv) cos 254 deg = cos(270 deg - 16 deg) = -sin 16 deg. v) tan 294 deg =

tan(270 deg + 24 deg) = -cot 24 deg. vi) cos 728 deg = cos(728 deg - 720 deg) =

cos 8 deg. vii) sin(-625 deg) = -sin 625 deg = -sin(625 deg - 360 deg) = -sin 265

deg = -(-cos 5 deg) = cos 5 deg. viii) cos(-435 deg) = cos 435 deg = cos(435 deg -

360 deg) = cos 75 deg = sin 15 deg. ix) sin 150 deg = sin(180 deg - 150 deg) = sin

30 deg.
Answers: i) -sin 16 deg ii) -cos 33 deg iii) -sin 41 deg iv) -sin 16 deg v) -cot

24 deg vi) cos 8 deg vii) cos 5 deg viii) sin 15 deg ix) sin 30 deg. Note: the printed

key labels the last answer 'x)'; the exercise as printed has nine parts, so the key's

numbering is treated as a misnumbering of part (ix).

Q3

3. Prove the following: i) sin(180 deg + alpha) sin(90 deg - alpha) = -sin alpha cos

alpha ii) sin 780 deg sin 480 deg + cos 120 deg sin 30 deg = 1/2 iii) cos 306 deg +

cos 234 deg + cos 162 deg + cos 18 deg = 0 iv) cos 330 deg sin 600 deg + cos 120

deg sin 150 deg = -1

i) sin(180 deg + alpha) = -sin alpha and sin(90 deg - alpha) = cos alpha, so the

product is -sin alpha cos alpha. ii) sin 780 deg = sin 60 deg = sqrt(3)/2 and sin 480

deg = sin 120 deg = sqrt(3)/2, so the first product is 3/4; cos 120 deg sin 30 deg =

(-1/2)(1/2) = -1/4; the sum is 3/4 - 1/4 = 1/2. iii) cos 306 deg = cos 54 deg, cos 234

deg = -cos 54 deg, cos 162 deg = -cos 18 deg, so the sum is cos 54 deg - cos 54

deg - cos 18 deg + cos 18 deg = 0. iv) cos 330 deg = cos 30 deg = sqrt(3)/2 and sin

600 deg = sin 240 deg = -sqrt(3)/2, so the first product is -3/4; cos 120 deg sin 150

deg = (-1/2)(1/2) = -1/4; the sum is -1.

Q4

4. Prove that: i) [sin^2(pi + theta) tan(3pi/2 + theta)] / [cot^2(3pi/2 - theta)

cos^2(pi - theta) cosec(2pi - theta)] = cos theta ii) [cos(90 deg + theta) sec(-theta)

tan(180 deg - theta)] / [sec(360 deg - theta) sin(180 deg + theta) cot(90 deg -

theta)] = -1

i) Numerator: sin^2(pi + theta) = sin^2 theta and tan(3pi/2 + theta) = -cot theta,

so the numerator is -sin^2 theta cot theta = -sin theta cos theta. Denominator:

cot^2(3pi/2 - theta) = tan^2 theta, cos^2(pi - theta) = cos^2 theta, cosec(2pi -

theta) = -cosec theta, so the denominator is tan^2 theta x cos^2 theta x (-cosec

theta) = -sin theta.
The ratio is (-sin theta cos theta)/(-sin theta) = cos theta. ii)

Numerator: cos(90 deg + theta) = -sin theta, sec(-theta) = sec theta, tan(180 deg -

theta) = -tan theta, so the numerator is sin theta sec theta tan theta. Denominator:

sec(360 deg - theta) = sec theta, sin(180 deg + theta) = -sin theta, cot(90 deg -

theta) = tan theta, so the denominator is -sin theta sec theta tan theta. The ratio is

-1.

Q5

5. If alpha, beta, gamma are the angles of a triangle ABC, then prove that i)

sin(alpha + beta) = sin gamma ii) cos((alpha + beta)/2) = sin(gamma/2) iii)

cos(alpha + beta) = -cos gamma iv) tan(alpha + beta) + tan gamma = 0

Since alpha + beta + gamma = 180 deg, we have alpha + beta = 180 deg -

gamma. i) sin(alpha + beta) = sin(180 deg - gamma) = sin gamma. ii) (alpha +

beta)/2 = 90 deg - gamma/2, so cos((alpha + beta)/2) = cos(90 deg - gamma/2) =

sin(gamma/2). iii) cos(alpha + beta) = cos(180 deg - gamma) = -cos gamma. iv)

tan(alpha + beta) = tan(180 deg - gamma) = -tan gamma, so tan(alpha + beta) +

tan gamma = 0.

mcqs.q: Find sin(-780 deg).
mcqs.why: sin(-780 deg) = -sin 780 deg = -sin(780 deg - 720 deg) = -sin 60 deg = -sqrt(3)/2.

mcqs.q: Find cot(-855 deg).
mcqs.why: cot(-855 deg) = -cot 855 deg = -cot(855 deg - 720 deg) = -cot 135 deg = -(-1) = 1.

mcqs.q: Find cosec(2040 deg).
mcqs.why: cosec(2040 deg) = cosec(2040 deg - 1800 deg) = cosec 240 deg = 1/sin 240 deg = 1/(-sqrt(3)/2) = -2/sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: Find sec(-960 deg).
mcqs.why: sec(-960 deg) = sec 960 deg = sec(960 deg - 720 deg) = sec 240 deg = 1/cos 240 deg = 1/(-1/2) = -2.

mcqs.q: Find tan(1110 deg).
mcqs.why: tan(1110 deg) = tan(1110 deg - 1080 deg) = tan 30 deg = 1/sqrt(3), subtracting three whole revolutions of 360 deg.

mcqs.q: Find sin(-300 deg).
mcqs.why: sin(-300 deg) = -sin 300 deg, and sin 300 deg = -sqrt(3)/2, so sin(-300 deg) = -(-sqrt(3)/2) = sqrt(3)/2.

mcqs.q: Express sin 196 deg as a trigonometric function of an angle of less than 45 deg.
mcqs.why: 196 deg is in quadrant III, where sine is negative, and its reference angle is 196 deg - 180 deg = 16 deg. Hence sin 196 deg = -sin 16 deg.

mcqs.q: Express cos 254 deg as a trigonometric function of an angle of less than 45 deg.
mcqs.why: Using the 270 deg allied angle, cos 254 deg = cos(270 deg - 16 deg) = -sin 16 deg, as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: Express tan 294 deg as a trigonometric function of an angle of less than 45 deg.
mcqs.why: Using the 270 deg allied angle, tan 294 deg = tan(270 deg + 24 deg) = -cot 24 deg, as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta, gamma are the angles of a triangle ABC, then cos((alpha + beta)/2) is equal to:
mcqs.why: Since alpha + beta = 180 deg - gamma, (alpha + beta)/2 = 90 deg - gamma/2. Hence cos((alpha + beta)/2) = cos(90 deg - gamma/2) = sin(gamma/2).

lessons.title: Exercise 10.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-2

1. Prove that: i) sin(180 deg + theta) = -sin theta ii) cos(180 deg + theta) = -cos

theta iii) tan(270 deg - theta) = cot theta iv) cos(theta - 180 deg) = -cos theta v)

cos(270 deg + theta) = sin theta vi) sin(theta + 270 deg) = -cos theta vii) tan(180

deg + theta) = tan theta viii) cos(360 deg - theta) = cos theta

These are the allied-angle formulas. i) sin(180 deg + theta) = -sin theta since the

angle is in the third quadrant with reference angle theta. ii) cos(180 deg + theta) =

-cos theta by the same reasoning. iii) tan(270 deg - theta) = cot theta (the 270 deg

shift changes tangent to cotangent with a positive sign). iv) cos(theta - 180 deg) =

cos(180 deg - theta) with sign: cos(theta - 180 deg) = -cos theta. v) cos(270 deg +

theta) = sin theta. vi) sin(theta + 270 deg) = -cos theta. vii) tan(180 deg + theta) =

tan theta (period 180 deg). viii) cos(360 deg - theta) = cos theta (cosine is even and

periodic).

2. Find the values of the following: i) sin 15 deg ii) cos 15 deg iii) tan 15 deg iv) sin

105 deg v) cos 105 deg vi) tan 105 deg (Hint: 15 deg = (45 deg - 30 deg) and 105

deg = (60 deg + 45 deg))

i) sin 15 deg = sin(45 deg - 30 deg) = sin 45 deg cos 30 deg - cos 45 deg sin 30 deg

= (1/sqrt(2))(sqrt(3)/2) - (1/sqrt(2))(1/2) = (sqrt(3) - 1)/(2sqrt(2)). ii) cos 15 deg =

cos(45 deg - 30 deg) = cos 45 deg cos 30 deg + sin 45 deg sin 30 deg = (sqrt(3) +

1)/(2sqrt(2)). iii) tan 15 deg = sin 15 deg/cos 15 deg = (sqrt(3) - 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1). iv)

sin 105 deg = sin(60 deg + 45 deg) = sin 60 deg cos 45 deg + cos 60 deg sin 45

deg = (sqrt(3) + 1)/(2sqrt(2)). v) cos 105 deg = cos(60 deg + 45 deg) = cos 60 deg

cos 45 deg - sin 60 deg sin 45 deg = (1 - sqrt(3))/(2sqrt(2)). vi) tan 105 deg = sin

105 deg/cos 105 deg = (1 + sqrt(3))/(1 - sqrt(3)).

Q3

3. Prove that: i) sin(45 deg + alpha) = (1/sqrt(2))(sin alpha + cos alpha) ii)

cos(alpha + 45 deg) = (1/sqrt(2))(cos alpha - sin alpha)

i) sin(45 deg + alpha) = sin 45 deg cos alpha + cos 45 deg sin alpha = (1/sqrt(2))

cos alpha + (1/sqrt(2)) sin alpha = (1/sqrt(2))(sin alpha + cos alpha). ii) cos(alpha +

45 deg) = cos alpha cos 45 deg - sin alpha sin 45 deg = (1/sqrt(2))(cos alpha - sin

alpha).

Q4

4. Prove that: i) tan(45 deg + A) tan(45 deg - A) = 1 ii) tan(pi/4 - theta) + tan(3pi/4

+ theta) = 0 iii) sin(theta + pi/6) + cos(theta + pi/3) = cos theta iv) [sin theta - cos

theta tan(theta/2)] / [cos theta + sin theta tan(theta/2)] = tan(theta/2) v) (1 - tan

theta tan phi)/(1 + tan theta tan phi) = cos(theta + phi)/cos(theta - phi)

i) tan(45 deg + A) = (1 + tan A)/(1 - tan A) and tan(45 deg - A) = (1 - tan A)/(1 +

tan A); their product is 1. ii) tan(3pi/4 + theta) = tan(pi - (pi/4 - theta)) = -tan(pi/4 -

theta), so the sum is 0.
Note: the right-hand side is cut off at the foot of book p. 326

in the scan; 0 is the value forced by the computation. iii) sin(theta + pi/6) = sin

theta cos pi/6 + cos theta sin pi/6 = (sqrt(3)/2) sin theta + (1/2) cos theta. cos(theta

+ pi/3) = cos theta cos pi/3 - sin theta sin pi/3 = (1/2) cos theta - (sqrt(3)/2) sin

theta.
Adding gives cos theta. iv) Put t = tan(theta/2), so tan theta = 2t/(1 - t^2).

Dividing numerator and denominator by cos theta gives (tan theta - t)/(1 + tan

theta x t) = (2t/(1 - t^2) - t)/(1 + 2t^2/(1 - t^2)) = (t(1 + t^2)/(1 - t^2))/((1 +

t^2)/(1 - t^2)) = t = tan(theta/2). v) Multiplying numerator and denominator by cos

theta cos phi gives (cos theta cos phi - sin theta sin phi)/(cos theta cos phi + sin

theta sin phi) = cos(theta + phi)/cos(theta - phi).

Q5-6

5. Show that: cos(alpha + beta) cos(alpha - beta) = cos^2 alpha - sin^2 beta =

cos^2 beta - sin^2 alpha

cos(alpha + beta) cos(alpha - beta) = (cos alpha cos beta - sin alpha sin beta)(cos

alpha cos beta + sin alpha sin beta) = cos^2 alpha cos^2 beta - sin^2 alpha sin^2

beta. Replacing cos^2 beta by 1 - sin^2 beta and sin^2 alpha by 1 - cos^2 alpha

gives cos^2 alpha - sin^2 beta. Replacing cos^2 alpha by 1 - sin^2 alpha and

sin^2 beta by 1 - cos^2 beta gives cos^2 beta - sin^2 alpha.

6. Show that: [sin(alpha + beta) + sin(alpha - beta)] / [cos(alpha + beta) +

cos(alpha - beta)] = tan alpha

The numerator is 2 sin alpha cos beta and the denominator is 2 cos alpha cos beta;

their ratio is tan alpha.

Q7

7. Show that: i) cot(alpha + beta) = (cot alpha cot beta - 1)/(cot alpha + cot beta) ii)

cot(alpha - beta) = (cot alpha cot beta + 1)/(cot beta - cot alpha) iii) (tan alpha +

tan beta)/(tan alpha - tan beta) = sin(alpha + beta)/sin(alpha - beta)

i) cot(alpha + beta) = cos(alpha + beta)/sin(alpha + beta) = (cos alpha cos beta -

sin alpha sin beta)/(sin alpha cos beta + cos alpha sin beta); dividing numerator and

denominator by sin alpha sin beta gives (cot alpha cot beta - 1)/(cot beta + cot

alpha). ii) Similarly, cot(alpha - beta) = (cos alpha cos beta + sin alpha sin beta)/(sin

alpha cos beta - cos alpha sin beta) = (cot alpha cot beta + 1)/(cot beta - cot alpha).

iii) Multiplying numerator and denominator by cos alpha cos beta gives (sin alpha

cos beta + cos alpha sin beta)/(sin alpha cos beta - cos alpha sin beta) = sin(alpha

+ beta)/sin(alpha - beta).

Q8

8. If sin alpha = 4/5 and cos beta = 40/41, where 0 < alpha < pi/2 and 0 < beta <

pi/2, show that sin(alpha - beta) = 133/205.

In the first quadrant, cos alpha = 3/5 and sin beta = 9/41.
Hence sin(alpha - beta) =

sin alpha cos beta - cos alpha sin beta = (4/5)(40/41) - (3/5)(9/41) = 160/205 -

27/205 = 133/205.

Q9

9. If sin alpha = 4/5 and sin beta = 12/13, where pi/2 < alpha < pi and pi/2 < beta

< pi, find i) sin(alpha + beta) ii) cos(alpha + beta) iii) tan(alpha + beta) iv) sin(alpha

- beta) v) cos(alpha - beta) vi) tan(alpha - beta). In which quadrants do the terminal

sides of the angles of measures (alpha + beta) and (alpha - beta) lie?

In the second quadrant, cos alpha = -3/5 and cos beta = -5/13. i) sin(alpha + beta)

= (4/5)(-5/13) + (-3/5)(12/13) = -20/65 - 36/65 = -56/65. ii) cos(alpha + beta) =

(-3/5)(-5/13) - (4/5)(12/13) = 15/65 - 48/65 = -33/65. iii) tan(alpha + beta) =

(-56/65)/(-33/65) = 56/33. iv) sin(alpha - beta) = (4/5)(-5/13) - (-3/5)(12/13) =

-20/65 + 36/65 = 16/65. v) cos(alpha - beta) = (-3/5)(-5/13) + (4/5)(12/13) = 15/65

+ 48/65 = 63/65. vi) tan(alpha - beta) = 16/63.
Since sin(alpha + beta) < 0 and

cos(alpha + beta) < 0, the terminal side of alpha + beta lies in quadrant III; since

sin(alpha - beta) > 0 and cos(alpha - beta) > 0, the terminal side of alpha - beta lies

in quadrant I.

Q10

10. Find sin(alpha + beta) and cos(alpha + beta), given that i) tan alpha = 3/4, cos

beta = 5/13 and neither the terminal side of the angle of measure alpha nor that of

beta is in the I quadrant ii) tan alpha = -15/8 and sin beta = -7/25 and neither the

terminal side of the angle of measure alpha nor that of beta is in the IV quadrant

i) tan alpha > 0 means quadrant I or III; not I, so quadrant III: sin alpha = -3/5, cos

alpha = -4/5. cos beta > 0 means quadrant I or IV; not I, so quadrant IV: sin beta =

-12/13.
Hence sin(alpha + beta) = (-3/5)(5/13) + (-4/5)(-12/13) = -15/65 + 48/65 =

33/65, and cos(alpha + beta) = (-4/5)(5/13) - (-3/5)(-12/13) = -20/65 - 36/65 =

-56/65. ii) tan alpha < 0 means quadrant II or IV; not IV, so quadrant II: sin alpha =

15/17, cos alpha = -8/17. sin beta < 0 means quadrant III or IV; not IV, so quadrant

III: cos beta = -24/25.
Hence sin(alpha + beta) = (15/17)(-24/25) + (-8/17)(-7/25) =

-360/425 + 56/425 = -304/425, and cos(alpha + beta) = (-8/17)(-24/25) -

(15/17)(-7/25) = 192/425 + 105/425 = 297/425.
FLAG: the printed key reads

(416/425, 3/5) for part (ii), but those two numbers are internally inconsistent

((416/425)^2 + (3/5)^2 = 1.318, not 1) and do not follow from the printed

conditions; the computed values (-304/425, 297/425) are given instead.

Q11

11. Prove that: (cos 8 deg - sin 8 deg)/(cos 8 deg + sin 8 deg) = tan 37 deg

Dividing numerator and denominator by cos 8 deg gives (1 - tan 8 deg)/(1 + tan 8

deg) = tan(45 deg - 8 deg) = tan 37 deg.

Q12

12. If alpha, beta, gamma are the angles of a triangle ABC, show that cot(alpha/2) +

cot(beta/2) + cot(gamma/2) = cot(alpha/2) cot(beta/2) cot(gamma/2)

Since (alpha + beta)/2 = 90 deg - gamma/2, we have cot((alpha + beta)/2) =

tan(gamma/2) = 1/cot(gamma/2).
But cot((alpha + beta)/2) = (cot(alpha/2)

cot(beta/2) - 1)/(cot(alpha/2) + cot(beta/2)).
Hence (cot(alpha/2) cot(beta/2) -

1)/(cot(alpha/2) + cot(beta/2)) = 1/cot(gamma/2), which cross-multiplies to

cot(alpha/2) cot(beta/2) cot(gamma/2) - cot(gamma/2) = cot(alpha/2) + cot(beta/2),

i.e. cot(alpha/2) + cot(beta/2) + cot(gamma/2) = cot(alpha/2) cot(beta/2)

cot(gamma/2).

Q13

13. If alpha + beta + gamma = 180 deg, show that cot alpha cot beta + cot beta

cot gamma + cot gamma cot alpha = 1

Since alpha + beta = 180 deg - gamma, tan(alpha + beta) = -tan gamma. Hence

(tan alpha + tan beta)/(1 - tan alpha tan beta) = -tan gamma, so tan alpha + tan

beta = -tan gamma + tan alpha tan beta tan gamma.
Dividing by tan alpha tan

beta tan gamma gives cot beta cot gamma + cot alpha cot gamma = -cot alpha cot

beta + 1, i.e. cot alpha cot beta + cot beta cot gamma + cot gamma cot alpha = 1.

Q14

14. Express the following in the form r sin(theta + phi): i) 12 sin theta + 5 cos theta

ii) 3 sin theta - 4 cos theta iii) sin theta - cos theta iv) 5 sin theta - 4 cos theta v) sin

theta + cos theta vi) 3 sin theta - 5 cos theta

Write a sin theta + b cos theta = r sin(theta + phi) with r = sqrt(a^2 + b^2), cos

phi = a/r, sin phi = b/r. i) r = 13, cos phi = 12/13, sin phi = 5/13: 13 sin(theta + phi)

with tan phi = 5/12 (phi in quadrant I). ii) r = 5, cos phi = 3/5, sin phi = -4/5: 5

sin(theta + phi) with tan phi = -4/3, phi in quadrant IV; equivalently 5 sin(theta -

psi) with tan psi = 4/3, psi in quadrant I. FLAG: the printed key reads tan phi = 4/3

for this part (unsigned), while the signed value in the form r sin(theta + phi) is -4/3;

the key gives signed values (-1, -4/5, -5/3) for parts (iii), (iv), (vi). iii) r = sqrt(2), cos

phi = 1/sqrt(2), sin phi = -1/sqrt(2): sqrt(2) sin(theta + phi) with tan phi = -1. iv) r =

sqrt(41), cos phi = 5/sqrt(41), sin phi = -4/sqrt(41): sqrt(41) sin(theta + phi) with

tan phi = -4/5. v) r = sqrt(2), cos phi = 1/sqrt(2), sin phi = 1/sqrt(2): sqrt(2)

sin(theta + phi) with tan phi = 1. vi) r = sqrt(34), cos phi = 3/sqrt(34), sin phi =

-5/sqrt(34): sqrt(34) sin(theta + phi) with tan phi = -5/3.
Note: the question's phrase

'terminal sides of theta and phi in the first quadrant' cannot hold for the minus

cases (ii), (iii), (iv), (vi), where phi lies in quadrant IV; the signed-phi convention

above is used throughout.

mcqs.q: Find sin 15 deg.
mcqs.why: sin 15 deg = sin(45 deg - 30 deg) = sin 45 deg cos 30 deg - cos 45 deg sin 30 deg = (1/sqrt(2))(sqrt(3)/2) - (1/sqrt(2))(1/2) = (sqrt(3) - 1)/(2 sqrt(2)).

mcqs.q: Find cos 15 deg.
mcqs.why: cos 15 deg = cos(45 deg - 30 deg) = cos 45 deg cos 30 deg + sin 45 deg sin 30 deg = (1/sqrt(2))(sqrt(3)/2) + (1/sqrt(2))(1/2) = (sqrt(3) + 1)/(2 sqrt(2)).

mcqs.q: Find tan 15 deg.
mcqs.why: tan 15 deg = sin 15 deg/cos 15 deg = ((sqrt(3) - 1)/(2 sqrt(2)))/((sqrt(3) + 1)/(2 sqrt(2))) = (sqrt(3) - 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1), the factors 2 sqrt(2) cancelling.

mcqs.q: Find sin 105 deg.
mcqs.why: sin 105 deg = sin(60 deg + 45 deg) = sin 60 deg cos 45 deg + cos 60 deg sin 45 deg = (sqrt(3)/2)(1/sqrt(2)) + (1/2)(1/sqrt(2)) = (sqrt(3) + 1)/(2 sqrt(2)).

mcqs.q: Find cos 105 deg.
mcqs.why: cos 105 deg = cos(60 deg + 45 deg) = cos 60 deg cos 45 deg - sin 60 deg sin 45 deg = (1/2)(1/sqrt(2)) - (sqrt(3)/2)(1/sqrt(2)) = (1 - sqrt(3))/(2 sqrt(2)).

mcqs.q: If sin alpha = 4/5 and cos beta = 40/41, with both alpha and beta in the first quadrant, find sin(alpha - beta).
If sin alpha = 4/5 and sin beta = 12/13, with both alpha and beta in quadrant II, find sin(alpha + beta).
If sin alpha = 4/5 and sin beta = 12/13, with both alpha and beta in quadrant II, find cos(alpha + beta).
mcqs.why: In quadrant II, cos alpha = -3/5 and cos beta = -5/13. cos(alpha + beta) = (-3/5)(-5/13) - (4/5)(12/13) = 15/65 - 48/65 = -33/65.

mcqs.q: If sin alpha = 4/5 and sin beta = 12/13, with both alpha and beta in quadrant II, find tan(alpha - beta).
If tan alpha = -15/8 and sin beta = -7/25, with neither terminal side in quadrant IV, find sin(alpha + beta), using the corrected value given in the notes.
mcqs.why: Alpha is in quadrant II: sin alpha = 15/17, cos alpha = -8/17. Beta is in quadrant III: cos beta = -24/25. sin(alpha + beta) = (15/17)(-24/25) + (-8/17)(-7/25) = -360/425 + 56/425 = -304/425. The printed key pair is inconsistent, since (416/425)^2 + (3/5)^2 is not 1.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Find the values of sin 2alpha, cos 2alpha and tan 2alpha, when: i) sin alpha =

12/13 ii) sin alpha = 12/13 iii) cos alpha = 3/5, where 0 < alpha < pi/2

i) Taking alpha acute, cos alpha = 5/13.
Then sin 2alpha = 2 sin alpha cos alpha =

2(12/13)(5/13) = 120/169; cos 2alpha = 1 - 2sin^2 alpha = 1 - 288/169 = -119/169;

tan 2alpha = -120/119. ii) Part (ii) is printed identically to part (i) (a duplication in

the book, with no distinguishing condition); the notes give the same values as (i).

FLAG: the printed key's second set of values (24/25, -7/25, -24/7) is exactly the

answer to part (iii), not to a distinct part (ii). iii) With cos alpha = 3/5 and 0 < alpha

< pi/2, sin alpha = 4/5.
Then sin 2alpha = 2(4/5)(3/5) = 24/25; cos 2alpha =

(3/5)^2 - (4/5)^2 = -7/25; tan 2alpha = -24/7.

Q2-7

2. Prove the following identities: 2. cot alpha - tan alpha = 2 cot 2alpha 3. sin

2alpha/(1 + cos 2alpha) = tan alpha 4. (1 - cos alpha)/sin alpha = tan(alpha/2) 5.

(cos alpha - sin alpha)/(cos alpha + sin alpha) = sec 2alpha - tan 2alpha 6. sqrt((1 +

sin alpha)/(1 - sin alpha)) = (sin(alpha/2) + cos(alpha/2))/(sin(alpha/2) -

cos(alpha/2)) 7. (cosec theta + 2 cosec 2theta)/sec theta = cot(theta/2)

2. cot alpha - tan alpha = cos alpha/sin alpha - sin alpha/cos alpha = (cos^2 alpha -

sin^2 alpha)/(sin alpha cos alpha) = cos 2alpha/((1/2) sin 2alpha) = 2 cot 2alpha. 3.

sin 2alpha/(1 + cos 2alpha) = 2 sin alpha cos alpha/(2cos^2 alpha) = tan alpha. 4.

1 - cos alpha = 2sin^2(alpha/2) and sin alpha = 2 sin(alpha/2) cos(alpha/2), so the

ratio is tan(alpha/2).
5. sec 2alpha - tan 2alpha = (1 - sin 2alpha)/cos 2alpha = (sin

alpha - cos alpha)^2/((cos alpha - sin alpha)(cos alpha + sin alpha)) = (cos alpha -

sin alpha)/(cos alpha + sin alpha). 6.
1 + sin alpha = (sin(alpha/2) +

cos(alpha/2))^2 and 1 - sin alpha = (sin(alpha/2) - cos(alpha/2))^2, so the square

root is (sin(alpha/2) + cos(alpha/2))/(sin(alpha/2) - cos(alpha/2)) with the sign choice

as printed.
7. cosec theta + 2 cosec 2theta = 1/sin theta + 1/(sin theta cos theta) =

(1 + cos theta)/(sin theta cos theta); dividing by sec theta (multiplying by cos theta)

gives (1 + cos theta)/sin theta = (2cos^2(theta/2))/(2 sin(theta/2) cos(theta/2)) =

cot(theta/2).

Q8-13

8. 1 + tan alpha tan 2alpha = sec 2alpha 9. (2 sin theta sin 2theta)/(cos theta + cos

3theta) = tan 2theta tan theta 10. sin 3theta/sin theta - cos 3theta/cos theta = 2

11. cos 3theta/cos theta + sin 3theta/sin theta = 4 cos 2theta 12. (tan(theta/2) +

cot(theta/2))/(cot(theta/2) - tan(theta/2)) = sec theta 13. sin 3theta/cos theta + cos

3theta/sin theta = 2 cot 2theta

8. tan alpha tan 2alpha = tan alpha x 2tan alpha/(1 - tan^2 alpha) = 2tan^2

alpha/(1 - tan^2 alpha), so 1 + tan alpha tan 2alpha = (1 + tan^2 alpha)/(1 - tan^2

alpha) = sec 2alpha. 9.
The denominator cos theta + cos 3theta = 2 cos 2theta cos

theta; the numerator 2 sin theta sin 2theta = 4sin^2 theta cos theta; the ratio is

2sin^2 theta/cos 2theta = tan 2theta tan theta (since tan 2theta tan theta =

2sin^2 theta/(cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta)). 10.
Combining over sin theta cos theta

gives (sin 3theta cos theta - cos 3theta sin theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = sin

2theta/(sin theta cos theta) = 2. 11.
Combining over sin theta cos theta gives (cos

3theta sin theta + sin 3theta cos theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = sin 4theta/(sin theta

cos theta) = 2 sin 4theta/sin 2theta = 4 cos 2theta.
12. tan(theta/2) + cot(theta/2)

= 2/sin theta and cot(theta/2) - tan(theta/2) = 2cos theta/sin theta, so the ratio is

sec theta. 13.
Combining over sin theta cos theta gives (sin 3theta sin theta + cos

3theta cos theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = cos 2theta/(sin theta cos theta) = 2 cot

2theta.

Q14-15

14. Reduce sin^4 theta to an expression involving only function of multiples of

theta, raised to the first power.

sin^2 theta = (1 - cos 2theta)/2, so sin^4 theta = (1 - cos 2theta)^2/4 = (1 - 2cos

2theta + cos^2 2theta)/4. Since cos^2 2theta = (1 + cos 4theta)/2, this becomes

(1 - 2cos 2theta + (1 + cos 4theta)/2)/4 = (3 - 4cos 2theta + cos 4theta)/8. Answer:

sin^4 theta = (3 - 4cos 2theta + cos 4theta)/8.

15. Find the values of sin theta and cos theta without using table or calculator,

when theta is i) 18 deg ii) 36 deg iii) 54 deg iv) 72 deg. Hence prove that: cos 36

deg cos 72 deg cos 108 deg cos 144 deg = 1/16

Let theta = 18 deg.
Then 2theta = 36 deg and 3theta = 54 deg = 90 deg - 2theta,

so sin 2theta = cos 3theta, i.e.
2 sin theta cos theta = 4cos^3 theta - 3 cos theta.

Cancelling cos theta gives 2 sin theta = 4(1 - sin^2 theta) - 3, i.e. 4sin^2 theta + 2

sin theta - 1 = 0, so sin theta = (sqrt(5) - 1)/4 (positive root).
Hence: i) sin 18 deg =

(sqrt(5) - 1)/4, cos 18 deg = sqrt(10 + 2sqrt(5))/4. ii) sin 36 deg = cos 54 deg =

sqrt(10 - 2sqrt(5))/4, cos 36 deg = sin 54 deg = (sqrt(5) + 1)/4. iii) sin 54 deg =

(sqrt(5) + 1)/4, cos 54 deg = sqrt(10 - 2sqrt(5))/4. iv) sin 72 deg = cos 18 deg =

sqrt(10 + 2sqrt(5))/4, cos 72 deg = sin 18 deg = (sqrt(5) - 1)/4.
For the product: cos

108 deg = -cos 72 deg and cos 144 deg = -cos 36 deg, so the product equals cos^2

36 deg cos^2 72 deg = ((sqrt(5) + 1)/4)^2 ((sqrt(5) - 1)/4)^2 = ((5 - 1)/16)^2 =

(1/4)^2 = 1/16.

mcqs.q: If sin alpha = 12/13 with alpha acute, find sin 2alpha.
mcqs.why: With alpha acute, cos alpha = 5/13. sin 2alpha = 2 sin alpha cos alpha = 2 x (12/13) x (5/13) = 120/169.

mcqs.q: If sin alpha = 12/13 with alpha acute, find cos 2alpha.
If cos alpha = 3/5 with 0 < alpha < pi/2, find sin 2alpha.
mcqs.why: In the first quadrant sin alpha = 4/5. sin 2alpha = 2 sin alpha cos alpha = 2 x (4/5) x (3/5) = 24/25.

mcqs.q: If cos alpha = 3/5 with 0 < alpha < pi/2, find cos 2alpha.
mcqs.why: cos 2alpha = cos^2 alpha - sin^2 alpha, with sin alpha = 4/5 in the first quadrant. So cos 2alpha = (3/5)^2 - (4/5)^2 = 9/25 - 16/25 = -7/25.

mcqs.q: If cos alpha = 3/5 with 0 < alpha < pi/2, find tan 2alpha.
mcqs.why: tan 2alpha = sin 2alpha/cos 2alpha. Using sin 2alpha = 24/25 and cos 2alpha = -7/25 from the same data, tan 2alpha = (24/25)/(-7/25) = -24/7.

mcqs.q: (1 - cos alpha)/sin alpha is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: 1 - cos alpha = 2 sin^2(alpha/2) and sin alpha = 2 sin(alpha/2) cos(alpha/2), so the ratio is sin(alpha/2)/cos(alpha/2) = tan(alpha/2).

mcqs.q: cot alpha - tan alpha is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: cot alpha - tan alpha = (cos^2 alpha - sin^2 alpha)/(sin alpha cos alpha) = cos 2alpha/((1/2) sin 2alpha) = 2 cot 2alpha.

mcqs.q: sin^4 theta reduced to functions of multiples of theta, raised to the first power, is:
mcqs.why: sin^4 theta = ((1 - cos 2theta)/2)^2 = (1 - 2 cos 2theta + cos^2 2theta)/4, and cos^2 2theta = (1 + cos 4theta)/2, giving (3 - 4 cos 2theta + cos 4theta)/8.

mcqs.q: Find sin 18 deg.
mcqs.why: With theta = 18 deg, sin 2theta = cos 3theta leads to 4 sin^2 theta + 2 sin theta - 1 = 0. The positive root is sin theta = (-2 + sqrt(4 + 16))/8 = (-2 + 2 sqrt(5))/8 = (sqrt(5) - 1)/4.

mcqs.q: Find cos 36 deg cos 72 deg cos 108 deg cos 144 deg.
mcqs.why: cos 108 deg = -cos 72 deg and cos 144 deg = -cos 36 deg, so the product is cos^2 36 deg cos^2 72 deg = [((sqrt(5) + 1)/4) x ((sqrt(5) - 1)/4)]^2 = [(5 - 1)/16]^2 = (1/4)^2 = 1/16.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Express the following products as sums or differences: i) 2 sin 3theta cos theta ii)

2 cos 5theta sin 3theta iii) sin 5theta cos 2theta iv) 2 sin 7theta sin 2theta v) cos(x

+ y) sin(x - y) vi) cos(2x + 30 deg) cos(2x - 30 deg) vii) sin 12 deg sin 46 deg viii)

sin(x + 45 deg) sin(x - 45 deg)

Using 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B), 2 cos A sin B = sin(A + B) - sin(A - B), 2

sin A sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B), 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A - B): i) 2 sin

3theta cos theta = sin 4theta + sin 2theta. ii) 2 cos 5theta sin 3theta = sin 8theta -

sin 2theta. iii) sin 5theta cos 2theta = (1/2)(sin 7theta + sin 3theta). iv) 2 sin 7theta

sin 2theta = cos 5theta - cos 9theta. v) cos(x + y) sin(x - y) = (1/2)(sin 2x - sin 2y).

vi) cos(2x + 30 deg) cos(2x - 30 deg) = (1/2)(cos 4x + cos 60 deg). vii) sin 12 deg

sin 46 deg = (1/2)(cos 34 deg - cos 58 deg). viii) sin(x + 45 deg) sin(x - 45 deg) =

(1/2)(cos 90 deg - cos 2x).

Q2

2. Express the following sums or differences as products: i) sin 5theta + sin 3theta

ii) sin 8theta - sin 4theta iii) cos 6theta + cos 3theta iv) cos 7theta - cos theta v) cos

12 deg + cos 48 deg vi) sin(x + 30 deg) + sin(x - 30 deg)

Using sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C - D)/2), sin C - sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2)

sin((C - D)/2), cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C - D)/2), cos C - cos D = -2

sin((C + D)/2) sin((C - D)/2): i) sin 5theta + sin 3theta = 2 sin 4theta cos theta. ii)

sin 8theta - sin 4theta = 2 cos 6theta sin 2theta. iii) cos 6theta + cos 3theta = 2

cos(9theta/2) cos(3theta/2). iv) cos 7theta - cos theta = -2 sin 4theta sin 3theta. v)

cos 12 deg + cos 48 deg = 2 cos 30 deg cos 18 deg. vi) sin(x + 30 deg) + sin(x - 30

deg) = 2 sin x cos 30 deg.

Q3

3. Prove the following identities: i) (sin 3x - sin x)/(cos x - cos 3x) = cot 2x ii) (sin 8x

+ sin 2x)/(cos 8x + cos 2x) = tan 5x iii) (sin alpha - sin beta)/(sin alpha + sin beta)

= tan((alpha - beta)/2) cot((alpha + beta)/2)

i) The numerator sin 3x - sin x = 2 cos 2x sin x; the denominator cos x - cos 3x = -2

sin 2x sin(-x) = 2 sin 2x sin x; the ratio is cot 2x. ii) The numerator sin 8x + sin 2x =

2 sin 5x cos 3x; the denominator cos 8x + cos 2x = 2 cos 5x cos 3x; the ratio is tan

5x. iii) The numerator sin alpha - sin beta = 2 cos((alpha + beta)/2) sin((alpha -

beta)/2); the denominator sin alpha + sin beta = 2 sin((alpha + beta)/2) cos((alpha -

beta)/2); the ratio is tan((alpha - beta)/2) cot((alpha + beta)/2).

Q4

4. Prove that: i) cos 20 deg + cos 100 deg + cos 140 deg = 0 ii) sin(pi/4 - theta)

sin(pi/4 + theta) = (1/2) cos 2theta iii) (sin theta + sin 3theta + sin 5theta + sin

7theta)/(cos theta + cos 3theta + cos 5theta + cos 7theta) = tan 4theta

i) cos 100 deg + cos 140 deg = 2 cos 120 deg cos 20 deg = 2(-1/2) cos 20 deg =

-cos 20 deg, so adding cos 20 deg gives 0. ii) sin(pi/4 - theta) sin(pi/4 + theta) =

(1/2)[cos(-2theta) - cos(pi/2)] = (1/2) cos 2theta. iii) The numerator groups as (sin

7theta + sin theta) + (sin 5theta + sin 3theta) = 2 sin 4theta cos 3theta + 2 sin

4theta cos theta = 2 sin 4theta (cos 3theta + cos theta); the denominator groups as

2 cos 4theta (cos 3theta + cos theta); the ratio is tan 4theta.

Q5

5. Prove that: i) cos 20 deg cos 40 deg cos 60 deg cos 80 deg = 1/16 ii) sin(pi/9)

sin(2pi/9) sin(pi/3) sin(4pi/9) = 3/16 iii) sin 10 deg sin 30 deg sin 50 deg sin 70 deg

= 1/16

i) cos 60 deg = 1/2.
Also cos 20 deg cos 40 deg cos 80 deg = 1/8: multiply by 8 sin

20 deg and use sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x three times (8 sin 20 deg cos 20 deg cos 40

deg cos 80 deg = sin 160 deg = sin 20 deg).
Hence the product is (1/2)(1/8) = 1/16.

ii) sin(pi/3) = sqrt(3)/2.
Also sin 20 deg sin 40 deg sin 80 deg = sqrt(3)/8 by the

identity sin x sin(60 deg - x) sin(60 deg + x) = (1/4) sin 3x with x = 20 deg (giving

(1/4) sin 60 deg = sqrt(3)/8).
Hence the product is (sqrt(3)/2)(sqrt(3)/8) = 3/16. iii)

sin 30 deg = 1/2.
Also sin 10 deg sin 50 deg sin 70 deg = 1/8 by the same identity

with x = 10 deg (sin 30 deg/4 = (1/2)/4 = 1/8).
Hence the product is (1/2)(1/8) =

1/16.

mcqs.q: Express 2 sin 3theta cos theta as a sum or difference.
mcqs.why: Using 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B) with A = 3theta and B = theta gives sin 4theta + sin 2theta.

mcqs.q: Express 2 cos 5theta sin 3theta as a sum or difference.
mcqs.why: Using 2 cos A sin B = sin(A + B) - sin(A - B) with A = 5theta and B = 3theta gives sin 8theta - sin 2theta.

mcqs.q: Express sin 5theta cos 2theta as a sum or difference.
mcqs.why: sin A cos B = (1/2)[sin(A + B) + sin(A - B)], so with A = 5theta and B = 2theta the product is (1/2)(sin 7theta + sin 3theta).

mcqs.q: Express 2 sin 7theta sin 2theta as a sum or difference.
mcqs.why: Using 2 sin A sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B) with A = 7theta and B = 2theta gives cos 5theta - cos 9theta.

mcqs.q: Express sin 5theta + sin 3theta as a product.
mcqs.why: Using sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C - D)/2) with C = 5theta and D = 3theta gives 2 sin 4theta cos theta.

mcqs.q: Express cos 7theta - cos theta as a product.
mcqs.why: Using cos C - cos D = -2 sin((C + D)/2) sin((C - D)/2) with C = 7theta and D = theta gives -2 sin 4theta sin 3theta.

mcqs.q: Express cos 12 deg + cos 48 deg as a product.
mcqs.why: Using cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C - D)/2): (12 + 48)/2 = 30 and (48 - 12)/2 = 18, giving 2 cos 30 deg cos 18 deg.

mcqs.q: (sin 3x - sin x)/(cos x - cos 3x) is equal to which of the following?
mcqs.why: The numerator sin 3x - sin x = 2 cos 2x sin x and the denominator cos x - cos 3x = 2 sin 2x sin x, so the ratio is cos 2x/sin 2x = cot 2x.

mcqs.q: Find cos 20 deg + cos 100 deg + cos 140 deg.
mcqs.why: cos 100 deg + cos 140 deg = 2 cos 120 deg cos 20 deg = 2 x (-1/2) x cos 20 deg = -cos 20 deg. Adding cos 20 deg gives -cos 20 deg + cos 20 deg = 0.

mcqs.q: Find cos 20 deg cos 40 deg cos 60 deg cos 80 deg.
mcqs.why: cos 60 deg = 1/2, and cos 20 deg cos 40 deg cos 80 deg = 1/8, shown by multiplying by 8 sin 20 deg and using sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x three times to get sin 160 deg = sin 20 deg. Hence the product is (1/2) x (1/8) = 1/16.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Trigonometric Functions and their Graphs

lessons.title: Exercise 11.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1-15

Find the periods of the following functions: 1. sin 3x 2. cos 2x 3. tan 4x 4. cot(x/2) 5.

sin(x/3) 6. cosec(x/4) 7. sin(x/5) 8. cos(x/6) 9. tan(x/7) 10. cot 8x 11. sec 9x 12.

cosec 10x 13. 3 sin x 14. 2 cos x 15. 3 cos(x/5)

The period of sin, cos, sec and cosec is 2pi, and of tan and cot is pi; the period of

f(kx) is the base period divided by |k|, and a constant factor does not change the

period. 1. sin 3x: 2pi/3.
2. cos 2x: 2pi/2 = pi. 3. tan 4x: pi/4.
4. cot(x/2): pi/(1/2) =

2pi.
5. sin(x/3): 2pi/(1/3) = 6pi.
6. cosec(x/4): 2pi/(1/4) = 8pi.
7. sin(x/5): 2pi/(1/5) =

10pi.
8. cos(x/6): 2pi/(1/6) = 12pi.
9. tan(x/7): pi/(1/7) = 7pi. 10. cot 8x: pi/8. 11. sec

9x: 2pi/9.
12. cosec 10x: 2pi/10 = pi/5. 13.
3 sin x: 2pi (the factor 3 changes the

amplitude, not the period). 14. 2 cos x: 2pi. 15.
3 cos(x/5): 2pi/(1/5) = 10pi. Note:

the running header on book pp. 341 and 351 repeats Chapter 9's title

('Fundamentals of Trigonometry'); the Contents title 'Trigonometric Functions and

their Graphs' is used here.

mcqs.q: Find the period of sin 3x.
mcqs.why: The period of sin is 2pi, and the period of f(kx) is the base period divided by |k|. Here 2pi/3, since the coefficient of x is 3.

mcqs.q: Find the period of cos 2x.
mcqs.why: The period of cos is 2pi, divided by the coefficient 2 of x: 2pi/2 = pi, so the period of cos 2x is pi.

mcqs.q: Find the period of tan 4x.
mcqs.why: The period of tan is pi, divided by the coefficient 4 of x: pi/4, so the period of tan 4x is pi/4.

mcqs.q: Find the period of cot(x/2).
mcqs.why: The period of cot is pi, divided by the coefficient 1/2 of x: pi/(1/2) = 2pi, so the period of cot(x/2) is 2pi.

mcqs.q: Find the period of sin(x/3).
mcqs.why: The period of sin is 2pi, divided by the coefficient 1/3 of x: 2pi/(1/3) = 6pi, so the period of sin(x/3) is 6pi.

mcqs.q: Find the period of cosec(x/4).
mcqs.why: The period of cosec is 2pi, divided by the coefficient 1/4 of x: 2pi/(1/4) = 8pi, so the period of cosec(x/4) is 8pi.

mcqs.q: Find the period of tan(x/7).
mcqs.why: The period of tan is pi, divided by the coefficient 1/7 of x: pi/(1/7) = 7pi, so the period of tan(x/7) is 7pi.

mcqs.q: Find the period of cot 8x.
mcqs.why: The period of cot is pi, divided by the coefficient 8 of x: pi/8, so the period of cot 8x is pi/8.

mcqs.q: Find the period of sec 9x.
mcqs.why: The period of sec is 2pi, divided by the coefficient 9 of x: 2pi/9, so the period of sec 9x is 2pi/9.

mcqs.q: Find the period of 3 cos(x/5).
mcqs.why: The period of cos is 2pi, divided by the coefficient 1/5 of x: 2pi/(1/5) = 10pi. The factor 3 changes only the amplitude, not the period.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned

against each: i) y = -sin x, x in [-2pi, 2pi] ii) y = 2cos x, x in [0, 2pi] iii) y = tan 2x, x

in [-pi, pi] iv) y = tan x, x in [-2pi, 2pi] v) y = sin(x/2), x in [0, 2pi] vi) y = cos(x/2), x

in [-pi, pi]

Construction instructions (plot the computed points on squared paper, join with a

smooth curve, and mark the asymptotes as dashed vertical lines; no fabricated plot

is printed here). i) y = -sin x is the sine wave reflected in the x-axis, period 2pi,

amplitude 1.
Key points: (-2pi, 0), (-3pi/2, -1), (-pi, 0), (-pi/2, 1), (0, 0), (pi/2, -1), (pi,

0), (3pi/2, 1), (2pi, 0). ii) y = 2cos x is the cosine wave stretched to amplitude 2,

period 2pi.
Key points: (0, 2), (pi/2, 0), (pi, -2), (3pi/2, 0), (2pi, 2). iii) y = tan 2x has

period pi/2.
Zeros at x = 0, +-pi/2, +-pi; vertical asymptotes at x = +-pi/4, +-3pi/4;

the curve rises from -infinity to +infinity between consecutive asymptotes and

passes through (pi/8, 1), (-pi/8, -1). iv) y = tan x has period pi.
Zeros at x = 0, +-pi,

+-2pi; vertical asymptotes at x = +-pi/2, +-3pi/2; the curve rises from -infinity to

+infinity between consecutive asymptotes and passes through (pi/4, 1), (-pi/4, -1),

(5pi/4, 1). v) y = sin(x/2) has period 4pi, so on [0, 2pi] only half a wave appears. Key

points: (0, 0), (pi/2, sin pi/4 = 0.707), (pi, 1), (3pi/2, 0.707), (2pi, 0). vi) y = cos(x/2)

has period 4pi.
Key points: (-pi, 0), (-pi/2, cos(-pi/4) = 0.707), (0, 1), (pi/2, 0.707),

(pi, 0).

Diagram: y = -sin x for x in [-2pi, 2pi].

Diagram: y = 2 cos x for x in [0, 2pi].

Diagram: y = tan 2x for x in [-pi, pi]; dashed lines are asymptotes.

Diagram: y = tan x for x in [-2pi, 2pi]; dashed lines are asymptotes.

Diagram: y = sin(x/2) for x in [0, 2pi].

Diagram: y = cos(x/2) for x in [-pi, pi].

Q2

2. On the same axes and to the same scale, draw the graphs of the following

function for their complete period: i) y = sin x and y = sin 2x ii) y = cos x and y =

cos 2x

Construction instructions. i) Draw y = sin x (period 2pi, amplitude 1) and y = sin 2x

(period pi, amplitude 1) on the same axes for one complete period of sin x, i.e. x in

[0, 2pi].
Both pass through (0, 0); sin 2x completes two full waves while sin x

completes one.
They cross where sin x = sin 2x, i.e. sin x (1 - 2cos x) = 0: x = 0,

pi/3, pi, 5pi/3, 2pi.
Mark these crossings and the peaks: sin x peaks at pi/2 (value 1)

and troughs at 3pi/2 (value -1); sin 2x peaks at pi/4 and 5pi/4 (value 1) and troughs

at 3pi/4 and 7pi/4 (value -1). ii) Draw y = cos x (period 2pi) and y = cos 2x (period

pi) on the same axes for x in [0, 2pi].
Both start at (0, 1); cos 2x completes two full

waves while cos x completes one.
They cross where cos x = cos 2x, i.e. 2cos^2 x -

cos x - 1 = 0, i.e. cos x = 1 or cos x = -1/2: x = 0, 2pi/3, 4pi/3, 2pi. Mark these

crossings and the peaks and troughs: cos x peaks at 0 and 2pi (value 1) and troughs

at pi (value -1); cos 2x peaks at 0, pi, 2pi (value 1) and troughs at pi/2 and 3pi/2

(value -1).

Diagram: y = sin x and y = sin 2x on [0, 2pi].

Diagram: y = cos x and y = cos 2x on [0, 2pi].

Q3

3. Solve graphically: i) sin x = cos x, x in [0, pi] ii) sin x = x, x in [0, pi]

i) Draw y = sin x and y = cos x on the same axes for x in [0, pi]. The curves cross

where sin x = cos x, i.e. tan x = 1, i.e. x = pi/4 (the only solution in [0, pi]). Answer:

x = pi/4. ii) Draw y = sin x and the line y = x on the same axes for x in [0, pi]. The

line y = x lies above the sine curve for every x > 0 in this interval (since sin x < x

for x > 0), so the only intersection is at the origin. Answer: x = 0.

Diagram: y = sin x and y = cos x on [0, pi]; they cross at x = pi/4.

Diagram: y = sin x and y = x on [0, pi]; they meet only at the origin.

mcqs.q: For y = -sin x, the key point at x = pi/2 is (pi/2, ?). Find the missing value.
mcqs.why: y = -sin x is the sine wave reflected in the x-axis. At x = pi/2, y = -sin(pi/2) = -(1) = -1, matching the key point (pi/2, -1) in the notes.

mcqs.q: For y = 2 cos x, find the value of y at x = pi.
mcqs.why: y = 2 cos x has amplitude 2. At x = pi, y = 2 cos pi = 2 x (-1) = -2, matching the key point (pi, -2) in the notes.

mcqs.q: Find the period of y = tan 2x.
mcqs.why: The period of tan is pi, divided by the coefficient 2 of x: pi/2, so y = tan 2x has period pi/2, as stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a vertical asymptote of y = tan 2x on [-pi, pi]?
mcqs.why: The notes list the asymptotes of y = tan 2x on [-pi, pi] as x = +-pi/4 and +-3pi/4, while x = 0, +-pi/2 and +-pi are zeros of the function, not asymptotes.

mcqs.q: The graph of y = tan x passes through (pi/4, ?). Find the missing value.
mcqs.why: At x = pi/4, y = tan(pi/4) = 1, so the graph of y = tan x passes through the point (pi/4, 1) listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: For y = sin(x/2), find the value of y at x = pi.
mcqs.why: At x = pi, y = sin(pi/2) = 1, since x/2 = pi/2 when x = pi. This is the key point (pi, 1) listed for y = sin(x/2) in the notes.

mcqs.q: For y = cos(x/2), find the value of y at x = -pi.
mcqs.why: At x = -pi, y = cos(-pi/2) = 0, since x/2 = -pi/2 when x = -pi. This is the key point (-pi, 0) listed for y = cos(x/2) in the notes.

mcqs.q: On [0, 2pi], the graphs of y = sin x and y = sin 2x cross at which of the following points, apart from the endpoints and x = pi?
mcqs.why: sin x = sin 2x gives sin x (1 - 2 cos x) = 0, so cos x = 1/2, giving x = pi/3 (and 5pi/3) inside the interval, as listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: On [0, 2pi], the graphs of y = cos x and y = cos 2x cross at which of the following points, apart from the endpoints?
mcqs.why: cos x = cos 2x gives 2cos^2 x - cos x - 1 = 0, so cos x = 1 or cos x = -1/2. The value cos x = -1/2 gives x = 2pi/3 (and 4pi/3), as listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: Solve graphically sin x = cos x for x in [0, pi].
mcqs.why: The curves y = sin x and y = cos x cross where sin x = cos x, i.e. tan x = 1. In [0, pi] this gives the single solution x = pi/4.

lessons.title: Exercise 12.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Find the values of: i) sin 53 deg 40' ii) cos 36 deg 20' iii) tan 19 deg 30' iv) cot 33

deg 50' v) cos 42 deg 38' vi) tan 25 deg 34' vii) sin 18 deg 31' viii) cos 52 deg 13'

ix) cot 89 deg 9'

Read from the tables of natural sines, cosines and tangents (values to four decimal

places, as printed in the book's Answers): i) sin 53 deg 40' = 0.8055. ii) cos 36 deg

20' = 0.8055. iii) tan 19 deg 30' = 0.3541. iv) cot 33 deg 50' = 1.4919. v) cos 42

deg 38' = 0.7357. vi) tan 25 deg 34' = 0.4784. vii) sin 18 deg 31' = 0.3175. viii) cos

52 deg 13' = 0.6127. ix) FLAG: the printed key gives 0.1736 for this part, but 0.1736

is cot 80 deg 9' (since cot 80 deg 9' = tan 9 deg 51' = 0.1736), whereas cot 89 deg

9' as printed in the question = tan 0 deg 51' = 0.0148.
The key's value therefore

belongs to 80 deg 9', not to the printed 89 deg 9'; both values are recorded here

and the discrepancy is the book's, not a silent correction.
Note on last digits: a

calculator gives sin 53 deg 40' = 0.8056 and sin 18 deg 31' = 0.3176, one unit in

the last place above the book's table readings 0.8055 and 0.3175; the table values

are given as the answers.

Q2

2. Find theta, if: i) sin theta = 0.5791 ii) cos theta = 0.9316 iii) cos theta = 0.5257

iv) tan theta = 1.705 v) tan theta = 21.943 vi) sin theta = 0.5186

Read inversely from the tables (angles to the nearest minute, as printed in the

book's Answers): i) sin theta = 0.5791 gives theta = 35 deg 23'. ii) cos theta =

0.9316 gives theta = 21 deg 18' (a calculator gives 21 deg 19'; the one-minute

difference is table rounding, and the table value is given). iii) cos theta = 0.5257

gives theta = 58 deg 17'. iv) tan theta = 1.705 gives theta = 59 deg 36'. v) tan

theta = 21.943 gives theta = 87 deg 23'. vi) sin theta = 0.5186 gives theta = 31

deg 14'.

mcqs.q: From the tables of natural sines, what is sin 53 deg 40'?
mcqs.why: Working: 53 deg 40' = 53.6667 deg, and sin(53.6667 deg) = 0.8056 by calculator; the book's table reading, given as the answer, is 0.8055 (one unit in the last place lower).

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is cos 36 deg 20'?
mcqs.why: Working: 36 deg 20' = 36.3333 deg, and cos(36.3333 deg) = 0.8055 to four decimal places, which is the table value stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: From the tables of natural tangents, what is tan 19 deg 30'?
mcqs.why: Working: 19 deg 30' = 19.5 deg, and tan(19.5 deg) = 0.3541 to four decimal places, exactly the table value given in the notes for this angle.

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is cot 33 deg 50'?
mcqs.why: Working: cot 33 deg 50' = 1/tan(33.8333 deg) = 1/0.6703 = 1.4919, which matches the table value printed in the book's answers.

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is cos 42 deg 38'?
mcqs.why: Working: 42 deg 38' = 42.6333 deg, and cos(42.6333 deg) = 0.7357 to four decimal places, the table reading recorded in the notes.

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is tan 25 deg 34'?
mcqs.why: Working: 25 deg 34' = 25.5667 deg, and tan(25.5667 deg) = 0.4784 to four decimal places, which is the value read from the tangent table.

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is sin 18 deg 31'?
mcqs.why: Working: 18 deg 31' = 18.5167 deg, and sin(18.5167 deg) = 0.3176 by calculator; the book's table reading, given as the answer, is 0.3175.

mcqs.q: From the tables, what is cos 52 deg 13'?
mcqs.why: Working: 52 deg 13' = 52.2167 deg, and cos(52.2167 deg) = 0.6127 to four decimal places, the table value stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: The printed key gives 0.1736 for cot 89 deg 9'. What is the correct value of cot 89 deg 9' as printed in the question?
mcqs.why: Correction: cot 89 deg 9' = tan(90 deg - 89 deg 9') = tan 0 deg 51' = tan(0.85 deg) = 0.0148. The key's 0.1736 is actually cot 80 deg 9' = tan 9 deg 51', so it belongs to 80 deg 9', not 89 deg 9'.

mcqs.q: Reading the sine table inversely, if sin theta = 0.5791, what is theta (to the nearest minute)?
mcqs.why: Working: theta = sin^-1(0.5791). Since sin(35.3833 deg) = 0.5791, theta = 35.3833 deg = 35 deg 23', the inverse table reading given in the notes.

lessons.title: Exercise 12.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

1. Find the unknown angles and sides of the following triangles (all right-angled): (i)

angle 45 deg, vertical side 4 (ii) angle 60 deg, hypotenuse 12 (iii) top side 5,

hypotenuse 10 (iv) vertical side 8, angle 40 deg (v) angle 56 deg, hypotenuse 15

(vi) top side 8, vertical side 8
